commits.subject: Renderer: FFT convolution bloom spike behind a temporary option (render features phase 4)
commits.message:
Renderer: FFT convolution bloom spike behind a temporary option (render features phase 4)

PostProcessing/BloomFFT.glsl, one compute shader with five modes: the scene area-averaged and
soft-thresholded into half of a 512x512 grid along its longer side (the other half is padding, so the
circular convolution never wraps), a lens-glare PSF (core, power-law halo, six faint streaks, slightly
chromatic), a 512-point shared-memory FFT per grid row or column, a spectral multiply normalised by the
kernel's DC term (energy is redistributed, not added), and a resolve into the bloom texture the composite
already reads. The kernel spectrum is built once; forward and inverse row passes cover only the source
rows. Grids: 2x RGBA32F + 2x RG32F 512^2, about 12 MB.

SceneRendererOptions::BloomFFT (golden option BloomFFT=1, not serialized) swaps it in for the mip bloom
to measure it before Phase 5 replaces the mip bloom. A-B-A on Benchmark, medians of 3: 1280x720 mip
0.059 / FFT 0.109 / mip 0.060 ms; 1920x1080 0.083 / 0.133 / 0.083 ms, far under the 0.6 ms budget.
Option off: Benchmark and RenderFeatures pixel-identical to the previous golden set; FFT on, Debug +
sync validation: 0 validation ids.

commits.subject: Renderer: glass refraction for transparent materials (render features phase 3)
commits.message:
Renderer: glass refraction for transparent materials (render features phase 3)

Transparent materials gain glTF-style refraction inputs on MaterialSurfaceParameters: Transmission,
IOR, Thickness, AttenuationColor and AttenuationDistance (YAML keys written when not default, so old
.lmat files load unchanged; asset packs reuse the YAML), imported from KHR_materials_transmission /
_ior / _volume, and edited in a "Refraction" section of the material editor shown for transparent
materials. The GPU material row grows to 11 vec4 (Transmission, AttenuationColor), both layouts together.

In HazelPBR_Transparent.glsl transmission takes its share from the diffuse lobe and adds the opaque
scene behind: the view ray refracted by the IOR and carried Thickness into the volume (0 = thin-walled,
blurred but not displaced), projected back with the flipped-Y convention and read from the
pre-convolved scene at a roughness mip capped at 5, the sky when it leaves the screen, absorbed
Beer-Lambert, tinted by the base colour and weighted by (1 - Fresnel). Alpha stays coverage, so
transmission 0 is exactly the old blend.

MaterialScene counts refractive rows (HasRefractiveMaterials); with any in the submitted render scene,
Pre-Convolution runs even without SSR and the transparent pass reads it at (1, 11), bound in
TransparentForwardPass (a black texture otherwise). RenderFeatures' glass becomes refractive: thin
panes, thick spheres, an absorbing block.

Verified: Release, Debug and Lux-Runtime build; golden rf3: Benchmark identical to rf2; RenderFeatures
panes sharp / frosted / rough, spheres bend, the block absorbs; with SSR off the glass is the same and
Pre-Convolution runs alone (0.088 ms); Debug + sync validation: 0 validation ids; the Refraction
section checked in the editor.

commits.subject: Renderer: sphere and tube area lights, and area lighting on transparents (render features phase 2)
commits.message:
Renderer: sphere and tube area lights, and area lighting on transparents (render features phase 2)

AreaLightShape gains Sphere and Tube (new Length key; Radius shared). A sphere is integrated as a disk
facing the shaded point and a tube as a rectangle facing it around its axis, lengthened by pi r / 4 per
end to keep the capsule silhouette's area (LTC_FacingShape), so the existing LTC polygon integral serves
all four shapes; lumens convert over each shape's full surface. Two-sided applies to flat shapes only
(hidden in the inspector otherwise), and the viewport outlines spheres and tubes.

HazelPBR_Transparent.glsl, the transparent pass's shader, adds LuxEvaluateAreaLights; the transparent
pass binds AreaLightData and the LTC tables, and the area buffer is now uploaded every frame (count 0
included) so glass never keeps lights that were removed. RenderFeatures gains a sphere and a tube.

Exported games carry everything (the shader pack is built from the whole library; the tables are
compiled into Core). Verified: Release, Debug and Lux-Runtime build; golden rf2: Benchmark identical to
rf1 except the colliders variant's other known line-blending state; RenderFeatures shows all four
shapes and lit glass; Debug + sync validation: 0 validation ids; shapes checked in the editor.

commits.subject: Renderer: rect and disk area lights with Linearly Transformed Cosines (render features phase 1)
commits.message:
Renderer: rect and disk area lights with Linearly Transformed Cosines (render features phase 1)

New AreaLightComponent: a rect (Width x Height) or disk (Radius) emitting along the entity's -Z, sized
by its transform, intensity as luminance or lumens (PhysicalLight::AreaIntensity), two-sided option,
range. It goes through every component touch point (copy, prefab, serializer both ways, hierarchy
panel create menu / add row / inspector) and reaches the renderer in LightEnvironment::AreaLights.
The viewport draws each light's shape outline.

SceneRenderer uploads the nearest 32 to AreaLightData at (1, 18) and adds an "Area Lights" pass
(DeferredLighting_Area.glsl + LTC.glslh) over deferred lighting, only on frames with area lights, so
deferred lighting never carries the LTC code. Diffuse is Lambert, specular GGX through the fitted LTC
tables; a disk is integrated as an area-matched 12-gon; horizon clipping uses the tables' sphere form
factor. The tables are Renderer::GetLTCMatrixTexture / GetLTCAmplitudeTexture at (3, 6) / (3, 7),
built from Core/vendor/ltc/LTCTables.h, converted from ltc_1/ltc_2.dds of selfshadow/ltc_code
(BSD-2-Clause, license alongside).

RenderFeatures gains a rect and a disk light; the generator no longer rewrites the asset registry
when its entries are already registered. Verified: Release, Debug and Lux-Runtime build; golden rf1:
all 17 Benchmark captures identical to rf0 (known 2-px noise), RenderFeatures shows the lights;
Debug + sync validation on RenderFeatures and Benchmark: 0 validation ids; inspector, create menu,
add-component row and outline checked in the editor.

area-light slots, clear/frosted/rough/tinted glass in front of a dark-grid wall, bright emitters for
bloom, chrome and satin spheres, under a dusk sun. Its 15 RF_* materials sit under their own handles
(16000000000000001000+) and entity range; the default Benchmark output is unchanged (original and new

commits.subject: Renderer: Cutout materials cast alpha-tested shadows
commits.message:
Renderer: Cutout materials cast alpha-tested shadows

The shadow shaders had an empty fragment stage (`TODO: Check for alpha in
texture`), so a leaf or chain card cast the shadow of its whole quad.

A Cutout caster's shadow draws are now their own buckets
(MeshKey::AlphaMasked) and switch, inside whichever cascade or spot-atlas
pass is open, to DirShadowMap_Masked / SpotShadowMap_Masked. Those shaders
apply the same alpha test as the pre-depth pass, from the material table
and bindless textures. Each kind has one never-begun RenderPass
(m_ShadowMapMaskedPass, m_SpotShadowMaskedPass) holding the pipeline and
its sets; one pipeline serves every pass of that depth format. All other
casters keep the depth-only shadow shaders, whose fragment stage does no
work.

A masked shadow depends on its material, so both static-cache hashes now
include the material revision for masked casters: editing a Cutout
material re-renders the static shadow caches.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Renderer: two-sided materials draw without back-face culling
commits.message:
Renderer: two-sided materials draw without back-face culling

MaterialSurfaceParameters::TwoSided was stored in the GPU material row but
nothing read it, so a two-sided leaf card vanished whenever its back faced
the camera.

Two-sided draws are now their own buckets (MeshKey::TwoSided, resolved by
MaterialScene::ResolveRasterState from what the material row is built
from) and draw through no-cull variants of the pre-depth and G-buffer
pipelines. Both passes take the same variant, since the G-buffer
depth-tests EQUAL against the prepass. GBuffer_Static lights a back face
with its normal and tangent frame flipped, glTF's double-sided rule.

The variants switch inside the open pass with the new
Renderer::SwitchRenderPassPipeline (RenderCommandBuffer::
RT_SwitchNRIRenderPassPipeline), which swaps the pipeline, layout and
sets without splitting the rendering scope. Draws sort by pipeline, so a
pass switches at most once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Assets: import glTF alphaMode and doubleSided, so Sponza's foliage is cut out
commits.message:
Assets: import glTF alphaMode and doubleSided, so Sponza's foliage is cut out

The Assimp importer never read the glTF alpha mode, alpha cutoff or
doubleSided flag. A MASK material keeps its alpha in the base colour
texture with a factor of 1, so the factor test saw an opaque material and
Sponza's plant and chain cards drew as solid quads.

MASK now imports as Cutout with the authored cutoff, BLEND as a
transparent asset, and Assimp's two-sided flag sets TwoSided. Sponza's
three masked materials (0, 1, 20; Assimp reorders them from the glTF's
0, 3, 20) carry the same values, without needing a re-import.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Export: build Lux-Runtime and scripts off the main thread, lock the editor behind a progress overlay
commits.message:
Export: build Lux-Runtime and scripts off the main thread, lock the editor behind a progress overlay

The export's MSBuild/make/dotnet ran through std::system on the main thread, so the editor
froze "Not Responding" for the whole build (a minute or more for Dist) and a failed build left
the export window with no reason.

- RuntimeExport::RuntimeBuildJob runs the build on a named Lux::Thread (not the JobSystem,
  which runs inline under Single). Paths are resolved on the main thread in Start; the worker
  never reads Project. Poll() hands the result back at the top of OnImGuiRender.
- A failed build stops the export with its exit code in the export window.
- Exporting shows a modal overlay that locks the editor: an indeterminate bar while compiling
  (Cancel Export drops the export; the build finishes in the background), then a step bar while
  the package is written, one step per frame so the bar advances. OnEvent drops shortcuts,
  picking and camera input meanwhile.
- The Project Settings Build buttons share the job, so only one build runs at a time.
- Threading.md and Architecture-LuxEngine.md describe the build worker and the export flow.

commits.subject: Log: warnings and errors reach disk before a kill, everything else within a second
commits.message:
Log: warnings and errors reach disk before a kill, everything else within a second

The LUX and APP file sinks had no flush policy, so they were stdio-buffered in
4 KiB chunks. A process killed by Visual Studio's Stop Debugging (TerminateProcess)
or a crash lost its last <4 KiB of LUX log and often the whole APP log, which
holds every LUX_CONSOLE_LOG_* line, export and build errors included.

Log::Init now sets flush_on(warn) on the LUX, APP and Console loggers and
registers them, so spdlog::flush_every writes trace/info out once a second,
which also covers a hung process. Log::Shutdown calls spdlog::shutdown() to
join the flusher thread before the loggers close.

Verified with a test exe linking Core.lib that logs marker lines and is then
killed with TerminateProcess: before, both files were 0 bytes; after, every
warn/error line (and the lines logged before it) is on disk, and info-only
lines arrive within the 1 s interval. Init -> Shutdown -> Init (Lux::Main's
restart loop) works. Per-frame warn+ sites are deduplicated, so the extra
flush (~25 us per warn+ line, Debug) only shows up during load-time bursts.

commits.subject: Export: build Lux-Runtime with the solution's SolutionDir, find MSBuild with vswhere
commits.message:
Export: build Lux-Runtime with the solution's SolutionDir, find MSBuild with vswhere

When an export found Lux-Runtime older than its sources, the editor ran
MSBuild on Lux-Runtime.vcxproj alone. Outside the solution MSBuild defaults
$(SolutionDir) to each project's own folder, and premake writes
%{wks.location} as $(SolutionDir), so Core's post-build copied Coral from
Core\Core\vendor and the export failed with MSB3073 ("The system cannot find
the path specified"). The command now passes /p:SolutionDir=<repo root>,
which also reaches the referenced projects. The value has no trailing
backslash: every generated use is "$(SolutionDir)\...", and PowerShell
quotes an argument containing spaces, where a final backslash would escape
the closing quote. Only the toolset line of .lastbuildstate forces a
rebuild, so the different spelling from a solution build does not.

MSBuild is now found with vswhere (any VS 2017+ edition or version)
instead of a hard-coded VS 18 Community path, falling back to PATH.

Verified with the exact command, through std::system, against a touched
Core source in Dist: the old command reproduces MSB3073, the new one
builds Core, runs its post-build and links Lux-Runtime.exe.

commits.subject: VR: Lux-Runtime --vr head-looks with the LUX OPTIC tracker (VR plan phase 1)
commits.message:
VR: Lux-Runtime --vr head-looks with the LUX OPTIC tracker (VR plan phase 1)

First phase of docs/VR_PLAN.md: native 3DoF support for the LUX OPTIC DIY
headset, without SteamVR. Mono for now; stereo, lens distortion, headset
output and calibration are the next phases.

- HID::InputDevice reads input reports with a timeout: overlapped ReadFile on
  Windows (queue cut to the 2-report minimum and flushed on open, since every
  queued report is latency), poll + read on hidraw.
- Core/Source/Lux/VR: LuxOpticTracker reads the tracker (USB 303A:1001, report
  1 = w, x, y, z floats in the engine's own axes) on a "Head Tracker" thread,
  draining to the newest report and reconnecting by itself. StereoRig puts the
  camera at the head: the scene camera's position and heading, then the head
  rotation, so a game never tilts the horizon. LuxOpticConfig keeps the
  headset's measurements in LuxOptic.yaml in the user data folder, one per
  machine. VRSession ties them together for a host, with an Alt+mouse head
  while no tracker is connected.
- Lux-Runtime: --vr (or VR: true in RuntimeSettings.yaml) renders the primary
  camera through the head and shows tracker stats (Ctrl+F6). Ctrl+F5
  recenters, Ctrl+F8 reloads the settings. DOF is forced off, and the runtime's
  ImGui overlays are off while VR is on.
- CommandLineParser::HaveOpt now means "given", so a bare trailing --vr counts
  (it had no callers).

Also adds the plan, with the Phase 0 GPU budget: one 1440x1440 eye costs
3.7 ms on Benchmark, so stereo fits 120 Hz at ~7.1 ms, while 2016x2016 does
not, hence a default render scale of 1.0. Architecture gains § 2.16 VR and the
HID input notes; Threading lists the tracker thread.

Builds in Debug, Release and Dist on Windows. Not yet run with the tracker,
and not compiled on Linux. New files: regenerate projects.

commits.subject: Editor: on Linux the startup splash is a card-sized window, not a maximized one
commits.message:
Editor: on Linux the startup splash is a card-sized window, not a maximized one

Without platform viewports the splash draws in the main window, which started
maximized, so it showed as a 960x540 card in a full-screen window. The splash
now sizes the main window to the card and centres it while startup runs, and
the new StartupSplash::Finish (end of OnAttach) sets it back to the
application size, maximizes it and draws until the window manager has done
so: a first editor frame at the card's size would pull floating ImGui windows
into it, and ImGui saves that.

A DeferWindowShow window is no longer maximized while hidden (X11 cannot
restore it before it is shown); whoever shows it calls the new
Application::PlaceWindow, which the Windows splash does on creation as before.
Window gains SetSize, and CenterWindow skips Wayland, where GLFW cannot
position windows and logged an error.

Fix the Wayland startup crash: no layer events until OnAttach returns

The startup splash shows the main window from inside EditorLayer::OnAttach when
there are no platform viewports (always on Linux). On Wayland glfwShowWindow
does a roundtrip that delivers the configure synchronously, so the resize event

commits.subject: Renderer: fix the GTAO noise index at 0 so AO stops cycling with the frame-in-flight slot
commits.message:
Renderer: fix the GTAO noise index at 0 so AO stops cycling with the frame-in-flight slot

GTAO fed Renderer::GetCurrentFrameIndex() % 64 into XeGTAO's NoiseIndex, which only rotates the
noise for a TAA to resolve. With no temporal resolve the AO noise cycled with the 3 frame-in-flight
slots: a 3-frame shimmer, and golden captures that depended on which slot a frame landed in (the
settle-window wobble seen with MoveStop).

Golden set (17 variants, 0 validation ids) passes against the previous captures; every GTAO
variant moves by 37-278 px as the noise pattern settles on index 0, noGTAO and moving are
identical. settling vs the unmoved image: 16,952 px (max 21) -> 60 px (max 1); that small
intermittent remainder is not explained yet.

commits.subject: Renderer: keep cull groups on move-only frames, and keep shadows of casters that just stopped
commits.message:
Renderer: keep cull groups on move-only frames, and keep shadows of casters that just stopped

Any changed proxy used to throw the cull groups away, so one moving entity resubmitted all ~7k
proxies. A move updates a proxy's GPUScene rows in place (instances are keyed by primitive and
submesh) and the GPU culls read the new transforms, so the groups are now kept when every change is
a Transform-only move of a visible proxy outside the shadow cull groups
(m_ShadowCullGroupPrimitives); a static caster that starts moving, or any other change, still
rebuilds them.

On a kept-groups frame a proxy that moved within StaticShadowCasterStableFrames is no longer treated
as covered: it submits its CPU-path shadows, and m_NextStaticCasterFrame is recomputed every submit.
This also fixes casters losing their shadows for about three frames after they stopped (the old
freeze skipped them while they settled). New golden option MoveStop=K and variant `settling`
(MoveEntities=256,MoveStop=2) capture inside that window.

Golden set: 16/16 identical to the previous build (colliders and meshShaders checked against re-runs
for their known noise), settling shows the shadows (1736 -> ~50 px >3 levels; the rest is a
pre-existing GTAO wobble in the settle frames, identical with GTAO off). Moving A-B-A (medians of 3):
SubmitRenderScene 2.54 / 0.55 / 2.09 ms, main thread 5.74 / 3.39 / 4.49 ms.

commits.subject: Renderer: depth-only shadow maps and no static-cache copy without dynamic casters
commits.message:
Renderer: depth-only shadow maps and no static-cache copy without dynamic casters

RenderDoc on the moving Benchmark showed the four static-cache to ShadowMapArray copies taking about
1.5 ms of the ~2.6 ms ShadowMapPass every moving frame (and the 0.2 ms Phase 4 gap was not GPU work:
draws, copies and cache texels were identical to Phase 3).

The directional cascades, the spot atlas and both static caches are now DEPTH32F instead of
D32_SFLOAT_S8_UINT; nothing used the stencil. A frame without dynamic casters renders the static
casters straight into the shadow map and copies nothing; the cache image is filled from the map the
first frame dynamic casters need a clean static base.

Golden set (default + 15 variants) pixel-identical to Phase 5, 0 validation ids. Moving A-B-A
(medians of 3): ShadowMapPass GPU 2.50 / 2.09 / 2.44 ms, total GPU 5.46 / 4.86 / 5.41 ms.

commits.subject: Renderer: retained-scene stats in the Renderer Debugger and same-frame mesh hot reload (retained plan phase 5)
commits.message:
Renderer: retained-scene stats in the Renderer Debugger and same-frame mesh hot reload (retained plan phase 5)

The Renderer Debugger's GPU Scene tab gains a Retained Scene table (proxies changed and removed
this frame, cached submit entries, cull groups kept or rebuilt, static shadow casters, whether
the shadow cull ran), backed by SceneRenderer::Statistics::RetainedScene.

A proxy kept the StaticMesh and MeshSource it first resolved while its handle stayed the same, so
a hot-reloaded mesh never reached it (this predates phase 1). AssetManagerBase::GetDataGeneration
is now bumped whenever a loaded asset's data is replaced (ReloadData, an async load landing, a
runtime-pack reload), and RenderScene re-resolves every mesh on a frame where it moved.

Final A-B-A against phase 0, Benchmark 1280x720 Release, medians of 3: sync + submit + flush
18.73/2.38/18.01 ms, main thread 19.00/2.69/18.39 ms, frame 23.00/6.92/22.15 ms. The image is
identical to phase 0's own capture; golden default + 15 variants and the single-threaded policy
identical to phase 4.

commits.subject: Fix the Debug exit-time VMA leak assert: drain shutdown releases until nothing is left
commits.message:
Fix the Debug exit-time VMA leak assert: drain shutdown releases until nothing is left

Renderer::Shutdown executed the render command queues once, then drained the
GPU deletion queue. A BindlessTextureTable's destructor queues a release whose
lambda holds Ref<Texture2D> for every slot, so draining it dropped the last
reference to the white texture and the material textures. Their frees were
queued into the render command queues again, which Shutdown then deleted
without executing. 93 textures outlived the NRI device, and in Debug VMA
asserted "Unfreed dedicated allocations found!" in vmaDestroyAllocator; the
CRT dialog blocked exit, so Debug golden runs waited out their timeout.
Release leaked the same textures silently.

Shutdown now repeats execute queues / wait idle / drain releases until both
are empty. Debug builds also track every NRITexture/NRIBuffer and name the
survivors when RHIDevice::Shutdown runs, which is how these were found.

Verified: Debug + sync-validation Benchmark golden run exits on its own in
111 s (status OK, 0 validation ids, no leaks); Release Benchmark with the
same project settings as bin/golden/fixrel is pixel-identical (bad=0, max=0).

commits.subject: Renderer: GPU shadow culling for static casters through shadow cull groups (retained plan phase 4)
commits.message:
Renderer: GPU shadow culling for static casters through shadow cull groups (retained plan phase 4)

A cull-group instance that casts shadows and has not moved for StaticShadowCasterStableFrames
syncs (new StaticMeshRenderProxy::LastMovedFrame) joins a shadow cull group; groups rebuild on the
frame a caster settles. The new ShadowCulling.glsl, run before the shadow passes only when a static
shadow cache re-renders, culls each instance per cascade (the CPU's own frustum planes plus the
tiny-caster rule) and for the spot atlas, picks its LOD with the metric now shared through
MeshLOD.glslh, and writes per (target, LOD) instance ranges and indirect args that the static caches
draw. The static caches re-render when the static caster set or the cull's camera inputs change;
moving casters keep the exact CPU shadow path. With the groups kept, SubmitRenderScene skips every
non-selected proxy they cover.

Benchmark 1280x720 Release, A-B-A medians of 3 against phase 3: SubmitRenderScene 3.16/0.30/3.22
ms, main thread 5.66/2.87/5.84 ms, frame 6.65/4.25/6.85 ms; static shadow passes stay cached.
Moving variant: frame 8.25/6.92/8.17 ms; ShadowMapPass about 0.2 ms above phase 3 (open). Golden
default + 15 variants identical; Debug + sync validation clean.

commits.subject: Renderer: GPU LOD and visibility for the main view through cull groups (retained plan phase 3)
commits.message:
Renderer: GPU LOD and visibility for the main view through cull groups (retained plan phase 3)

Proxy instances with a GPUScene row join persistent main-view cull groups (mesh, submesh, and
material key when transparent), rebuilt only when the submitted scene's change list or the
submit-cache epoch moves, so the CPU does no main-view culling or LOD for them. FlushDrawList
expands each group into one draw per LOD with its own visible range and indirect args, and
MeshCulling.glsl picks each instance's LOD with SelectStaticMeshLOD's metric. An early dispatch of
the same shader (frustum and LOD, no HZB) writes the depth prepass's instances into ObjectIndexes,
now GPU-only, and the prepass draws cull-group draws indirect, so prepass and G-buffer agree on
every LOD. Selection outlines, shadows and non-proxy submissions keep the CPU path; the mesh-shader
prepass keeps the phase 2 path.

Benchmark 1280x720 Release, A-B-A medians of 3 against phase 2: SubmitRenderScene 3.40/2.91/3.30
ms, main thread 5.64/5.22/5.52 ms; early cull 0.05 ms GPU. Golden default + 15 variants identical
to phase 2; Debug + sync validation clean.

commits.subject: Fix the Debug + sync-validation golden run: copy-queue barriers and a zero-size InvisibleButton
commits.message:
Fix the Debug + sync-validation golden run: copy-queue barriers and a zero-size InvisibleButton

The async upload batch on the transfer-only queue recorded ShaderResource transitions with
SHADER_READ access and ALL stages, which that queue cannot execute (VUID-VkImageMemoryBarrier2-
*AccessMask-07454/03909, vkCmdPipelineBarrier2 09675/09676). NRIBarrierEmitter now knows its
queue; on the copy queue it keeps only copy accesses and ALL stages and keeps the layout change.
The reading queue's timeline-semaphore wait already orders and publishes the upload.

The title-bar drag zone passed a width of exactly 0 to InvisibleButton when the host window was
narrower than the logo plus window controls, asserting in Debug on the first editor frame. It is
now skipped then; the Scene Renderer card header and the content-browser list row are clamped to
at least one pixel for the same reason.

commits.subject: Renderer: one hash lookup per instance per bucket in the static-mesh submit (retained plan phase 2, step 2)
commits.message:
Renderer: one hash lookup per instance per bucket in the static-mesh submit (retained plan phase 2, step 2)

MeshKeyHasher is now a multiply-xorshift mix instead of six byte-wise FNV std::hash calls; draw
order does not depend on map order, since BuildSortedDrawCommandOrder sorts on every key field.
Each transform bucket remembers its draw per pass, so later instances only bump the count: an
opaque instance does one lookup instead of three, a shadow instance one instead of two.
CalculateShadowCasterHashes hashes transform rows 64 bits at a time.

Benchmark 1280x720 Release, A-B-A medians of 3 against step 1: SubmitRenderScene 3.91/3.27/3.93
ms, FlushDrawList 1.48/1.26/1.50 ms, main thread 6.34/5.53/6.42 ms; default image identical.

commits.subject: Renderer: cache per-proxy submit data and drop per-instance lookups (retained plan phase 2, step 1)
commits.message:
Renderer: cache per-proxy submit data and drop per-instance lookups (retained plan phase 2, step 1)

SceneRenderer caches each proxy's camera-independent submit data (material handle and asset,
transparency, shadow casting, sort keys) by RenderPrimitiveID, invalidated by the proxy's
revision, RenderScene::GetGeneration, MaterialTable::GetGlobalRevision and the new
MaterialScene::GetAssetRevision. SubmitMeshPassDraw counts a repeat key before touching the
draw-command cache, per-pass sort keys are read once per frame, shadow-caster motion is a dense
vector with an exact row compare, transform-bucket vectors are recycled, and the submesh world
transform is only computed where it is used.

Benchmark 1280x720 Release, A-B-A medians of 3: SubmitRenderScene 9.66/4.48/8.68 ms, main thread
12.54/7.70/11.24 ms; the default image is pixel-identical.

commits.subject: Renderer: unchanged static meshes skip their proxy in the render-scene sync
commits.message:
Renderer: unchanged static meshes skip their proxy in the render-scene sync

RenderScene keeps a dense record of each entity's last sync inputs in sync order. An unchanged
entity is now a sequential compare against that record and never reads its proxy node; last
frame's record at the cursor replaces the hash lookup. MaterialTable gains a process-wide
revision, so while no table changed no table is read per entity, and EndSync skips its removal
walk when every proxy was synced.

Benchmark 1280x720 Release, A-B-A medians of 3 against the previous commit: RenderSceneSync
1.27/0.53/1.28 ms (the per-entity loop 0.68 -> 0.10 ms). Golden default + all feature variants
identical; moving identical to phase 0. Completes the retained plan's phase 1 sync target.

commits.subject: Scripting: keep script field values through load, copy and save
commits.message:
Scripting: keep script field values through load, copy and save

Script field overrides were lost in several places:

- A scene loaded while its script was not in the app assembly dropped
  its StoredFields, and the next save wrote none. They are now kept in
  ScriptStorage::UnresolvedStorage, saved back unchanged and applied
  once the script resolves. A reload that loses a script keeps its
  values the same way; the next good reload applies them again.
- Scene::Copy did not copy ScriptStorage. OpenScene edits a copy of the
  scene asset and Play runs on a copy, so opening and saving a scene
  dropped every override even with the assembly loaded, and overrides
  never reached Play. Copy and CopyTo now copy the storage and bind it
  to the loaded assembly.
- Fields with no captured default (every bool, entity and asset
  reference) started as uninitialized heap memory, so unset bools came
  out true at random in C# and in saved scenes. They now start zeroed,
  and bool initializers from C# are captured.
- Duplicating an entity, creating or instantiating a prefab and prefab
  revert/apply copied the ScriptComponent but not its values. They now
  copy them with ScriptStorage::CopyEntityFields.

FieldStorage caches IsArray, since its Coral type dangles after a
reload. Resolved StoredFields are written sorted by field ID, so equal
values always give equal text for undo diffs and prefab override
detection. Saving with unresolved scripts logs a Scripting warning, and
the serializer round-trip self-test covers an unresolved script.

Benchmark and FMODDemo get back the overrides lost in bb209835, taken
from 137ef833 (13 fields on 9 entities, 10 fields on 2 entities); no
other line changes. The Benchmark camera path plays on start again.
FMODDemo's InvertGamepadY=true is restored as it was, though it may
have come from the uninitialized-bool bug (its C# default is false).

Checked without the editor, in a console program linking Core.lib:
the pre-loss Benchmark saved without the assembly is text-identical;
with LuxSample.dll every value is kept and 25 scalars match the live
C# objects; failed and good reloads, duplicates and prefab paths keep
the values.

commits.subject: RenderThread: finish the in-flight frame before the final pump in Terminate
commits.message:
RenderThread: finish the in-flight frame before the final pump in Terminate

Terminate() kicked while the render thread could still be Busy with the
previous frame. Set(Kick) overwrote Busy, the render thread set Idle when done
and exited, so the last submitted frame never ran on it and Renderer::Shutdown
replayed the whole frame on the main thread after the renderer was torn down.

Wait for Idle first, pump the last frame on the render thread, then kick once
more so it observes IsRunning() == false and returns. m_IsRunning is atomic.

commits.subject: Renderer: retained static-mesh sync with refcounted materials (retained plan phase 1)
commits.message:
Renderer: retained static-mesh sync with refcounted materials (retained plan phase 1)

RenderScene::SyncStaticMesh compares each entity's inputs with its retained proxy in place
instead of rebuilding and reassigning a full proxy every frame. Meshes resolve only when the
handle changes, bounds only when the transform or mesh does, and the material table is rehashed
only when MaterialTable::GetRevision changes. Material rows and texture slots are reference
counted by the proxies' GPU instances, and MaterialScene rebuilds a row when its asset object or
MaterialAsset::GetRevision changes, so the per-frame touch walk is gone.

Benchmark 1280x720 Release, A-B-A medians of 3: RenderSceneSync 6.42/1.23/6.13 ms, main
thread 15.02/9.98/14.34 ms. Golden default + all feature variants match HEAD; moving is
pixel-identical to phase 0.

commits.subject: Renderer: CPU stage timings and a moving-mesh golden test (retained plan phase 0)
commits.message:
Renderer: CPU stage timings and a moving-mesh golden test (retained plan phase 0)

Phase 0 of docs/RENDER_SCENE_RETAINED_PLAN.md: measure before changing.

- SceneRenderer::RecordStageCPUProfile / ScopedStageProfile record CPU
  stages as pass profiles without adding them to TotalCPUTime, since
  they enclose pass zones. perf.json now lists RenderSceneSync (timed
  into FrameRenderPacket::MeshSyncMs while the packet is built and
  recorded after BeginScene), SubmitRenderScene and FlushDrawList.
- GoldenCapture MoveEntities=N moves the first N static-mesh entities
  (by UUID) around a 16-frame loop every frame, captures only on a frame
  at the loop's start and restores them at the end; golden_run.py gets a
  "moving" variant (MoveEntities=256).

Baseline, Benchmark 1280x720 Release, medians of 3: RenderSceneSync 7.61
ms, SubmitRenderScene 8.09 ms, FlushDrawList 1.57 ms of a 17.70 ms main
thread. The moving captures are identical to each other and match the
unmoved one within golden_compare tolerance (37 px of draw-order
change). Recorded in the plan.

commits.subject: Docs: retained render scene plan
commits.message:
Docs: retained render scene plan

docs/RENDER_SCENE_RETAINED_PLAN.md plans making static meshes retained
(skip unchanged meshes in the render-scene sync and submit) and moving
per-frame LOD and visibility to the GPU culling pass, in six phases with
Phase 2 as a shippable stopping point.

commits.subject: Sample scenes: auto exposure in NewSceneSystem; re-save the rest
commits.message:
Sample scenes: auto exposure in NewSceneSystem; re-save the rest

NewSceneSystem switches to histogram auto exposure (compensation 0,
gamma 2.2), moves its spot light to 125.9 lumens at 7100 K, and points
the sky light at dikhololo_night_4k.hdr; its old environment map handle
was not in the asset registry.

Benchmark and FMODDemo are re-saves. They were saved while the script
assembly was not loaded, so their script field overrides were not kept
and those fields now take the script defaults: the Benchmark camera
path no longer plays on start, its doors all start closed, the listener
camera speed is 5 and the plaza emitter plays on start at 0.7; FMODDemo's
camera no longer inverts gamepad Y. Most of the line churn is entity
order and inline empty lists.

commits.subject: Asset: hot EditorAssetManager lookups no longer copy metadata
commits.message:
Asset: hot EditorAssetManager lookups no longer copy metadata

GetAsset (for loaded assets), IsAssetHandleValid and GetAssetType all
went through GetMetadata, which returns AssetMetadata by value, so every
call copied the asset's std::filesystem::path: a wide-string allocate,
copy and free, plus memory tracking in Release. The renderer makes these
calls per mesh and per material every frame. They now read the registry
entry in place under the same shared lock; an asset that still needs
loading takes the unchanged copying path.

Benchmark, 1280x720 Release, same session (HEAD 3 runs, change 6 runs in
two sets, medians): main thread 18.95 -> 17.28 ms, frame 19.99 -> 18.46
ms, image pixel-identical. Run-to-run noise was high this session.

commits.subject: Renderer: stop recomputing material complexity per submesh per frame
commits.message:
Renderer: stop recomputing material complexity per submesh per frame

SubmitStaticMeshInternal and the bound-material draw path called
MaterialAsset::UpdateMaterialComplexityMetadata for every submesh every
frame (the second one on the render thread), each doing two uniform
lookups by string. Every MaterialAsset setter already recomputes it, and
nothing changes a material's inputs any other way, so the per-frame calls
only repeated work. The copying constructor now computes it once too.

Benchmark, 1280x720 Release, median of 3: frame 17.24 -> 15.37 ms, main
thread 16.58 -> 14.72 ms, image pixel-identical.

commits.subject: Core: Ref registers live references only on the first reference
commits.message:
Core: Ref registers live references only on the first reference

Ref::IncRef locked the global live-reference registry and inserted the
pointer on every copy, so every Ref copy paid a mutex and a hash. The
registry only needs an object from its first reference until it is
deleted, so IncRefCount now returns the new count and IncRef registers
only on 0->1. WeakRef::IsValid answers exactly as before.

Benchmark, 1280x720 Release, median of 3: frame 22.41 -> 17.24 ms, main
thread 21.74 -> 16.58 ms, image pixel-identical.

commits.subject: Sample project: render without mesh shaders
commits.message:
Sample project: render without mesh shaders

With MeshShaders on, the depth prepass runs PreDepthMeshletPass, which
costs 23.8 ms of a 25.8 ms GPU frame on Benchmark (1280x720 Release,
median of 3). The classic prepass draws the same depth in 0.18 ms and
the frame is pixel-identical, so the sample project uses it until the
meshlet path is fixed.

commits.subject: Renderer: GTAO visibility-bitmask mode and noise passes
commits.message:
Renderer: GTAO visibility-bitmask mode and noise passes

GTAO gains a second estimator next to XeGTAO's horizon integral: a
32-sector visibility bitmask (Therrien et al. 2023). Each sample
occludes only the sectors between its front surface and a point
GTAOThickness metres behind it, so thin objects no longer darken
everything under their horizon. Sectors are spaced in sin(angle from the
normal), equal cosine-weighted area each, so the result stays comparable
to GTAO's integral; both ends round to the nearest sector so samples on
a flat surface's horizon claim nothing. The mode keeps the surface
normal as the bent normal.

GTAONoisePasses (1..3) re-runs the slices with the noise shifted along
R2 and averages them, spatially within the frame. The AO tier sets it
(Ultra 2, Cinematic 3); the bitmask is opt-in. All three settings are in
the Screen-Space Effects card and saved with the project (runtime format
27). Sky pixels already exit early (reverse-Z depth 0).

The horizon path renders unchanged (pixel-identical Benchmark capture).
The golden capture tool takes GTAOBitmask=1.

commits.subject: Editor: floor grid colours and widths in editor preferences
commits.message:
Editor: floor grid colours and widths in editor preferences

The grid's colours, line widths, cell size and fade distance were fixed
in SceneRenderer::Init. They are now SceneRenderer::GridSettings, set
with SetGridSettings (clamped to a usable range), and the editor keeps
them as Editor.Grid.* preferences with a Grid section on Application
Settings > Viewport, including a reset.

commits.subject: Renderer: spot/point PCSS in linear depth; CPU-built shadow kernel
commits.message:
Renderer: spot/point PCSS in linear depth; CPU-built shadow kernel

Spot and point-light PCSS computed the penumbra from raw perspective
depth, so penumbra width was wrong, and took a fixed 0.01-UV search.
The receiver's linear depth is now its clip.w in the tile, and blocker
depths linearize as B / (d + A) with A and B read from the tile's
view-projection matrix, so no near/far data is uploaded. The search
covers the emitter's projection at the near plane, the filter radius is
the penumbra half-width at the receiver, both in tile UV, and the search
is capped at the 5% margin point-light faces keep. The spot light's
Falloff is the emitter diameter in metres: labelled "Light Size" in the
editor, LightSize on the GPU, same YAML key.

PCSS taps come from RendererData.ShadowKernel: 32 entries built on the
CPU, a Vogel disk over the filter count in xy and one over the blocker
count in zw. The counts are SceneRendererOptions::ShadowBlockerSamples /
ShadowFilterSamples, set by the shadow quality tier (Low 8/12, Medium
and High 16/24, Ultra 16/32, Cinematic 32/32), shown in the Shadows
card and saved with the project (runtime format 26). A blocker search
that finds every tap occluded returns fully shadowed without filtering.
The 64-entry Poisson table is gone.

The golden capture tool takes PCSS=1, and golden_run.py has a PCSS
feature variant.

commits.subject: Renderer: albedo and emissive maps take sRGB bindless slots
commits.message:
Renderer: albedo and emissive maps take sRGB bindless slots

Texture assets load as RGBA8 UNORM, and the bindless table bound them
as stored, so the deferred G-buffer and the forward shaders' bindless
lookup used sRGB-encoded albedo and emissive as linear. Only the
per-material u_AlbedoTexture fallback went through the sRGB copy, so
the same texture shaded differently between paths.

Bindless slots are now a GPUTextureSlot: texture asset plus colour
space. MaterialScene resolves albedo and emissive maps as sRGB, and
SceneRenderer binds those slots to MaterialAsset::GetSRGBTexture, the
shared sRGB copy (now public and mutex-guarded), so the sampler decodes
them and their mips are averaged in linear space. Data maps stay
linear. Only RGBA8 sources get a copy.

Textured surfaces render darker and more saturated, which is correct.

commits.subject: Renderer: sRGB colour mips average in linear space
commits.message:
Renderer: sRGB colour mips average in linear space

Albedo textures load as RGBA8 UNORM, so their mip chain averaged the
sRGB-encoded bytes, and CreateFromSRGB copied that darkened chain into
the sRGB copy. GenerateMips now handles SRGBA textures: it builds the
chain in an RGBA scratch image with LinearSampleSRGB.glsl (decode, 2x2
average, encode) and copies it back. CreateFromSRGB copies mip 0 only
and regenerates.

Mip sizes are max(size >> mip, 1) with rounded-up dispatches; the
truncated size / 8 left the edge texels of odd-sized levels unwritten.
Texture2D::Invalidate no longer generates every chain twice.

commits.subject: Sample scenes: re-tune lights for physical lighting
commits.message:
Sample scenes: re-tune lights for physical lighting

The sample scenes' lights were authored for the old model (diffuse
without Lambert's 1/PI, a 1 - d^2/r^2 falloff), so under physical
lighting their point and spot lights came out far too dim. Every Unitless
light is rescaled: the sun by PI, which keeps sunlit diffuse identical,
and each point and spot light so its diffuse light at half its range
matches the old look exactly (Benchmark, FMODDemo, NewSceneSystem: 241
lights). Closer than that they are now brighter and further out dimmer,
as inverse-square light is. Sun highlights get stronger, since the old
specular term was already normalized.

commits.subject: Renderer: GTAO and SSR reconstruct view positions correctly
commits.message:
Renderer: GTAO and SSR reconstruct view positions correctly

NDCToViewMul/Add were {2/P0, 2/P5} and {-1, -1}: x came out off-centre
and y pointed down, matching XeGTAO only for a square 90-degree camera.
GTAO's slice stepping assumes XeGTAO's y-up view space, so its horizons
did not line up with the surface normals. The constants are now XeGTAO's:
Mul = (2 tanX, -2 tanY), Add = (-tanX, tanY), with the matching
orthographic form.

SSR had worked around the old constants in a y-flipped space. It now uses
the renderer's view space as is: the G-buffer normal is no longer flipped,
and reprojection maps NDC to uv with v = 0.5 - 0.5 ndc.y. Its view
positions also follow the orthographic branch, and GTAO and SSR use the
constant view vector for an orthographic camera.

Rendering.md records the convention.

commits.subject: Renderer: orthographic camera support, sky rotation, new editor grid
commits.message:
Renderer: orthographic camera support, sky rotation, new editor grid

Orthographic cameras: UBCamera gains IsOrthographic (in the GLSL block,
ClusterBuild's inline copy and the HLSL Camera alike). Depth unpacking is
affine for an orthographic projection; LinearizeDeviceDepth and
GetViewDirection (Buffers.glslh) replace the perspective-only versions in
deferred and forward lighting, AO composite, DOF, SSR, scene composite and
GTAO, which also reconstructs view positions without the depth scale.
Cluster AABBs use parallel rays and a positive near plane, and the skybox
looks along the camera axis.

Sky rotation: SkyLightComponent::Rotation (degrees about +Y, serialized,
in the inspector) travels through the frame packet into
SceneData.EnvironmentMapRotation. IBL adds it to any per-material
rotation, the irradiance lookup now turns with the environment too, and
the skybox rotates by the same amount.

Editor grid: Grid.glsl is rewritten as a camera-centred floor grid with
constant-width anti-aliased lines that fade to their average coverage
below a pixel, power-of-ten cell sizes with a crossfade, coloured X/Z
axes, and distance and grazing-angle fades.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Renderer: point-light shadows, hardware PCF, cascade normal-offset bias
commits.message:
Renderer: point-light shadows, hardware PCF, cascade normal-offset bias

Point lights cast shadows through the spot shadow atlas: a shadowed light
takes six consecutive tiles, one per cube face, rendered at ~96 degrees so
the face the shader picks by the major axis stays inside its tile and
filter taps never cross a seam. Up to 8 point lights (scored by intensity
and distance) share the atlas with up to 16 spot lights; the atlas grows to
64 tiles (8x8). The point-light GPU struct reuses its dead MinRadius and
Falloff slots for the first tile index and the tile scale, so its layout
size is unchanged, and the buffer is uploaded after tile selection.
PointLightComponent::CastsShadows (default on) and SoftShadows now take
effect.

Every hard and PCF shadow tap goes through a new linear depth-comparison
sampler (r_ShadowSampler, set 3 binding 8), so each is a hardware 2x2 PCF.

Deferred directional shadows add a normal-offset receiver bias of 1.5
texels of each cascade, the texel size taken from the cascade matrix.

The light settings panel drops the dead point-light Falloff and Min Radius
rows. Rendering.md records the atlas layout, the sampler and the bias.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Renderer: physical punctual lighting; GTAO occludes indirect light only
commits.message:
Renderer: physical punctual lighting; GTAO occludes indirect light only

Every analytic light now goes through one shared BRDF (PBR.glslh,
LuxEvaluateDirectBRDF): Frostbite diffuse with Lambert's 1/PI, GGX with
height-correlated Smith visibility, Turquin multiscatter compensation and
a saturation-preserving firefly clamp. Point and spot lights fall off as
inverse-square, windowed to zero at their range. Light intensities now
mean what PhysicalLight.h says (illuminance for the sun, intensity for
point and spot lights), so existing scenes' punctual lights render
darker until re-tuned. Point lights' Falloff and Min Radius no longer do
anything and leave the inspector; they stay serialized.

GTAO used to multiply the finished scene color, darkening sunlight and
emission. GTAO and the AO composite now run before deferred lighting; the
composite resolves to its own RED8UN image, and deferred lighting applies
it with material AO to the IBL term only (also driving specular
occlusion). BeginScene binds it per frame on the render thread, or white
when GTAO is off.

Rendering.md updates the pass order and records both rules.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Merge editor-launch file-churn fix into dev
commits.message:
Merge editor-launch file-churn fix into dev

Editor launches no longer rewrite sample-project files (asset registry,
.lmat), and transparent draws sort by material handle, not address.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Renderer: IBL reads cube texel centres and the BRDF LUT at mip 0
commits.message:
Renderer: IBL reads cube texel centres and the BRDF LUT at mip 0

GetCubeMapTexCoord mapped each invocation to its texel's corner, half a
texel off on every mip of the equirect-to-cube, mip-filter and irradiance
passes. Rough surfaces read the smallest radiance mips, where a 1x1 face
was filtered around a cube corner instead of its centre, so rough walls
in Benchmark picked up sky colour. It now uses the texel centre, as
PreethamSky.glsl already did.

The BRDF LUT was created with a mip chain and sampled with
derivative-based LOD. Its (NdotV, roughness) coordinates are not a screen
UV, so silhouettes and normal-mapped detail read averaged mips. It is now
read at mip 0 and created without mips.

Rendering.md records both rules. Checked with golden captures of
Benchmark: rough walls and sphere silhouettes change, nothing else does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Renderer: transparent draws sort by material handle, not address
commits.message:
Renderer: transparent draws sort by material handle, not address

The transparent pass draws in sort-key order with no depth sort, and
the material key was the Material object's heap address. Benchmark has
two transparent materials (Bench_Glass, Bench_GlassAmber); their
relative address follows async load order, so the blend order of the
overlapping pavilion glass flipped between runs and Benchmark captured
one of two images (2.35% of pixels, max diff 154).

A draw with a material asset now sorts by its handle; raw override
materials, which have no handle, keep the pointer. Rendering.md's
determinism note says why a sort key that changes the image must come
from a stable ID.

Verified: forcing the key to handle ascending reproduced one image
exactly (max 0) and handle descending the other, so this order is the
whole difference. With the fix Benchmark matches the pre-change capture
(bad 0%, max 1, the unmodified build's run-to-run noise). No other
sample scene uses a transparent material.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Asset: an editor launch no longer rewrites sample-project files
commits.message:
Asset: an editor launch no longer rewrites sample-project files

Opening a scene rewrote every material imported from a mesh source
(31 .lmat files for FMODDemo, Benchmark and Physics), and every launch
rewrote AssetRegistry.lzr.

- MaterialSerializer: the mesh importer re-serializes each source
  material on load, and the existing unchanged-content check failed
  only because the YAML writer ends a document with a newline that the
  committed files (old emitter output) lack. The comparison now ignores
  leading and trailing whitespace.
- EditorAssetManager: the registry stores only Handle, FilePath and
  Type. Status and FileLastWriteTime are per-session state: entries load
  as not loaded, and ProcessDirectory re-reads every file's timestamp at
  startup before anything compares it, so the persisted values were
  never used. A saved "Loading" would also have kept GetAssetAsync from
  queueing the load. The file is written only when its content changes.
- AssetRegistry.lzr migrated once to that format (byte-identical to the
  writer's output); tests/yaml/reference.txt re-recorded for it.
- Architecture doc: the rule in the asset system section.

Verified (Release, golden_run.py FMODDemo,Benchmark,Physics in a clean
worktree): before, 31 .lmat files and the registry were dirtied; after,
no tracked file under Editor/LuxSampleProject changes or has its mtime
touched. An old-format registry is rewritten once to exactly the
committed file and left alone on the next launch. A material that did
change is still rewritten. FMODDemo and Physics captures match the
pre-change set at max diff 0. tests/yaml/run.py passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Core: Windows HasEnvironmentVariable reads the process environment
commits.message:
Core: Windows HasEnvironmentVariable reads the process environment

On Windows it only queried HKCU\Environment, the persistent user
variables, so variables a launcher sets for the editor process were
invisible. GoldenCapture never saw LUX_GOLDEN_DIR and every
golden_run.py capture timed out; LUX_THREADING_POLICY (--threading,
threading_ab.py) was ignored too. Linux already read getenv, which is
where the capture was developed. It now matches Linux.

Verified: two FMODDemo captures compare clean (max diff 0), Physics
opens on request, and single vs multi threading render identically.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Tools: single- vs multi-threaded A/B capture (threading_ab.py)
commits.message:
Tools: single- vs multi-threaded A/B capture (threading_ab.py)

LUX_THREADING_POLICY (Single / Multi) overrides the editor's threading
setting for one launch without saving it. golden_run.py --threading sets
it, and the summary records which policy ran. perf.json gains frameMs,
the whole main-loop iteration, the number that compares across the two
policies.

tests/rendering/threading_ab.py builds (Windows: Win-GenProjects.py
--last, then MSBuild; Linux: make Core and Editor), captures the scene

commits.subject: Core: deferred events no longer stall the event queue
commits.message:
Core: deferred events no longer stall the event queue

DispatchEvent<T> without DispatchImmediately queues an entry that waits
for SyncEvents(), and ProcessEvents stops at the first such entry. Nothing
ever called SyncEvents(), so the first deferred event (SelectionManager
sends one on every selection change) blocked the queue for good, and
every QueueEvent behind it never ran: the titlebar minimize,
maximize/restore and close buttons stopped working after the first
selection.

Application::Run now syncs once at the end of every frame, so deferred
events dispatch one frame later as documented. ProcessEvents also runs
the ready entries outside the queue lock, so a queued function that
queues another no longer deadlocks.

commits.subject: Renderer: NRI command buffers, submission and timeline fences (NRI Phase 13, step 6)
commits.message:
Renderer: NRI command buffers, submission and timeline fences (NRI Phase 13, step 6)

NRI now owns every command buffer and queue submission; NVRHI records and
submits nothing.

- RHIQueueTimeline (RHI/): one NRI timeline fence per queue. Submit runs
  under RenderCommandBuffer::LockQueue and returns the submission's value;
  AddWait makes a queue's next command-buffer submission wait for another
  queue's value; Wait/GetCompletedValue/GetSubmittedValue replace NVRHI's
  execution instances and event queries. Created by Window after
  RHIDevice::Init.
- CommandBufferPool (RHI/): NRI command buffers with their own allocators,
  one per frame-in-flight slot to start with, reused once their submission
  completes and grown, like NVRHI's command lists, when all are in flight.
  RenderCommandBuffer and the upload batch record from pools; the NVRHI
  command lists, their NRI wrappers and Get() are gone.
- RT_Submit takes an optional binary-semaphore wait (an NRI wrapper).
  Semaphore waits are no longer left for whichever submission comes next:
  the swapchain hands out its acquire semaphore once per frame
  (TakeAcquireSemaphore) to the first command buffer that draws to the back
  buffer, and Present waits for it itself when nothing did. The upload
  batch no longer takes the cross-queue waits added for the command buffer
  it is flushed ahead of (it did under NVRHI). RT_Wait is removed.
- VulkanSwapChain wraps its acquire and present semaphores as NRI fences.
  Present flushes the upload batch, then signals the present semaphore in
  a signal-only NRI submission. Frame pacing and Renderer::RT_BeginFrame
  wait for graphics timeline values instead of NVRHI event queries.
- A queue the device does not have (no compute family) records on
  graphics, with a warning; waits on it are dropped.
- RT_WaitForCompletion waits for the last submission's value; no fence
  per call.

Docs: Rendering.md (command buffers and submission, release queue),
Threading.md (queue lock rule), Architecture-LuxEngine.md, Conventions.md.

commits.subject: Renderer: GPU queries and markers on NRI (NRI Phase 13, step 5)
commits.message:
Renderer: GPU queries and markers on NRI (NRI Phase 13, step 5)

Timer queries, pipeline statistics and debug markers record through NRI;
NVRHI now records nothing into its command lists.

- Each command list slot owns a QuerySlot: an NRI TIMESTAMP pool (2048),
  a PIPELINE_STATISTICS pool on graphics queues (one query per frame
  segment) and a HOST_READBACK results buffer. The slot's first RT_Begin
  of a render frame publishes its previous frame and resets the pools;
  each RT_End copies what it wrote (CmdCopyQueries) and adds a barrier
  into host reads. One slot per frame in flight is required (frame pacing
  makes the read safe); command buffers with fewer get no queries, with a
  warning.
- The frame total keeps its segment semantics (Begin(true) adds a
  segment, a plain Begin restarts the measurement); pipeline statistics
  now cover every segment instead of the last submit. A timer used more
  than once in a frame reports its total.
- Timestamps are legal inside rendering, so timer queries no longer split
  NRI render passes.
- The raw Vulkan pipeline-statistics pools, which were never destroyed,
  are gone; the NRI pools are freed with the command buffer.
- Markers are CmdBeginAnnotation/CmdEndAnnotation; Aftermath checkpoints
  and Tracy zones take the NRI wrapper's native command buffer.
- VulkanDeviceManager enables meshShaderQueries when supported, and the
  NRI fork (LUX-2) adds the task/mesh counters only with that feature.

Docs: Rendering.md (GPU timing, rendering-scope splits), Architecture-
LuxEngine.md, Conventions.md.

commits.subject: Renderer: readbacks on NRI, NVRHI barrier mode removed (NRI Phase 13, step 4)
commits.message:
Renderer: readbacks on NRI, NVRHI barrier mode removed (NRI Phase 13, step 4)

Image2D and TextureCube::CopyToHostBuffer read back through ReadbackTexture
(Renderer/TextureReadback): the texture is required as CopySource, copied
with CmdReadbackTextureToBuffer into an NRI HOST_READBACK buffer, followed
by a global barrier into host reads (a fence wait alone does not make
device writes visible to the host, and the tracker has no host state),
submitted, and waited on with the new RenderCommandBuffer::
RT_WaitForCompletion (an NRI fence signalled after the submission). Rows
come back tightly packed, as before.

This also fixes a step-1 regression: the NVRHI staging copies relied on
NVRHI's own texture state, which nothing updates since barriers moved to
NRI, so their first transition named an undefined old layout.

- The NVRHI staging textures and the Automatic barrier mode are gone, so
  every command buffer records the tracker's barriers: BarrierMode,
  SetBarrierMode, RT_UsesExplicitBarriers and their branches removed.
- GetActive() is removed: no NVRHI resource command is left. NVRHI records
  only markers and timer queries.
- TextureCopyLayout (RHI/StagingMemory) now holds the row math shared by
  uploads and readbacks, including the NRI fork's four-byte depth plane of
  D32S8.
- Dead commented-out NVRHI barrier code in TextureCube::GenerateMips
  removed.

Docs: Rendering.md (readbacks; the barrier-mode bullet and the GetActive
rules replaced), Conventions.md, Architecture-LuxEngine.md.

commits.subject: Renderer: uploads on NRI, first texture transitions (NRI Phase 13, step 3)
commits.message:
Renderer: uploads on NRI, first texture transitions (NRI Phase 13, step 3)

Every GPU-side write is now an NRI copy from Lux-owned staging memory; no
writeBuffer or writeTexture is left.

- StagingStream (RHI/StagingMemory): 4 MiB HOST_UPLOAD pages handed out
  linearly, larger uploads on a page of their own, recycled through the
  deletion queue once the frame that submitted the copies completes. Pages
  of the default size return to a pool (two created by Renderer::Init, at
  most sixteen kept).
- UploadContext (RHI/UploadContext): what RecordResourceUpload callbacks
  record into. The upload batch has its own NRI wrapper, tracker and
  staging stream; WriteBuffer/WriteTexture require CopyDest and record
  CmdCopyBuffer/CmdUploadBufferToTexture (texture rows repacked at NRI's
  row alignment), and the flush returns every resource to its resting
  state before submitting.
- RenderCommandBuffer::RT_WriteBuffer for GPU-only StorageBuffer::RT_SetData
  and VertexBuffer::RT_SetData; its staging is retired at RT_Submit.
  VertexBuffer::RT_SetData now honours its offset (NVRHI's call dropped it).
- New textures and swapchain images are created undefined, but the tracker
  starts every texture in its resting state. NVRHI covered that with its
  per-texture stateInitialized flag; since step 1 the NRI barriers named
  the resting layout as the old layout. NRITexture::Create and
  VulkanSwapChain::Create now record the first transition (undefined ->
  resting state) in the upload batch, which is submitted before any
  command buffer that could use the texture.
- The tracker and emitter can run on any thread (the batch's): their
  one-time error reports are now locked or atomic.
- Dead commented-out NVRHI code in VertexBuffer::SetData removed.

Deviation from the plan: no per-frame-slot UploadRing; staging is a pool
of pages per submitting stream, which serves the any-thread upload batch
and frame command buffers alike.

The async transfer path (off by default) stays invalid as before: graphics
barriers on the copy queue and no queue-ownership transfer.

Docs: Rendering.md (uploads, staging, first transitions, the copy-queue
caveat), Threading.md, Conventions.md, Architecture-LuxEngine.md.

commits.subject: Renderer: copies and clears on NRI (NRI Phase 13, step 2)
commits.message:
Renderer: copies and clears on NRI (NRI Phase 13, step 2)

Copies and clears record with NRI inside RenderCommandBuffer::RT_BeginNRITransfer,
which closes an open NRI rendering scope and opens a segment that commits the
tracker's barriers, so their RT_CommitBarriers lines are gone.

- Renderer::CopyImage and Texture2D::CreateFromSRGB: CmdCopyTexture (the sRGB
  copy is one whole-resource copy of every mip).
- The cluster light grid and counter zero-fills: CmdZeroBuffer.
- Renderer::ClearImage: CmdClearStorage through a StorageImageClear. NRI clears
  storage only through a view held by a bound descriptor set, so the clear owns
  a one-set DescriptorSetGroup with that view, built once, and binds it with a
  shared one-set compute layout created in Renderer::Init. A clear keeps the
  texture it was built for; SceneRenderer rebuilds the pre-integration
  visibility clear with the texture's views (resize and re-aliasing).
- The image is cleared in UnorderedAccess rather than CopyDest, and
  UnorderedAccess now carries CLEAR_STORAGE access: vkCmdClearColorImage is a
  transfer write, which shader-storage access alone does not cover.

Docs: Rendering.md, Conventions.md and Architecture-LuxEngine.md describe
NRI copies, clears and StorageImageClear; the stale "NVRHI keeps barrier
emission" lines are corrected.

commits.subject: Renderer: barriers recorded as NRI barriers (NRI Phase 13, step 1)
commits.message:
Renderer: barriers recorded as NRI barriers (NRI Phase 13, step 1)

The resource state tracker now works out each transition itself (before
and after state, per run of subresources) and NRIBarrierEmitter records
them with CmdBarrier into the command list's NRI wrapper, created at
RT_Begin. Access, layout and stages follow NVRHI's Vulkan mapping; the
copy states wait on all commands, as NRI's COPY stage does not cover
clears and fills. NVRHIBarrierEmitter and the Debug Tracker/NVRHI
cross-check are gone.

Resources are named by tracked descriptions made when they are created
(NRITexture/NRIBuffer::GetTracked, ImageInfo::Tracked, swapchain images
resting in Present), whose handles are the NRI texture or buffer. Raw-view
and UAV buffers get NRI's shader-resource usages so NRI validation
accepts their barriers. NVRHI copies, clears and writeBuffer that remain
commit the tracker's barriers first.

commits.subject: Renderer: one recording path on NRI (NRI Phase 12, step 1)
commits.message:
Renderer: one recording path on NRI (NRI Phase 12, step 1)

The Renderer.ExplicitBarriers, NRICompute, NRIGraphics and NRIImGui
settings are gone with their NVRHI branches: every pass, draw and
dispatch, the UI included, records through NRI under explicit barriers.
Work NRI cannot record is skipped and logged once per pipeline or shader.

Barrier requirements no longer come from NVRHI binding sets and graphics
state. Each DescriptorSetGroup records what its sets access
(DescriptorSetUses) while it is written; RT_BeginNRIRenderPass requires
the attachments and the pass's sets, RT_BeginNRIDraw the draw's set and
buffers, RT_BeginNRIDispatch the dispatch's sets, with NVRHI's change
detection. GraphicsState, ComputeState, MeshletState and the RT_Commit*
functions are removed, as is the NVRHI meshlet binding set and the ImGui
NVRHI path. A UI frame that cannot be drawn still waits for the acquire.

commits.subject: ImGui: drawn with NRI (NRI Phase 11, step 2)
commits.message:
ImGui: drawn with NRI (NRI Phase 11, step 2)

Renderer.NRIImGui (off by default, latched in RT_BeginFrame) draws the UI
and platform windows with NRI into the swapchain, under explicit barriers.
The pipeline for the main window's format is made in Init; geometry is
host-visible per frame slot and written through Map before recording, so
a failure falls back to NVRHI with nothing recorded. Descriptor sets come
from per-slot pools reset when the slot comes round, growing by doubling.

RenderCommandBuffer gains RT_SetNRIScissor and 16-bit index buffers;
VulkanSwapChain exposes its NRI color format.

commits.subject: ImGui: textures are engine images; command buffer barrier modes (NRI Phase 11, step 1)
commits.message:
ImGui: textures are engine images; command buffer barrier modes (NRI Phase 11, step 1)

ImGuiTextureInfo now holds a Ref<Image2D> and a resolved
TextureSubresourceRange instead of a raw nvrhi::ITexture*. The
snapshot's copies of the texture tables keep every drawn image alive,
so its separate NVRHI keep-alive list goes.

ImGui-owned textures (the font atlas) are Image2Ds uploaded through
Image2D::SetData and the shared upload list. That fixes the old path,
which ran RT_Begin/RT_Submit on the renderer's command buffer from the
main thread while the render thread could be using it, and lets the
resource state tracker model the atlas like any texture. An update
uploads into a new image rather than one frames in flight may still
sample (the upload may run on the copy queue).

RenderCommandBuffer::SetAutomaticBarriersOnly becomes SetBarrierMode
(Settings, Automatic, Explicit), read at each RT_Begin: readbacks stay
Automatic, the ImGui renderer is Automatic on NVRHI and will be
Explicit on NRI (step 2).

commits.subject: Renderer: inside-rendering audit for NRI passes (NRI Phase 10, step 6)
commits.message:
Renderer: inside-rendering audit for NRI passes (NRI Phase 10, step 6)

In Debug, every time NVRHI work splits an NRI render pass (an NVRHI
command, draw or dispatch, a barrier, a timer query), the split is
reported once per pass and reason:

  NRI render pass '<pass>' (<command buffer>) is split by <reason> inside it

A split is correct but stores and reloads every attachment, so a
reported command belongs before or after its pass. Where the plan
asserted, this reports: the splits keep rendering correct, and an
assert would stop the first verification run at the first one.

commits.subject: Renderer: render passes and draws on NRI (NRI Phase 10, step 5)
commits.message:
Renderer: render passes and draws on NRI (NRI Phase 10, step 5)

Behind the new Renderer.NRIGraphics setting (default off, latched per
render frame), render passes and draws are recorded with NRI inside
the NVRHI command buffers.

- BeginRenderPass, and the meshlet pre-depth pass, open an NRI render
  pass (RenderCommandBuffer::RT_BeginNRIRenderPass): the clears become
  load ops; the pipeline, layout, viewport, line width, shading rate
  and the pass's sets are bound once per rendering scope.
- RenderQuad, RenderGeometry, SubmitFullscreenQuad(WithOverrides) and
  SceneRenderer's static mesh (indexed and indirect) and meshlet draws
  record through Renderer::RT_DrawIndexedWithNRI / RT_DrawMeshTasksWith
  NRI, which bind only set 0, the vertex and index buffers and the root
  constants, skipping repeats. Each keeps its NVRHI path as the
  fallback, logged once per pipeline.
- NVRHI never records inside an NRI rendering scope: GetActive(), the
  RT_Commit* functions, RT_CommitBarriers with barriers pending and
  timer queries close it, and the next draw reopens it with the
  attachments loaded and the pass state rebound. That reproduces
  NVRHI's implicit render-pass splitting. Markers stay inside.
- Barriers are the tracker's, so NRI graphics implies explicit
  barriers. ResourceStateTracker::HasPendingBarriers says when a draw
  needs a commit between two scopes; CPU-visible and volatile buffers,
  which NVRHI never transitions, do not count.
- The one raw vkCmdSetLineWidth sets line pipelines' width (LUX-1).
- NRI viewports keep NVRHI's Y convention (same negative-height flip).
- Fix from step 2: NRI mesh pipelines take no shading-rate state, as
  NVRHI's MeshletPipelineDesc has none.

The editor's Application Settings gains "NRI Graphics". Rendering.md,
Architecture and Conventions describe the model.

commits.subject: Renderer: NRI meshlet descriptor sets (NRI Phase 10, step 4)
commits.message:
Renderer: NRI meshlet descriptor sets (NRI Phase 10, step 4)

MeshSource::RT_GetOrCreateNRIMeshletSet builds the NRI twin of the
meshlet binding set (set 0 of the meshlet shader: the meshlet, meshlet
vertex, meshlet triangle and render vertex buffers as read-only raw
views), as NVRHI's set is built: per mesh, on demand, keyed by the
shader's layout, and dropped when the mesh rebuilds its geometry. It
is a one-instance DescriptorSetGroup written once, since a mesh's
meshlet buffers never change; the pool is freed through the deletion
queue with the mesh. A failed build is logged once per layout; missing
buffers are not cached, so a still-streaming mesh gets its set later.

Deferred from Phase 9 to here, its first user (the mesh-shader draw,
step 5).

commits.subject: Renderer: NRI framebuffer attachment views (NRI Phase 10, step 3)
commits.message:
Renderer: NRI framebuffer attachment views (NRI Phase 10, step 3)

Framebuffer::RT_Invalidate builds an NRI color / depth-stencil
attachment view beside each NVRHI attachment, from the same image,
mip, layer (ExistingImageLayer) and format override, as NVRHI's
createFramebuffer resolves them. The views come from the images' view
caches (which own them) and are rebuilt whenever the NVRHI framebuffer
is, so the stale-attachment repair covers both. Swapchain targets
return the acquired back buffer's Phase 8 view
(VulkanSwapChain::GetCurrentNRIColorAttachment).

Read-only depth and 3D attachments get no NRI views (Lux uses neither);
such a framebuffer logs why and its passes stay on NVRHI.

NRITextureViewKey gains a Format (UNKNOWN = the texture's own) for the
attachment format override.

commits.subject: Renderer: NRI graphics and mesh pipelines (NRI Phase 10, step 2)
commits.message:
Renderer: NRI graphics and mesh pipelines (NRI Phase 10, step 2)

Every Pipeline gets an NRI twin, created eagerly in RT_Invalidate with
the NVRHI pipeline (and recreated with it on shader reload), for vertex
and mesh-shader pipelines alike. It is translated from the finished
NVRHI desc, as Phase 8 did for textures and buffers, so the two cannot
drift apart while both exist:

- vertex input from NVRHI's attribute array: attribute i at location i,
  one binding per buffer index, stride and step rate per buffer;
- topology, fill, cull, winding, depth bias and VRS from the raster
  state; MSAA from the framebuffer's sample count;
- one blend state per color attachment, formats and depth format from
  the framebuffer info NVRHI builds its pipeline against;
- the shader's NRI layout and its SPIR-V (VS/PS or TASK/MESH/PS).

Anything NRI cannot express (triangle fans, stencil, array attributes,
VRS NRI reports as unsupported, unknown formats) leaves the pipeline
NVRHI-only, logged. The NRI pipeline is freed through the GPU deletion
queue. Nothing binds it yet (step 5).

NRI layouts now carry the shader's own stage mask: NRI's validation
checks each graphics pipeline stage against it and reads StageBits::ALL
(0) as no stages. ToNRIFormat moves into NVRHIWrappers for reuse.

Renderer: review fixes for NRI Phases 6-8

From a review pass over the P6-P8 commits:

- NRITexture/NRIBuffer::Create log why they failed (no NRI format for
  the NVRHI one, or NRI creation failed). Callers that only branched on

commits.subject: Renderer: NRI compute dispatches (NRI Phase 9, step 5)
commits.message:
Renderer: NRI compute dispatches (NRI Phase 9, step 5)

Compute dispatches can be recorded with NRI inside the NVRHI command
buffers, behind the Renderer.NRICompute setting (default off, latched
per render frame like Renderer.ExplicitBarriers).

RenderCommandBuffer gains NRI segments: a non-owning NRI wrapper of the
open command list's VkCommandBuffer, made by the first segment after
RT_Begin and destroyed by RT_End. A segment starts with NVRHI's pending
barriers committed and ends with NVRHI's cached state cleared, so NVRHI
rebinds after it. Barriers stay NVRHI's: setComputeState still runs in
both modes.

The NRI path binds the shader's NRI layout, the pass's NRI pipeline,
the NRI sets matching the NVRHI bindings (the material's in its set)
and the push constants as root constants. A missing NRI object falls
back to NVRHI, logged once per shader. ToNRIQueueType moves to
RHIDevice.

commits.subject: Renderer: NRI descriptor sets beside NVRHI binding sets (NRI Phase 9, step 4)
commits.message:
Renderer: NRI descriptor sets beside NVRHI binding sets (NRI Phase 9, step 4)

- DescriptorSetGroup (Renderer/RHI): an NRI pool with one set per frame in
  flight, written while it is built and never again; shared like the NVRHI
  binding-set handles it mirrors, the last reference frees the pool through
  the deletion queue.
- DescriptorSetManager::BakeSet also builds the set's NRI group from the same
  inputs (constant buffers, raw storage views by reflected access, texture
  views matching NVRHI's dimension and subresources, samplers). Inputs can
  change several times per frame, so a re-bake replaces the group instead of
  rewriting a set the GPU may still read. Missing resources are deferred
  exactly as BakeSet defers them. GetNRIDescriptorSet(frame, set).
- VulkanShader gives the pool size and binding->range index per set.
- Material::GetNRIDescriptorSet (set 0).
- BindlessTextureTable: a bindless-only NRI layout, one NRI set per frame
  table (variable-sized to the capacity), written in RT_WriteTable with the
  NVRHI table; RT_GetNRISet.

Meshlet sets follow with mesh-shader draws in Phase 10. New files: regenerate
the projects.

commits.subject: Renderer: NRI pipeline layouts and compute pipelines (NRI Phase 9, step 3)
commits.message:
Renderer: NRI pipeline layouts and compute pipelines (NRI Phase 9, step 3)

- VulkanShader builds an NRI pipeline layout with its NVRHI binding layouts
  (end of CreateDescriptors, so at load and after every reload): one
  descriptor set per declared set number (register space = set number), ranges
  from the reflection (constant buffers, raw storage buffers as structured
  views, textures, samplers, storage images), StageBits::ALL so equal bindings
  give compatible set layouts, the shared bindless range for set 4, and one
  root-constant block covering the push constants. GetNRISetIndex maps a set
  number to its position in the layout. Released through the deletion queue.
- BindlessTextureTable::GetNRIRange is that shared bindless range.
- PipelineCompute creates the NRI compute pipeline next to the NVRHI one
  (constructor and shader reload).

Failures are logged and leave the NRI objects null; the NVRHI path is
unaffected. Nothing records with them yet.

commits.subject: Renderer: NRI owns GPU textures and buffers (NRI Phase 8)
commits.message:
Renderer: NRI owns GPU textures and buffers (NRI Phase 8)

Every GPU texture and buffer is now allocated by NRI; NVRHI keeps rendering
through non-owning handles to the same VkImage/VkBuffer, created with the same
NVRHI desc as before, so binding sets, framebuffers, barriers and uploads are
unchanged.

- Renderer/RHI/NVRHIWrappers: move-only NRITexture / NRIBuffer owners. The NRI
  desc is derived from the NVRHI desc (format through the VkFormat, usage from
  NVRHI's flags, EXCLUSIVE images like NVRHI's, memory location from
  cpuAccess). Destroying or reassigning one frees the NVRHI handle and then the
  NRI resource through the GPU deletion queue.
- Image2D, VertexBuffer, IndexBuffer, UniformBuffer, StorageBuffer, meshlet
  buffers and the ImGui renderer use them; CPU writes go through
  NRIBuffer::Map. ImageInfo gains RHITexture and the live-image registry is
  keyed by the NRI texture.
- Swapchain images get non-owning NRI wrappers and color-attachment views.
- GetGPUMemoryStats uses NRI's QueryVideoMemoryInfo; VK_EXT_memory_budget is
  enabled when supported and the raw Vulkan helpers are gone.
- SubmitResourceFree releases immediately once the renderer has shut down.
- RHIDevice::Init failure is fatal now that nothing allocates without it.
- VertexBuffer::SetData applies the offset to the destination (all callers
  pass 0).

commits.message:
Renderer: Nsight Aftermath on the Lux-created device (NRI Phase 7)

On NVIDIA, Debug and Release now produce GPU crash dumps. VulkanDeviceManager
enables Aftermath before vkCreateDevice when the GPU supports
VK_NV_device_diagnostic_checkpoints and VK_NV_device_diagnostics_config, adds
both extensions (so NVRHI and NRI get them) and chains
VkDeviceDiagnosticsConfigCreateInfoNV. Elsewhere the log says why Aftermath is
unavailable and nothing else changes.

- Debug/Aftermath.{h,cpp} replaces NVIDIA's sample files, which exit(1)ed on
  any Aftermath error and loaded mock cube.*.spirv shaders. The Aftermath
  library is loaded at runtime (new Lux::SharedLibrary) instead of linked, so
  a missing library no longer stops the executables from starting; Editor and
  Lux-Runtime copy it beside themselves in every config but Dist.
- RenderCommandBuffer::RT_BeginMarker sets a checkpoint; the crash callback
  resolves the checkpoint pointers into names (.markers.txt and the log).
- VulkanShader::LoadAndCreateShaders registers the SPIR-V the driver gets,
  for shader address mapping.
- VulkanDeviceManager::ReportDeviceLost handles NVRHI's "Device Removed!"
  message and VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST from acquire and present: it waits for the
  dump, logs its path under <log directory>/GPUCrashDumps and aborts.

no-ops there.
