commits.subject: Renderer: vendor NRI and wrap the Vulkan device (NRI Phase 6)
commits.message:
Renderer: vendor NRI and wrap the Vulkan device (NRI Phase 6)

NRI is the submodule Core/vendor/NRI, fork starbounded-dev/NRI branch lux
(StudioCherno hazel merged with NVIDIA-RTX/NRI main, v181), built by the fork's
own premake5.lua into five static libraries. NRI uses its own Vulkan headers
(v1.4.364) and VMA; Core keeps the SDK headers and defines NRI_STATIC_LIBRARY.

RHIDevice (Renderer/RHI) wraps the VkDevice, queues and extension lists that
VulkanDeviceManager creates with nriCreateDeviceFromVKDevice, fetches the Core,
Helper, WrapperVK, SwapChain and MeshShader interfaces and the queues, and logs
NRI's DeviceDesc. Window::Init creates it right after the device; Window::Shutdown
destroys it before the device manager. A Debug self-test creates a buffer,
texture and view, records a barrier and a zero fill, submits under the queue
lock and waits on a fence. Nothing renders through NRI yet.

NRI reads feature support from the physical device rather than from what was
enabled, so VulkanDeviceManager now enables, when supported: sync2 from core 1.3
support, 1.4 maintenance5/maintenance6/pushDescriptor (the KHR extensions on 1.3
devices), shaderDrawParameters, samplerFilterMinmax, hostQueryReset and the
descriptor-indexing UpdateAfterBind/UpdateUnusedWhilePending bits.

NRI errors log under the Renderer tag and break only in Debug (NRI's default
raises SIGTRAP).

commits.subject: RenderGraph: access kinds, buffers and pass-entry barriers (NRI Phase 5)
commits.message:
RenderGraph: access kinds, buffers and pass-entry barriers (NRI Phase 5)

The graph now records how each pass touches each resource (AccessKind:
sampled, storage read/write, color/depth attachment, copy, indirect,
uniform) and models storage buffers (AddExternalBuffer: tagged handles,
slots after the textures, never transient or aliased). AddPass extends
Reads/Writes from the accesses; accesses and buffers are folded into
the structure hash.

Compile() prebuilds each pass's entry requirements (resources it uses
in a single state); Execute(result, commandBuffer) requires them in one
batch before the pass when explicit barriers are on. In Debug a tracker
requirement log flags UndeclaredAccess: a pass requiring a graph
resource it did not declare, the case that can become a
use-after-alias. Four new self-tests cover buffers, access-derived
Reads/Writes, hash sensitivity and entry requirements; all pass.

SceneRenderer derives texture kinds from each pass's existing
Reads/Writes (so lifetimes and aliasing are unchanged) and declares the
cluster, culling, indirect, light-list and exposure buffers. The cluster
passes no longer need UntrackedResources. The Renderer Debugger shows
buffers and the runtime diagnostics.

With explicit barriers off (the default) execution is unchanged.

commits.subject: Renderer: resource state tracker and explicit barriers (NRI Phase 4)
commits.message:
Renderer: resource state tracker and explicit barriers (NRI Phase 4)

Adds Renderer/RHI/ResourceStateTracker (per-command-buffer state model,
subresource-granular, resting states restored at RT_End, Debug
cross-check against NVRHI) and NVRHIBarrierEmitter. Behind the new
Renderer.ExplicitBarriers setting (Application Settings, default off,
latched per render frame), NVRHI's automatic barriers are turned off and
the tracker places every barrier.

The commit functions require everything the graphics/compute/meshlet
state binds, mirroring NVRHI's automatic change detection rule for rule
(changed sets, dirty after copy/clear/write, UAV sets always, other
kinds reset per commit), so both modes emit the same barriers.
Copy/clear/write sites call RT_Require*; the manual transitions that
were always there (PipelineCompute barriers, bloom/pre-convolution mip
chains, GenerateMips) now go through RT_Transition*. Readback and ImGui
command buffers keep automatic barriers until NRI Phases 13 and 11.

With the toggle off nothing changes: the explicit paths are skipped and
transitions issue the same NVRHI calls as before. Turning it on by
default waits on the goldens/validation/cross-check runs listed in the
plan's Appendix C, along with the deviations from the plan.

commits.subject: Renderer: frame-numbered GPU lifetime and render frame slots (NRI Phase 3)
commits.message:
Renderer: frame-numbered GPU lifetime and render frame slots (NRI Phase 3)

RT_GetCurrentFrameIndex() was the swapchain back-buffer index. Under
MAILBOX that is not sequential, so a per-frame slot (descriptor sets,
bindless tables, buffer sets, command lists) could be rewritten while
the GPU still read it; with more than three swapchain images it also
indexed past DescriptorSetManager's 3-entry arrays.

Renderer::RT_BeginFrame, first in every render frame, closes the ending
frame behind a graphics-queue event, advances a monotonic frame number,
waits for frame N - FramesInFlight and retires the releases queued up to
it. RT_GetCurrentFrameIndex() is now frameNumber % FramesInFlight, safe
to reuse because of that wait. Closing at the next frame's start covers
work queued after Present and frames whose acquire failed.

SubmitResourceFree now feeds Renderer/RHI/GPUDeletionQueue (frame-tagged
releases, pending count/bytes, traced in Debug), the NRI-ready
replacement for the slot ring. Shutdown waits for idle, then drains.
RendererConfig::MaxFramesInFlight sizes the per-frame static_vectors and
clamps FramesInFlight.

Build-verified only (Release Core/Editor/Lux-Runtime, Debug spot-build);
the validation, memory and present-mode checks are listed for the user
in the plan's Appendix C.

commits.subject: Renderer: drain the GPU release queue every frame, not only at shutdown
commits.message:
Renderer: drain the GPU release queue every frame, not only at shutdown

SubmitResourceFree lambdas were only ever executed in Renderer::Shutdown.
Its one live caller, ~BindlessTextureTable, therefore pinned three
16k-slot descriptor tables, and every texture they referenced, for the
rest of the session each time a SceneRenderer was destroyed.

The queues are now a render-thread slot ring. RT_ReleaseRetiredResources,
called after the swapchain acquire each frame, closes the current slot
behind a graphics-queue event query and runs the oldest slot once its
event has signalled. An event, not frame counting: NVRHI does not keep
descriptor tables alive from command lists, and Present() skips its
frame pacing when an acquire fails.

This also fixes the slot choice. The render thread used the back-buffer
index, which is not sequential under MAILBOX and reaches 7 with an
8-image swapchain (past the 3-entry array), and the main-thread path
used its own frame counter one frame ahead of the render thread. The
slot is now always taken on the render thread at the point of release.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Renderer: implement TextureCube readback and upload on NVRHI
commits.message:
Renderer: implement TextureCube readback and upload on NVRHI

CopyToHostBuffer and CopyFromBuffer had been empty since the move to
NVRHI. Both now use the pre-NVRHI layout (mip-major, six faces per mip,
tight rows): readback copies every mip/face to a staging cube on the
cube's own command list and waits; upload writes each mip/face through
the shared upload batch, clamped to the image's mip count and checked
against the buffer size.

Also fixed on the way:
- The TextureCube constructor sized initial data as 4 bytes per texel;
  a float cube's per-face upload would read past the copy. Size from the
  format, and refuse short data.
- TextureRuntimeSerializer slept a full second before every cube
  readback, recorded the full theoretical mip chain instead of the
  image's real count, and leaked the buffer on load.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Renderer: read back block-compressed textures instead of an empty buffer
commits.message:
Renderer: read back block-compressed textures instead of an empty buffer

Image2D::CopyToHostBuffer sized its buffer as width x height x BPP, and
BPP is 0 for BC formats, so every BC texture (any .dds import) read back
as zero bytes. The asset-pack builder serializes Texture2D through this
readback, so exported games got empty BC textures, which the runtime
zero-fills: DDS textures rendered black. Size and copy by row pitch and
block-row count instead (new Utils::GetImageMemoryRowCount).

ThumbnailCache wrote width x height x 4 bytes from whatever came back.
It was only safe because BC readback used to be empty; with real BC data
it would read past the buffer. The disk cache now writes only 8-bit
RGBA/SRGBA sources and checks the buffer size.

commits.subject: Fix custom-titlebar window controls on Windows
commits.message:
Fix custom-titlebar window controls on Windows

The editor hid the native titlebar with GLFW_DECORATED=false on every
platform. On Win32 that makes a WS_POPUP window without WS_THICKFRAME, and
the GLFW fork's custom frame (WM_NCCALCSIZE / WM_NCHITTEST: resize
borders, HTCAPTION titlebar drag, double-click maximize, Aero Snap) only
runs for thick-framed windows with the fork's GLFW_TITLEBAR hint off. So
none of it worked. Windows now keeps the decorated window and drops only
the caption with GLFW_TITLEBAR=false; X11/Wayland stay undecorated, which
is the path the fork implements there.

With the native frame active, the titlebar drag zone becomes HTCAPTION, so:
- on Windows it now starts after the menu bar (as on Linux), otherwise the
  menus would turn into drag handles;
- while any popup is open the titlebar claims no clicks, since a menu's
  dropdown starts inside the tall titlebar.

Not yet compiled or run on Windows.

commits.subject: Add Lux::Yaml, the engine YAML layer over rapidyaml (migration phase 2)
commits.message:
Add Lux::Yaml, the engine YAML layer over rapidyaml (migration phase 2)

Serialization/Yaml.h/.cpp: Load/LoadFile -> Node, Writer, and Convert<T>
conversions, shaped like the yaml-cpp subset the engine uses so
serializers port mechanically. Keeps the semantics callers rely on:
key-exists truthiness (empty values are defined), lenient yaml-cpp
bools, integer indices on maps are keys, Dump() is the value only.
Writes output style C: block containers, [x, y, z] vectors, shortest
round-trip floats, null-like strings quoted. rapidyaml stays out of the
header; a Node holds a Ref to its document; throwing error handlers are
installed via call_once (rapidyaml's defaults abort()).

tests/yaml/run.py also builds the oracle over Lux::Yaml: all 188
tracked YAML files match the yaml-cpp reference, all survive parse ->
Writer -> re-parse, and a self-test covers semantics, conversions,
quoting, determinism and malformed input. Conventions.md points new
YAML code at Lux::Yaml.

Requires project regeneration (scripts\Win-GenProjects.bat).

commits.subject: Scene: read YAML nodes const while deserializing entities
commits.message:
Scene: read YAML nodes const while deserializing entities

DeserializeEntities iterated non-const YAML::Node handles, so each
probe for a component an entity lacks (~36 keys per entity) made
yaml-cpp allocate and insert an empty node. On the 7,264-entity
Benchmark scene that was ~250k needless allocations: slow lookups, and
a bloated tree that was slow to free.

Bind every node read in DeserializeEntities const. Parsed values are
unchanged (present keys identical; missing keys still yield the
fallback or a caught YAML::Exception); verified by opening and
re-saving Benchmark with no diff.

Tracy, Release, Benchmark open: 24.1 s -> 11.1 s
(component pass 11.4 -> 2.5 s, tree destruction 6.7 -> 2.8 s).
Standalone yaml-cpp: 36-key probe 472 -> 130 ms, tree free 297 -> 107 ms.

commits.subject: Renderer: guard the Image2D registry with a mutex
commits.message:
Renderer: guard the Image2D registry with a mutex

s_ImageReferences was written by RT_Invalidate on the render thread
(and by Release/SetTransientAliasSource wherever an image dies) while
SceneRenderer::UpdateMemoryStatistics iterated it on the main thread via
GetImageRefs(), which handed out the raw map. A resize or release during
that walk could invalidate the iterator or free an image mid-read.

Guard every access with s_ImageReferencesMutex and replace
GetImageRefs() with ForEachLiveImage(fn), which visits under the lock;
Release() erases under the same lock, so a dying image waits for the
visit. Drops an unused [[maybe_unused]] GetImageRefs() handle in the
Vulkan validation callback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Renderer: replace the TextureCube registry with an atomic counter
commits.message:
Renderer: replace the TextureCube registry with an atomic counter

s_TextureCubeReferences was an unsynchronised std::map written on
create and release, while cubes are created on the main/asset threads
and destroyed wherever their last Ref drops (often the render thread).
Its only reader was .size() in two log lines. Replace it with an atomic
live-cube count, and demote the per-destroy WARN (routine, not a
warning) to a Renderer trace.

commits.subject: Renderer: set environment bindings on the render thread
commits.message:
Renderer: set environment bindings on the render thread

SceneRenderer set the environment cubes on the deferred-lighting and
transparent passes (BeginScene) and the skybox material (SkyboxPass) on
the main thread every frame, while the render thread read the same
inputs in Prepare for the previous frame. Harmless while the cube never
changed; on Stop the runtime environment was released and swapped out
mid-read, so the render thread copied a Ref to a freed TextureCube and
double-freed it (heap breakpoint in Allocator::Free).

Apply those bindings (and the skybox LOD/intensity) inside
Renderer::Submit lambdas so they are ordered before the reads. Documents
the rule in Threading.md.

commits.subject: Editor: undo/redo patches only the step's entities in place
commits.message:
Editor: undo/redo patches only the step's entities in place

Every Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y rebuilt the whole scene from the baseline and
swapped it in, re-deserializing every entity and forcing a full renderer
re-sync (seconds on the 7,264-entity Benchmark scene).

RestoreSceneStep now applies just the step's entity blocks to the live
scene via SceneSerializer::ApplyEntitySnapshots, which removes each
entity with the new Scene::DestroyEntityForRestore (DestroyEntity's
cleanup without child recursion or parent-list edits) and re-runs the
normal entity deserializer on the blocks. A step is closed over
hierarchy edits, so Parent/Children links stay consistent. On failure,
and in LUX_DEBUG on any divergence from the baseline, it falls back to
the full rebuild. Scene metadata read is shared via
DeserializeSceneMetadata.

commits.subject: Editor: fix viewport picking always selecting the ground
commits.message:
Editor: fix viewport picking always selecting the ground

RayIntersectsEntity compared hit distances in each entity's local
space, so a large-scale entity (the ground plane) reported a tiny t and
won over everything in front of it. It also tested bounds with the
local transform, so parented entities were tested at the wrong place,
and placed light/camera icons at the local translation.

Use the world transform and compare world-space distances along the ray.

commits.subject: Editor: snapshot only the edited entities on scoped undo commits
commits.message:
Editor: snapshot only the edited entities on scoped undo commits

Every undoable edit re-serialized all entities (~1.1 s on the 7,264-
entity Benchmark scene). EditorStack now records each signal's scope:
MarkSceneEdited is scene-wide, MarkEntitiesEdited names entities (the
gizmo), and PushCopy uses the active ScopedEditTarget, which
SceneHierarchyPanel::DrawComponents sets to the selection, falling back
to scene-wide. Scoped commits serialize and diff only those entities
plus the scene metadata; any scene-wide signal forces a full snapshot.

The baseline stays complete (undo restores the whole scene from it),
and LUX_DEBUG builds verify each scoped commit against a full capture,
logging and resyncing if an edit touched entities it did not name.

commits.subject: ImGui: fix use-after-free when a platform viewport closes
commits.message:
ImGui: fix use-after-free when a platform viewport closes

Render tasks for secondary ImGui viewports captured a raw pointer to
ImGuiViewportData. The render thread runs those tasks after the next
frame's UI pass, where UpdatePlatformWindows may already have destroyed
the viewport (e.g. closing the material picker popup), crashing in

skipping it when expired. Document the one-frame lambda delay rule in
Threading.md.

commits.subject: Assets: regenerate default capsule mesh with UVs
commits.message:
Assets: regenerate default capsule mesh with UVs

Capsule.gltf was the only default primitive exported without
TEXCOORD_0. The importer fills missing UVs with (0,0), so every capsule
sampled a single corner texel; materials whose corner texel is black
(several Sponza textures) rendered pitch black, and no tangents could be
generated for normal mapping.

Regenerated procedurally with the same shape (Y-up, radius 0.5, height 2),
arc-length V, and a duplicated seam column.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Renderer: fix vertically mirrored cluster light grid
commits.message:
Renderer: fix vertically mirrored cluster light grid

NVRHI's Vulkan backend uses a negative-height (D3D-convention) viewport,
so NDC y=+1 is pixel row 0. ClusterBuild built cluster rows bottom-up
while SetupClusterLights looks them up top-down via gl_FragCoord, so
fragments read the light list of the vertically mirrored cluster and
lost lights (far geometry near the top of the screen went unlit).

Flip Y in ClusterBuild's pixel->NDC mapping, and document the viewport
convention in Rendering.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Renderer: count every segment of a split frame in the GPU frame time
commits.message:
Renderer: count every segment of a split frame in the GPU frame time

The WorldOverlay2D pass ends, submits and re-begins the scene command
buffer every frame. RT_Begin reset the single frame-level timer query on
each Begin, so GetExecutionGPUTime (viewport HUD "GPU", and the input to
dynamic resolution) covered only the tail after the overlay: ~0.5 ms
against ~6 ms of per-pass GPU work.

Begin(continueFrame) now resumes a frame: each segment gets its own
timer query per frame index, and the published time is their sum once
all have resolved. Verified in the benchmark scene: frame total ~8.0 ms
against a per-pass sum of ~7.8 ms.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Renderer: rebuild each material once per render-scene sync
commits.message:
Renderer: rebuild each material once per render-scene sync

MaterialScene::UpsertMaterial rebuilt a material's GPU data on every
call, and it is called once per referencing submesh. In the benchmark
scene (7k meshes sharing 128 materials) that meant ~55 rebuilds per
material per frame, each validating every texture through the editor
asset manager (with wstring path copies) - 47% of the main thread.

A material's data cannot change within one sync, so return the existing
ID when it was already touched this frame. Benchmark edit mode, Release:
~51 ms -> ~18 ms per frame.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Physics2D: fix null-entity crash on first 2D contact
commits.message:
Physics2D: fix null-entity crash on first 2D contact

ContactListener2D dereferenced b2Body user data as an Entity*, but

commits.subject: Scene: fix worker crash in parallel static-mesh transform sync

Scene: fix worker crash in parallel static-mesh transform sync

SyncRenderScene's per-item lambda indexed a static thread_local vector.
Lambdas never capture thread_local variables, so on a JobSystem worker the
name resolved to that worker's own empty vector and read garbage once a
scene exceeded the 512-item inline threshold. Bind the caller's vector to
a local reference and capture that.

caller cannot return and destroy the mutex/cv while a worker is about to
notify.

commits.subject: Renderer: bindless material textures through NVRHI descriptor tables
commits.message:
Renderer: bindless material textures through NVRHI descriptor tables

Material textures were a fixed 1024-slot array inside set 2 of every
material pass. Each of the five passes held its own copy, so one texture
change meant five SetInput writes, and a scene could never use more than
1024 textures.

They are now one unsized array, u_GPUMaterialTextures[], at the reserved
descriptor set 4, backed by NVRHI descriptor tables:

- BindlessTextureTable: a process-wide bindless layout (created in
  Renderer::Init before any shader loads) and per-owner tables, one per
  frame in flight. NVRHI's bindless layouts are partially bound but not
  update-after-bind, so the render thread writes a table only when its
  frame comes round; the main thread just records writes. Capacity is
  16384 (MaterialScene.glslh mirrors it), clamped to the device's
  sampled-image limits and logged. Writes are skipped when the image
  handle is unchanged; full sweeps resend so hot-reloaded textures
  update.
- Each SceneRenderer owns a table (the viewport, material preview and
  thumbnailer each have their own texture index space). The material
  passes receive it once, and a texture change is one SetSlot. The
  periodic full sweep covers the slots in use, not the whole table.
- VulkanShader substitutes the shared layout for set 4, and
  RenderPass::GetBindingSets places the current frame's table there when
  the pass's shader declares the set.

Verified on Linux: Debug and Release editor and the runtime build, the
Debug editor rendering FMODDemo under the Vulkan validation layer with
no validation errors, and every material pipeline created against the
new layout. Not yet run on Windows.

commits.subject: Fix shutdown AV and minimize crash in the Vulkan driver
commits.message:
Fix shutdown AV and minimize crash in the Vulkan driver

Shutdown: MaterialAsset's file-scope s_SRGBAlbedoTextureCache held Ref<Texture2D>
past Renderer::Shutdown and the device teardown; the CRT destroyed it at exit and
vkDestroyImage ran against a dead VkDevice (AV in nvoglv64 / vulkan-1, and heap
corruption in the editor). Captured stack: atexit -> s_SRGBAlbedoTextureCache ->
Texture2D -> Image2D::Release -> nvrhi Texture dtor -> nvoglv64. Release it in
Renderer::Shutdown alongside the mip-gen pipeline cache.

Minimize: a 0x0 surface made OnResize destroy the swapchain without creating a new
one, but the render thread still had one frame queued that acquired on it ->
vkAcquireNextImageKHR(VK_NULL_HANDLE) in the driver. Keep the old swapchain while
the surface is 0x0 and retry until restored. Present now skips itself when the
acquire failed, replacing the loop-local frameBeginSuccess that the render-thread
lambdas read by reference after it went out of scope.

commits.subject: Sample: send both events to the Reverb return, driven by ReverbSend

Sample: send both events to the Reverb return, driven by ReverbSend

ReverbSend was present on both events but drove nothing: no event had a
send, so there was no level to automate and the value the engine writes
each frame was discarded.

unmuffled.

local Occlusion and ReverbSend parameters, occlusion automating the EQ
cutoff, and ReverbSend automating the send level.

commits.subject: Renderer: cutout alpha mode (material editor phase 3b)
commits.message:
Renderer: cutout alpha mode (material editor phase 3b)

Phase 3a landed the Lux Standard surface inputs but left alpha unfinished:
MaterialScene wrote a hardcoded 0.5 cutoff with a comment saying cutout
would arrive with the alpha-mode work, and nothing could select Masked -
the GPU alpha mode was only ever `transparent ? Blend : Opaque`.

  - MaterialSurfaceParameters gains AlphaMode (Opaque/Cutout/Blend),
    AlphaThreshold and TwoSided. Defaults reproduce existing shading, so a
    .lmat without these keys renders unchanged; the serializer writes them
    only when non-default and reads missing keys as the default.
  - MaterialScene resolves the authored mode into the material row and
    writes the real threshold into Surface.z. A transparent asset stays
    Blend; authored Blend on a non-transparent asset resolves to Opaque,
    because such a material is not in the sorted forward pass and reporting
    Blend would describe a mode the frame never runs.
  - GetGPUMaterialAlphaCutoff in MaterialScene.glslh, with a fallback for an
    unusable row so a missing material cannot discard a whole mesh. All four
    PBR shaders now read it; two were hardcoding 0.5.
  - PreDepth alpha-tests cutout materials. It previously had an empty
    fragment shader, so cutout geometry punched full depth and occluded
    whatever was behind the transparent parts of the texture. The pass now
    binds the material table, its bindless textures and RendererData -
    explicitly rather than through BindSceneRenderPassInputs, which would
    also rebind ObjectIndexes to the visible set when pre-depth needs the
    unculled one. GetMaterialMipBias is duplicated verbatim from
    GBuffer_Static: if the two passes sample different mips they discard
    different fragments and the G-buffer fails its depth-equal test.
  - PreDepth joins the passes whose bindless texture array is re-bound as
    textures stream in; without that it would keep the white placeholder and
    never discard.

Two-sided is authored, serialized and reaches GPUMaterialFlags::TwoSided,
but nothing consumes that flag yet, so no editor control is offered for it.
Honouring it needs a second render pass and pipeline per cull mode for the
G-buffer and pre-depth, since RT_DrawStaticMesh never sets gs.pipeline and
every draw in a pass inherits the pass's one. Shadow cascades already render
without culling to avoid peter-panning, so they need no bucket.

Verified: Core and Editor build clean in release; editor runs to the render
loop with no shader compile errors, no Vulkan validation errors and no
crash. Not visually verified - a cutout texture on a plant or fence mesh
still needs a look.

Known gap: PreDepth_Meshlet does not alpha-test, so with mesh shaders
enabled cutout geometry still writes full depth.

The surface and dialogue table serializers cap their YAML at 1 MiB and 8 MiB
and enforce it at four separate boundaries — editor save, loose-file load,
asset-pack write and asset-pack read — but none of that was written down.

commits.subject: Relicense from GPL-3.0 to Apache-2.0
commits.message:
Relicense from GPL-3.0 to Apache-2.0

GPL-3.0 was the wrong license for this project. It is viral across linking,
so any game shipped against Lux-Runtime would have to publish its source —
which contradicts the goal of being a usable 3D engine. It also conflicts
with the engine's own hard dependencies: premake now calls ValidateAudioSDK()
unconditionally, so building requires linking the proprietary FMOD and
Vercidium Audio SDKs, and a GPL-3.0 combined work cannot license those.

Apache-2.0 matches Hazel upstream, which this engine descends from and which
16 files still credit, and it adds an explicit patent grant.

  - LICENSE: canonical Apache-2.0 text.
  - NOTICE: new. Credits the Hazel lineage, the 26 permissively licensed
    components vendored in Core/vendor, the proprietary redistributables that
    are tracked here (NVIDIA Aftermath, Discord Social SDK), and the
    build-time SDKs that are not (FMOD, VA, Vulkan SDK). This attribution
    was owed under the previous license too and was not being met.
  - SPDX headers on 487 first-party sources. The 17 files carrying a
    third-party copyright are deliberately untouched.

Verified: Core and Editor both build clean in release.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Fix FMOD update failing every frame with Live Update; close leaked ImGui headers
commits.message:
Fix FMOD update failing every frame with Live Update; close leaked ImGui headers

AudioPerformance enabled input metering on the head DSP of Studio's bus
channel groups. With FMOD Live Update on (the sample project's setting),
changing metering on a Studio-owned DSP makes every later
Studio::System::update return FMOD_ERR_BADCOMMAND. The engine only logs
when the result changes, so it appeared once while failing every frame.
Found by bisecting on Windows; failures stop with the metering call

commits.subject: Fix GPU reset and Vulkan sync hazards in deferred lighting
commits.message:
Fix GPU reset and Vulkan sync hazards in deferred lighting

The editor reset the GPU under the sample scene. Four separate defects,
each verified with the Khronos validation layer and sync validation on:

- Tone mapping bound PreDepth as a colour+depth attachment while also
  sampling it. Give SceneComposite a colour-only framebuffer sharing the
  composite image; the depth-bearing framebuffer stays the target for
  world/editor overlays. Drops the suppressed PreDepth layout VUIDs in
  Window.cpp, which were masking this.
- Compute-to-draw barriers took StorageBuffer from main-thread Get(),
  which can select a different frame's buffer than the recorded draw
  uses. Add StorageBufferSet overloads that resolve RT_Get() at record
  time, and map IndirectCommandRead to nvrhi IndirectArgument so the
  indirect-draw barrier transitions to the right state.
- Mesh-culling outputs (VisibleObjectIndexes, IndirectDrawCommands) were
  CPU-visible; NVRHI skips state transitions for those, so the barriers
  above were no-ops. Make them GPUOnly - CPU init already goes through
  writeBuffer.
- PCSS indexed the 64-entry Poisson table dynamically, which RADV expands
  into per-fragment scratch copies and hangs the deferred lighting draw.
  Use constant-index lookups; tests/rendering/run_shadow_shader.py
  compiles the shader and fails if the local tables come back.

Also drops the unused u_SceneColor binding from DeferredLighting, which
caused a further invalid transition of the pass's own colour output.

Verified: Debug editor, sample scene, PCSS soft shadows, grid and entity
icons on - no validation errors, no SYNC-HAZARD, no GPU reset over a
multi-minute run, clean shutdown. Debug and Release build Core, Editor
and Lux-Runtime.

commits.subject: Renderer: depth-tested collider pass, and point-sampled selection outlines
commits.message:
Renderer: depth-tested collider pass, and point-sampled selection outlines

Physics colliders previously drew through the selection wireframe pass, which
has depth testing off so selection stays visible through geometry. Colliders
inherited that and floated in front of the walls containing them. They now
have their own pass with depth testing on and depth writes off, reusing the
pre-depth output; the on-top behaviour is still available through the
existing Show Physics Colliders On Top option, which routes back to the
wireframe pass. The render graph declares the collider depth read so the
dependency is real rather than incidental.

Grid and wireframe pipelines gain BackfaceCulling off and DepthWrite off,
which is what those passes actually want - they overlay rather than
contribute occlusion.

Selection outlines sample the jump-flood mask and distance buffers with a
point sampler instead of a linear one. Those textures hold mask classes and
distance vectors, not colour: interpolating them blends values across the
selection boundary, which is meaningless and shows up as a frayed outline.
The composite's alpha ramp is inverted to match, so the edge falls off
outward.

The jump-flood ping-pong reuses one pass across iterations, so its input is
now bound inside the render queue rather than at record time - otherwise the
first draw of an iteration can observe the previous iteration's binding.

commits.subject: Audio: bank-aware event picking, and a source that only owns what it should
commits.message:
Audio: bank-aware event picking, and a source that only owns what it should

Two related passes over AudioSourceComponent.

Picking an event
----------------
Events now record which bank describes them, captured during enumeration -
the only place that relationship is known without asking FMOD again. The
inspector picker becomes two stages, bank then event, with a search inside
the dropdown, because one flat list is fine for five events and unusable for
five hundred. Strings banks are excluded from the bank list: they carry the
path table rather than events, so they would offer a permanently empty list.

The bank is stored on the component as a hint, exactly like the event path -
refreshed from the loaded banks on display and never used to resolve. The
GUID still resolves the event on its own, whichever bank it turns out to live
in. Filter and search state live on the panel rather than the component,
since they are a view preference, not something to serialize into scenes.

Trimming the component
----------------------
AudioSourceConfig carried fifteen fields, most of which an FMOD Studio event
now owns. Keeping them was worse than useless: visible, editable, and
silently ignored the moment an event was assigned. Removed Spatialization,
AttenuationModel, RollOff, Min/MaxGain, Min/MaxDistance, the three cone
angles and DopplerFactor, along with the AttenuationModelType enum and the
setters that fed them. What remains is volume, pitch, play-on-awake, and
looping for the legacy path.

The playlist goes with them - AudioData, the four component helpers, its
runtime storage and about forty-five lines of index juggling in Scene. A
multi-instrument does the same job in Studio, with weighting and no-repeat.
Removing the struct also exposed an OnComponentAdded<AudioData>
specialization that had always been dead, since AudioData was never a
component.

In their place, ParameterOverrides: name/value pairs applied once when the
instance is created, so two entities can share one event and still sound
different. Scripts will drive parameters continuously through the C# API;
these are the authored starting point.

Behaviour changes worth knowing
-------------------------------
Spatialization defaulted to false, which quietly made every raw source 2D
unless someone ticked it. The legacy path is now always 3D with FMOD's
default rolloff - tuning raw-file attenuation is precisely what an event
should be doing instead.

Old scenes still carry the removed keys. The deserializer ignores them
deliberately, with the reason recorded: reading them would resurrect settings
that no longer reach the mixer. Scenes keep playing, with default attenuation
rather than whatever was tuned in the component.

Paused now defaults to true so play-on-awake fires once for events. That
required OnRuntimeStart to clear it when it starts a raw source - otherwise
the per-frame path stays armed and restarts the source every time it
finishes, turning a one-shot into an unintended loop.

commits.subject: Audio: play FMOD Studio events from AudioSourceComponent
commits.message:
Audio: play FMOD Studio events from AudioSourceComponent

Sources can now reference an authored FMOD Studio event instead of a raw
audio file. When an event is set it supersedes the file: spatialisation,
attenuation, cones, doppler and randomisation are authored in the event, and
the component's config fields for those no longer apply.

Events are referenced by GUID, not by path. The path is stored alongside it
purely as a label and is refreshed from the loaded banks on display - never
used to resolve. Renaming or moving an event in FMOD Studio changes its path
but not its GUID, so a path-referencing scene would go silently mute the
first time a designer reorganises the project, with no error anywhere.

AudioEventInstance wraps FMOD::Studio::EventInstance. Two details worth
knowing: IsPlaying counts SUSTAINING, because an event holding at a sustain
point is audible even though its state is neither STARTING nor PLAYING; and
the destructor stops IMMEDIATE rather than ALLOWFADEOUT, because it runs
during teardown where a fade would outlive the thing being torn down.

Scene owns instances per entity. A null entry in that map is meaningful - it
records an event that could not be resolved, so the "not in any loaded bank"
warning is logged once rather than on every frame. Instances are released
both per entity and with the runtime, since they hold Studio resources.

Ray-traced acoustics reach events as named parameters (Occlusion,
ReverbSend) rather than as a filter applied by the engine. That is the
philosophical difference between the two paths: on the legacy path the
engine decides what occlusion does to a sound, while an event is told what
was measured and its author decides what it means. An event declaring
neither parameter is simply unaffected.

The inspector gains an event picker listing what the loaded banks describe,
with the GUID and 3D/oneshot shown on hover. An assigned event missing from
the loaded banks is flagged rather than reading as "nothing assigned".

The legacy raw-file path is retained and marked as such. The project's
.fspro has no authored sounds yet, so removing it now would leave the engine
playing nothing at all.

Verified end to end: a 3D event authored through fmodstudiocl's scripting
API and built into the master bank is enumerated by the engine on project
open ("Loaded 2 bank(s) describing 1 event(s)"), which exercises bank
enumeration, GUID formatting and the list the picker and serializer share.

Note for anyone adding to this: AudioEventInstance.cpp is a new translation
unit, so the projects need regenerating - and regeneration drops the
--fmod / --raytraced-audio options, which must be passed again.

commits.subject: Audio: VA acoustics at full output, 3D debug view, FMOD Studio pipeline
commits.message:
Audio: VA acoustics at full output, 3D debug view, FMOD Studio pipeline

Three strands of work on the audio stack.

Ray-traced acoustics (Vercidium)
--------------------------------
Rebuilt to the topology Vercidium's docs describe: the listener is the only
ray caster, casting all five ray types (including the ambient pair we were
leaving at zero), and every source is registered as one of its targets.
Adding a source now costs a target on the listener's existing ray budget
rather than a second budget of its own.

The simulation's full EAX/I3DL2 reverb set is read (vaEmitterGetEAX) and
mapped onto FMOD_REVERB_PROPERTIES - previously one field of ~25 was used.
Every value is clamped to FMOD's documented range because FMOD rejects the
whole struct if one field is out, silently keeping the old reverb.

Occlusion is applied as two bands rather than one scalar: the low-frequency
gain scales the channel's volume (how much gets through) and the relative
high-frequency loss drives the occlusion filter (how much more the highs are
cut). Feeding HF straight into set3DOcclusion double-counts the loss and
makes an occluded source inaudible instead of muffled.

The frame is now explicitly two-phase - WaitForResults, then mutate and read,
then OnUpdate - because the simulation is asynchronous and results were being
read while workers were still writing them. Stop() also waits unconditionally
before draining: vaWorldGetThreadsRunning reads false for work that has been
queued but not started, which skipped the drain entirely.

Measured end to end: reverb decay tracks room size (0.10s open field, 0.32s
small room, 1.39s large hall) and reaches FMOD accepted. Occlusion does not
respond to geometry at all - a Vercidium defect, with a self-contained repro
under docs/vercidium-repro/ that includes reverb from the same emitter as a
control, proving the rays do reach the geometry.

3D visualisation and the Audio Debugger
---------------------------------------
Visualisation rays are delivered on Vercidium's worker threads and are valid
only inside the callback, so they are copied out under a lock and copied
again by the renderer. A ray that hits nothing still occupies its slot,
filled with a far out-of-world sentinel, so bounces are classified by world
containment and each polyline stops at its first miss.

New AudioDebugPanel (View -> Audio Debugger) renders both halves of the
stack, with the reverb the simulation produced and the values FMOD actually
received side by side. Deliberately free of LUX_ENABLE_FMOD /
LUX_ENABLE_RAYTRACED_AUDIO, which are Core-only defines: each backend names
itself through its stats struct instead.

FMOD Studio pipeline
--------------------
Studio is linked alongside Core and owns it - Studio::System::initialize
creates the core system, so Shutdown releases only Studio (releasing both is
a double free) and Update calls Studio then Core. Studio's update does NOT
recompute Core's 3D attenuation; measured with Channel::getAudibility, Studio
alone leaves audibility frozen at the geometry a channel started with, which
is indistinguishable from spatialisation being off.

AudioBankBuilder shells out to fmodstudiocl the way ScriptBuilder shells out
to dotnet, and is not behind LUX_ENABLE_FMOD - building banks needs the
Studio application, not the SDK. Banks rebuild on Play when the .fspro is
newer, and load strings-bank-first (it carries the path table; loading it
late makes every event lookup fail unhelpfully).

.fspro and .bank are asset types so the Content Browser can show and activate
them - activation opens FMOD Studio. Both the browser and the asset registry
treat a Studio project directory as opaque: it is dozens of GUID-named XML
files plus gitignored build output, and importing the banks would put
regenerable files into the tracked registry.

Known gap: the binary runtime project format does not carry the Studio
settings and runtime export does not copy banks, so an exported game ships
without audio. That belongs with the runtime export work.

commits.subject: Audio: FMOD playback backend + Vercidium ray-traced acoustics (both opt-in)
commits.message:
Audio: FMOD playback backend + Vercidium ray-traced acoustics (both opt-in)

Adds two independent, opt-in audio subsystems and fixes several latent bugs
found while wiring them up.

WHAT

- FMOD Engine as an alternative playback backend (--fmod, LUX_ENABLE_FMOD).
  AudioEngine/AudioSource/AudioListener now compile against either miniaudio
  (default) or FMOD Core, selected by #ifdef within each .cpp, so call sites
  never see the backend and the default build has no FMOD dependency.
  AudioEngine::Update() pumps FMOD::System::update() once per frame from
  Application::Run; it is a no-op under miniaudio.

- RaytracedAudioScene (--raytraced-audio, LUX_ENABLE_RAYTRACED_AUDIO): wraps
  the Vercidium Audio SDK behind a Pimpl. One VAWorld per Scene, created on
  OnRuntimeStart, mirroring static MeshCollider geometry and tracking one
  emitter per AudioSourceComponent. Its per-source occlusion/reverb results
  feed FMOD's Channel::set3DOcclusion / setReverbProperties. Built without
  the SDK every method is a no-op, matching the DiscordSocial pattern.

Both SDKs are proprietary and gitignored; their EULAs forbid redistributing
the SDK itself, so they are fetched manually. Configure.py warns when a
feature is enabled without its SDK present.

BUGS FIXED ALONG THE WAY

- AudioSourceComponent/AudioListenerComponent were never serialized, and a
  legacy-schema guard hard-rejected any scene containing them. Both now
  round-trip through SceneSerializer.
- The same two components were missing from AllComponents/DuplicateComponents,
  so Scene::Copy silently dropped them on Play - audio could never work at
  runtime regardless of backend.
- AttenuationModel was emitted as uint8_t; yaml-cpp writes unsigned char as a
  *character*, so saving a scene with an audio source wrote a raw control byte
  and corrupted the .luxscene. Now uint32_t both directions.
- VA emitters default to zero rays of every type, so sources produced no
  occlusion or reverb at all. Ray counts are now set explicitly.
- GetResult() segfaulted inside the SDK when querying an emitter created in
  the same frame, before its first vaWorldUpdate. Now guarded.
- Stop() destroyed emitters the world still owned pending their reverb tail
  (vaWorldRemoveEmitter answers VA_PENDING_REMOVAL), double-freeing them in
  vaWorldDestroy. Teardown now only destroys what it actually removed.
- Linux-Build.sh regenerated makefiles without the feature flags, silently
  producing a build with the features compiled out. It now forwards
  LUX_PREMAKE_OPTIONS.

VERIFICATION

Core, Editor and Lux-Runtime all build clean with --fmod --raytraced-audio.
FMOD initialises against a real device; scene loads; VA world creation and
static-geometry mirroring verified correct in-editor (mirrored AABB matches
the source transform exactly); per-emitter results reach the playback layer
(Valid=true). Every VA and FMOD call site was additionally compiled against
the real vendored headers in standalone harnesses.

KNOWN ISSUES - --raytraced-audio should stay OFF by default

- Creating a VAWorld inside the engine process corrupts the heap on Play.
  Isolated: FMOD-only is clean, and the identical VA calls are clean in a
  standalone harness, so it is an interaction, root cause not yet found.
- VA occlusion output does not respond to geometry (identical values with no
  wall and with a 100x75m wall), reproducible standalone. Open with Vercidium.
- Windows FMOD paths in Dependencies.lua are unverified placeholders; only the
  Linux package has been fetched.
- Static geometry is mirrored once at Play start and does not follow moving
  colliders; all geometry is hardcoded to VAMaterialConcrete.

Requires project regeneration (new files + premake changes).

commits.subject: Fix shutdown segfault: release assets before the device, leak live-ref registry
commits.message:
Fix shutdown segfault: release assets before the device, leak live-ref registry

On exit (File > Exit / SIGTERM), the editor segfaulted while destroying GPU resources.
Root cause was a static-destruction-order fiasco: Project::s_AssetManager is an inline
static Ref that outlives Application shutdown, so its cached scenes' Vulkan resources
(IndexBuffer, etc.) were freed at program exit — after the device was already gone.

Two fixes:
- EditorLayer::OnDetach now calls Project::SetActive(nullptr), which runs the asset
  manager's Shutdown() and drops the static Ref while the Vulkan device is still alive.
- RefUtils' live-reference registry (Ref.cpp) is now an intentionally-leaked, construct-
  on-first-use singleton, so it outlives every static Ref and RemoveFromLiveReferences()
  can never erase() into a freed hash table (the deeper latent cause of the same crash).

commits.subject: Fix double titlebar on Wayland by disabling libdecor
commits.message:
Fix double titlebar on Wayland by disabling libdecor

On Wayland, GLFW prefers libdecor for client-side decorations whenever
it is installed. libdecor draws its own titlebar and does not honour
set_visibility(false) for our undecorated window on KWin, so its header
rendered on top of the editor's custom titlebar. Disable libdecor via
glfwInitHint before glfwInit so GLFW uses the native xdg-decoration
protocol instead: the undecorated window requests CLIENT_SIDE and KWin
draws no server titlebar of its own. The hint is Wayland-only and ignored
on Windows/X11.

commits.subject: Fix Vulkan depth format and a mistyped-ternary crash in SceneRenderer
commits.message:
Fix Vulkan depth format and a mistyped-ternary crash in SceneRenderer

ImageFormat::Depth aliased DEPTH24STENCIL8, which maps to Vulkan's
VK_FORMAT_D24_UNORM_S8_UINT. That format is optional in the spec and
unsupported on Mesa RADV/ANV (AMD/Intel), so every shadow map and G-buffer
depth attachment failed to create (VK_ERROR_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED) on those
drivers, leaving nothing depth-tested able to draw. Alias to
DEPTH32FSTENCIL8UINT instead, which is the format the device's own
FindDepthFormat() probe already prefers.

Separately, CreatePreConvolutionPassMaterials() passed a ternary mixing
Ref<Image2D> and Ref<ImageView> — two unrelated types — into Material::Set.
Ref<T> only defines operator bool(), so the compiler silently unified the
ternary through that instead of failing to compile, turning the texture
argument into `true` and asserting "Could not find uniform 'u_Input'"
whenever SSR is enabled. Split into an if/else so each branch keeps its
real type and hits the correct Material::Set overload.

commits.subject: Version-control the asset registry and generated materials
commits.message:
Version-control the asset registry and generated materials

AssetHandle is a random UUID assigned at import time, and AssetRegistry.lzr
is the only record of which handle maps to which file path. It was
gitignored (along with the mesh importer's auto-generated *.lmat files), so
a fresh clone re-imports every asset with brand-new random handles that
don't match the AssetID references baked into committed .luxscene files —
meshes and textures silently fail to resolve on any machine other than the
one that first imported them.

Track the registry and the sample project's generated materials so asset
identity is stable across clones/machines, matching how scenes and source
textures are already versioned.

commits.subject: Order the mesh-culling instance-count reset against its atomics
commits.message:
Order the mesh-culling instance-count reset against its atomics

MeshCulling.glsl zeroes the indirect draw's instanceCount from invocation 0
with a plain store, then relies on barrier() before all 64 invocations
atomicAdd that same address.

barrier() synchronises execution and, in a compute shader, implies a memory
barrier for SHARED variables only. b_IndirectDrawCommands is a plain
(non-coherent) SSBO, so the store is not ordered against the atomics. When
the reset lands after other invocations have already incremented, their
counts are discarded and instanceCount ends up lower than the number of
visible object indices actually written - the draw silently renders fewer
instances than were culled in. Being a race, which invocations lose varies
per frame, so geometry flickers as the visible set churns.

Adds the missing memoryBarrierBuffer().

Found while investigating geometry popping, but almost certainly NOT the
cause of that report: this races every frame, whereas the reported artifact
only appears immediately after the editor window regains focus. Committed
separately for that reason - it is an independent correctness fix, and the
focus-triggered artifact is still unexplained.

Verified: shader recompiles and the MeshCulling compute pipeline builds
clean. Shader only - no C++, no new files, so no rebuild or project
regeneration. Not visually verified: the fix only removes lost atomic
increments, so it can add instances back to a draw, never remove them.

commits.subject: Drive GTAO sample counts from the AO quality tier
commits.message:
Drive GTAO sample counts from the AO quality tier

SliceCount = 9 and StepsPerSlice = 3 were struct defaults that nothing ever
assigned. That is XeGTAO's Ultra preset - 9 * 3 * 2 = 54 depth samples per
pixel - and it ran identically at Low, Medium, High, Ultra and Cinematic.
The quality tier adjusted denoise passes and resolution but never touched
the pass's dominant cost, so GTAO was the same price at every setting.

ApplyAmbientOcclusionQuality now sets both, using XeGTAO's own preset
values: Low 1/2, Medium 2/2, High 3/3, Ultra 9/3, Cinematic 9/3. The two
constant-buffer fields already existed on both the C++ and HLSL sides, so
no shader change is involved - they simply start being written.

Wiring the tier alone was not enough, and measuring caught it: Cinematic
1.696 ms vs High 1.709 ms, no change. On project load the tier is only a
label (see the legacy-path comment in DeserializeRendererSettings) and the
raw serialized values are what take effect, so an unserialized field falls
back to its default every launch. The counts are therefore serialized like
every other resolved quality value: YAML both directions, plus the binary
pack behind a version bump 15 -> 16. The guarded read sits between
GTAODenoisePasses and AOShadowTolerance, mirroring the write exactly, so a
v15 pack skips the two fields and resumes at the correct offset instead of
shifting every subsequent field by 8 bytes. Values are clamped on load
(slices 1-9, steps 1-4).

Measured with the Tracy GPU zones, isolating slice count by holding
everything else at Cinematic (bent normals on, full resolution, 8 denoise
passes): GTAO 1.696 ms -> 0.579 ms at 3 slices, a 2.93x reduction against a
predicted 3x. GTAO-Denoise measured 0.711 ms in both runs, identical to
three decimals, which confirms the two captures are comparable and that
only GTAO changed.

LuxSample.luxproj keeps 9/3, matching the Cinematic mapping, so behaviour
is unchanged until a tier is chosen - dropping to 3 slices is a visible
quality trade, not a free win.

Verified: Debug and Release build clean. No files added or removed, so no
project regeneration required.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Bound the DOF gather radius per pixel instead of always to MAX_BLUR_SIZE
commits.message:
Bound the DOF gather radius per pixel instead of always to MAX_BLUR_SIZE

DOF was the most expensive pass in the frame at 3.13 ms of ~7.6 ms, and
almost all of it was work that provably changed nothing.

The gather always ran until radius reached MAX_BLUR_SIZE - roughly 200
iterations at two texture fetches each - but a sample only contributes
through smoothstep(radius - 0.5, radius + 0.5, sampleSize). Once no
reachable surface has a blur radius above the current one, every remaining
iteration has m == 0, and "color += mix(color / tot, sampleColor, 0)"
degenerates to re-adding the running average: the result is unchanged
while still paying both fetches. With a typical focus setup that is the
large majority of the loop. At FocusDistance 5.1 / BlurSize 0.6 a
background pixel at infinity has a blur radius of about 2.4 px, so the
loop spent ~195 of 200 iterations producing nothing.

ComputeSearchRadius now bounds the loop per pixel:

- Behind the centre the bound is exact, not an approximation. Those
  samples are already clamped to centerSize * 2 in the gather, so nothing
  past centerSize * 2 + 0.5 can contribute; the bound uses + 1.0 and is
  strictly conservative. No image change from this half.
- In front, samples are deliberately unclamped - that is what lets a
  blurry foreground bleed over a sharp background - so they can still
  reach in from the full radius. Twelve depth-only taps across two rings
  probe for them instead of paying for the whole gather.
- When the background bound already saturates at MAX_BLUR_SIZE the probe
  cannot raise it and is skipped, so heavily blurred pixels (which still
  pay the full gather) do not carry the taps as overhead.

Weighting and accumulation for contributing samples are untouched; only
provably zero-weight iterations are removed.

The foreground probe is a heuristic: a blurry foreground thinner than the
ring spacing (10 px and 20 px) can lose its bleed halo. FOREGROUND_PROBE_RINGS
is the knob if that shows up; the alternative is a max-CoC tile prepass.

Measured with the Tracy GPU zones: DOF 3.127 ms -> 0.324 ms, a 9.6x
improvement, dropping it from the most expensive pass to sixth. Untouched
passes in the same capture serve as the control - GTAO 1.424 -> 1.308,
GTAO-Denoise 0.622 -> 0.621 - so the DOF/GTAO ratio moved 2.20 -> 0.25,
which rules out a GPU clock or environment artifact. Shader recompilation
was confirmed from the cache timestamps rather than assumed.

Shader only: no C++, no new files, so no rebuild or project regeneration.
Visual verification of foreground bleed is still outstanding.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Add frame-rate limit, present mode, and swapchain image count settings
commits.message:
Add frame-rate limit, present mode, and swapchain image count settings

The editor was pinned to 120 fps regardless of render settings, which no
amount of lowering quality would move. It was never a GPU cost: MAILBOX on
a composited (windowed/DWM) surface still releases images on the
compositor's schedule, so the frame rate tracks the display - measured at
refresh (60) while focused and ~(images-1) x refresh (120) while
unfocused. IMMEDIATE is the only present mode the spec guarantees will not
block on vblank, and is confirmed uncapped here.

Three new editor settings, all persisted in App.lsettings:

- Frame Rate Limit: Unlimited / 60 / 120 / 165 / 240 / 360 / 720 / Custom,
  with a 30-1000 slider for Custom. Disabled under VSync, where the display
  already paces the loop.
- Present Mode: Mailbox (no tearing) or Immediate (uncapped, may tear).
  Exposed rather than hard-coded because neither is unconditionally better
  and the winner is driver- and compositor-dependent.
- Swapchain Images: 2-5. Under MAILBOX this is what sets the ceiling.

Pacing is Application::SetTargetFrameRate, a deadline-carried sleep-then-
spin in the main loop. The deadline is carried between frames rather than
recomputed from "now", so per-frame oversleep cannot accumulate into rate
drift, and it resyncs after a hitch instead of running flat out to catch up
on frames already gone. The spin margin is capped at a quarter of the frame
so the high presets do not peg a core in the yield loop - a flat 1.2 ms
would be longer than a whole frame at the 1000 fps slider maximum.

All three settings are read when the swapchain is built, so they are
applied together on one recreate in Window::ProcessEvents, at the existing
point where both threads are idle. They are routinely changed as a group
(ApplyEditorPreferences pushes all of them), and a recreate rebuilds every
swapchain image and framebuffer, so one per setting would triple that cost.

Rendering.md documents the present-mode behaviour, including that a frame
rate pinned to the refresh rate or a clean multiple of it is a presentation
ceiling rather than a render cost, and that window focus changes the result
by 2x - which makes any benchmark of a script-launched (unfocused) window
non-comparable to a focused session.

Verified: Debug and Release build clean; Immediate confirmed uncapped in a
focused session; the present-mode setting confirmed to flip the swapchain
in both directions via the creation log; the coalesced recreate confirmed
to drop from two per launch to one. No files added or removed, so no
project regeneration required.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Add Tracy GPU zones for every profiled render pass
commits.message:
Add Tracy GPU zones for every profiled render pass

Tracy captures previously contained CPU zones only - the engine never
created a Vulkan GPU context - so a capture could show where the frame
went on the CPU but was blind to the GPU, which is where this renderer is
actually bound.

VulkanDeviceManager now owns a TracyVkCtx, created at the end of
CreateDevice and destroyed in DestroyDevice before vkDestroyDevice. It
gets a dedicated command pool because Tracy records, submits, and
vkQueueWaitIdles that buffer itself during clock calibration, so it
cannot share anything nvrhi tracks. Creation is best-effort and every
consumer tolerates a null context.

Zones are emitted from RenderCommandBuffer::RT_BeginTimerQuery /
RT_EndTimerQuery - the pair Renderer::BeginGPUPerfMarker and
SceneRenderer::BeginProfiledGPU already funnel through - so all profiled
passes are instrumented without touching SceneRenderer. TracyVkCollect
runs in RT_End, outside any render pass and before close().

Zone lifetime is the sharp edge: ~VkCtxScope issues a vkCmdWriteTimestamp,
so a zone must never outlive its command buffer's recording state. RT_End
force-closes any zone left open by a begin/end mismatch, while the buffer
is still recording.

TracyVulkan.hpp is included only in these two Vulkan-aware headers,
deliberately not in Debug/Profiler.h, which reaches nearly every
translation unit through the PCH. The whole path compiles out in Dist and
is inert until a profiler connects (TRACY_ON_DEMAND).

First result from the new data: DOF costs 3.13 ms of a ~7.6 ms frame at
2564x1506, more than any other pass by a wide margin. GTAO-Denoise, which
looked expensive by inspection (8 serialized full-resolution dispatches),
is only 0.62 ms.

Verified: Debug and Release build clean. Captured with tracy-capture and
exported with tracy-csvexport -g - 49,486 GPU zone events across 17
passes, no mismatch warnings, no validation errors. Instrumentation only;
no files added or removed, so no project regeneration required.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Fix cross-thread indexing in renderer GPU instrumentation
commits.message:
Fix cross-thread indexing in renderer GPU instrumentation

Frame-level GPU time and pipeline statistics were written on the render
thread indexed by Renderer::RT_GetCurrentFrameIndex() (the swapchain
back-buffer index) but read on the main thread indexed by
Renderer::GetCurrentFrameIndex() (Application::m_CurrentFrameIndex).
Those are unrelated sequences with different periods, and under
VK_PRESENT_MODE_MAILBOX_KHR the acquired back-buffer index is not even
monotonic, so readers picked up a foreign slot.

Publish both as single latest values instead, mirroring
m_NamedTimerQueryResults which is keyed by name only and has always
reported correctly for this reason. Both are atomic, so the render-thread
write and main-thread read are no longer a data race.

Also gate the pipeline-statistics store on vk::Result::eSuccess.
vkGetQueryPoolResults leaves the destination untouched on eNotReady, so
storing unconditionally would publish zeros over a good sample.

The viewport HUD summed MainThreadWorkTime + RenderThreadWorkTime, which
double-counts under MultiThreaded where the two overlap - it made the HUD
contradict its own frame time. It now takes the max there, and still sums
under SingleThreaded where the render work runs inline and the spans are
sequential.

Known remaining issue, separate cause: "Scene GPU Command Buffer" still
reads ~0.01 ms. The WorldOverlay2D pass ends and re-begins the command
buffer mid-frame (SceneRenderer.cpp), which resets and restarts the same
frame-level timer query, so only the tail segment is ever measured. Fixing
that needs per-segment queries plus a frame-boundary signal. "Profiled GPU
Pass Sum" is unaffected and remains the correct GPU figure.

Verified: Debug solution builds clean (0 errors, 1 pre-existing warning),
confirmed by artifact timestamp; editor launched and the HUD confirmed
reporting max() rather than sum. Instrumentation only - no files added or
removed, so no project regeneration required.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Replace render volumes with scene-wide post-process settings
commits.message:
Replace render volumes with scene-wide post-process settings

Removes the spatial render-volume system and relocates what it carried, rather
than deleting it: the volumes were only an override layer, but they were the
sole home for exposure mode, physical camera, auto-exposure, colour grading and
tonemap. Dropping them outright would have frozen all of that at struct
defaults with no way to author it.

Deleted: RenderVolumeShape, the 27-flag override enum, RenderVolumeComponent
(unbound / blend distance / blend weight / priority / debug colour),
PostProcessVolumeComponent, RenderVolumeBaseSettings, RenderVolumeEnvironment,
RenderVolumeEvaluationInput and RenderVolumeEvaluator - proximity weighting,
priority sorting, per-property blending and the self-tests - plus all of
RenderVolumes.cpp. Editor side: the volume gizmos, the "Show Render Volumes"
toggle and its persisted setting, the Volumes create menu, the add-component
rows and the debugger's volume counters.

Relocated: RenderVolumePostProcessSettings becomes PostProcessSettings in its
own header, owned by Scene, serialized as a scene-level "PostProcess" block, and
edited from a new "Post Processing (Scene)" section in the Scene Renderer panel
(which already owns bloom and DOF). The per-property "Override X" checkboxes are
gone - they only expressed which volume wins, which is meaningless with a single
global set.

Bloom, DOF and exposure still come from renderer state and are overlaid each
frame by GetEffectivePostProcessSettings, which is the same overlay the old
GetBaseRenderVolumeSettings performed, so that path is unchanged.

Scenes written before this load cleanly - unknown YAML keys are ignored, so old
RenderVolumeComponent / PostProcessVolumeComponent blocks are skipped and the
scene starts from PostProcessSettings defaults. Any grading those volumes held
is still readable in the scene YAML if it needs to be carried over by hand.

Requires project regeneration (RenderVolumes.cpp removed, PostProcessSettings.h
added).

Verified: Core and Editor build clean in Debug and Release, no reference to any
removed symbol remains, and the editor was run - post-processing works.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Remove volumetric clouds, height fog and sky atmosphere
commits.message:
Remove volumetric clouds, height fog and sky atmosphere

Deletes the whole atmospheric stack: 10 shaders (SkyAtmosphere, AtmosphericFog,
VolumetricClouds + composite, three CloudNoise bake passes, and the Atmosphere /
FogClusterLights / CloudNoise includes), Atmosphere.h in full, the
SkyAtmosphere / VolumetricCloud / ExponentialHeightFog components, and the
AtmosphereVolume / LocalFogVolume render volumes.

Renderer side: five pass bodies, UBAtmosphere including its 64 local-fog rows,
the shared AtmosphereData UBO at (set 2, binding 3), PassInputAtmosphere and its
place in PassInputFrameUniforms, the graph nodes, the resize/repair sweeps and
the baked 3D cloud-noise volumes. Volume side: the sky/cloud/fog override enums
(54 flags), BlendSky/BlendClouds/BlendFog, and local-fog culling and GPU
packing. Editor side: hierarchy UI, create-entity menus, add-component rows,
debugger stats and the LocalFogDensity debug view.

Skybox and SkyLight IBL are untouched, so scenes keep environment lighting.

None of this had ever executed. Every atmosphere pass and material was declared
but never assigned - zero assignments at 2ba41b22 and three months earlier, and
no CloudNoise bake pipelines appear in a startup log. SceneRenderer.cpp carried a
note saying the creation block had already been cut, leaving roughly 300
references of consumption behind. This finishes that removal rather than
removing a working feature.

Done by hand per file with brace-aware block removal and a grep sweep after each,
rather than the line-pattern scripting that caused the previous crash.

Verified: Core and Editor build clean in Debug and Release; no reference to any
deleted symbol or shader remains; every ShaderLibrary::Load path resolves.
Not yet run.

commits.subject: Fix crash from temporal removal: null names in the profiled-pass array
commits.message:
Fix crash from temporal removal: null names in the profiled-pass array

s_ProfiledSceneRendererPasses was declared std::array<const char*, 30> while
the temporal removal cut it to 28 entries. That is legal C++: the two trailing
elements value-initialise to nullptr. ResetProfilingData assigns every element
as a PassProfile::Name, so two profiles carried a null name, and the next
GetOrCreatePassProfile ran std::strcmp against it - an access violation reading
0x0, surfacing as 0xC0000005 inside ucrtbase with no hint of the real cause.

The size is now deduced via std::to_array so the count cannot drift from the
contents again, which is the actual defect - the hardcoded 30 was a trap that
compiled cleanly and failed only at runtime.

Also fixes SMAAPass leaving the SubsampleIndices push constant uninitialised.
Its initialiser referenced IsSMAATemporalActive() and went out with the
temporal removal, so stack garbage was uploaded and fed to SMAAArea as an
AreaTex subtexture offset. Always zero now - that is the SMAA 1x value.

Material::Set/Get asserts now name the uniform and the material. A bare
"Could not find uniform!" is unactionable, and this class of bug - C++ writing
a member a shader edit silently dropped - is exactly what it should catch.

Verified by running the editor: previously faulted within ~30s of launch,
now runs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Remove all temporal rendering; add per-category quality tiers
commits.message:
Remove all temporal rendering; add per-category quality tiers

Two intertwined changes in the same files - the quality appliers were written
and then had their temporal branches stripped, so an intermediate state would
not compile.

Remove temporal rendering entirely
----------------------------------
Deletes TAA, SMAA T2x, GTAO and SSR temporal accumulation, and volumetric cloud
temporal accumulation: five shaders, nine options, ten history images, their
compute passes, graph nodes, dispatches, resize paths, and the Halton jitter.

Every one of these trades ghosting and smearing behind moving geometry for its
performance win, which is not a trade this engine makes. Quality is bought
spatially instead: GTAO High goes from 2 to 4 denoise passes, and SMAA
High/Ultra/Cinematic drop the edge threshold from 0.1 to 0.05.

The volumetric cloud pass was the worst offender - ungated, always on whenever
clouds were enabled, with a hardcoded 0.92 history weight. The composite already
had a fallback to the raw half-res raymarch, which is now the only path.

Four failures here compile cleanly and only appear at runtime, so they are worth
naming: ShaderLibrary::Get is a map::at, so the orphaned "GTAO-Temporal" and
"SSR-Temporal" lookups would have thrown during init (and in Release the
preceding assert compiles out, losing the shader name); the SMAA availability
guard still listed the deleted "SMAA-Resolve" and would have silently disabled
SMAA at startup; and a Load() call survived for a deleted shader. Every Load()
path is now verified to resolve to a real file.

ProjectRuntimeFormat bumps to v15. The binary stream is positional, so pre-v15
packs must read past the removed fields or everything after them misaligns;
the read path does that under a version guard.

PreviousViewProjectionMatrix and the G-buffer velocity target are kept - the
velocity attachment is now written but unread, left in place because it is what
motion blur would need. Jitter/PreviousJitter stay in the Camera UB as permanent
zeros rather than being removed, since that block is set 2 binding 0 in nearly
every shader.

Per-category quality tiers
--------------------------
Replaces the 163-line ApplyQualityPreset monolith with seven appliers owning
disjoint field sets: Shadows, AmbientOcclusion, Reflections, AntiAliasing,
Textures, ResolutionScale, PostProcessing. QualityPreset gains Custom, meaning
"hand-edited, leave alone"; RendererQualityCategories::Unified() reports the
shared tier or Custom when they differ.

Each applier writes every field it owns for every tier, so a tier is fully
described by its own branch. The old baseline+switch shape had a latent bug
here: Low never set DistanceMipBias*, so it inherited whatever ran before it.

This also gives the Cinematic 2K shadow cap an escape hatch - editing the
resolution by hand marks Shadows as Custom, and a Custom category applies
nothing, so the tier stops overwriting the choice.

Not yet done: the per-category tiers are not serialized, so loading still takes
the legacy all-values path (TODO marked at the site). That is what actually
fixes settings being overwritten on load.

Verified: glslc compiles the touched shaders; SSROptionsUB/u_SSRInfo and
CBGTAOData/GTAOConstants edited on both sides; Core and Editor build Debug/x64.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Merge SMAA weight and blend into one compute pass
commits.message:
Merge SMAA weight and blend into one compute pass

Blending-weight calculation and neighbourhood blending were two dispatches
communicating through a full-screen RGBA8 intermediate. They are now one pass:
the weights stay in shared memory and m_SMAABlendImage is gone.

Neighbourhood blending only reads the current pixel's weights plus its right
and bottom neighbours, so an 8x8 group needs a 9x9 tile. Each thread computes
its own pixel and 17 threads compute one apron pixel each (8 down the right
column, 9 along the bottom row), then the group barriers and blends.

This is numerically identical to the two-pass version rather than an
approximation: the four weight fetches the separate pass did through a linear
sampler all landed exactly on texel centres, where bilinear degenerates to a
point fetch.

The bounds test in main() is deliberately placed after barrier(). Testing
first would let edge-of-screen groups return early and leave the rest of the
group waiting on a barrier those threads never reach. Out-of-bounds pixels
instead resolve inside ComputeBlendWeights as zero weights, matching what the
sampler's zero border produced before.

The shader-availability guard in CreateSMAAPasses still listed the two old
shader names; left alone it would have disabled SMAA at startup with only a
warning. Updated to the merged name.

T2x is unaffected - SMAA-Resolve reads m_SMAAOutputImage, which the merged
pass still writes.

Cost of the merge is 81 weight computations per 64 output pixels (~27% more
search/corner work) traded against one full-screen store and load. Not yet
measured; worth a GPU-marker comparison before assuming it is a win.

Verified: glslc --target-env=vulkan1.3 compiles the merged shader, SPIR-V
reflection shows set 1 bindings 0-4 matching the SetInput names; Core and
Editor build Debug/x64.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Convert SMAA to compute passes
commits.message:
Convert SMAA to compute passes

Moves edge detection, blending weights, neighbourhood blending and the T2x
resolve off graphics render passes onto compute passes writing storage images,
matching the existing GTAO/SSR pattern.

The four dispatches are driven from a single SMAAPass() entry point: they are
sequential and share push constants, so splitting them across separate render
graph nodes bought nothing.

Resources are now storage images owned by the renderer -- m_SMAAEdgesImage
(RG8), m_SMAABlendImage (RGBA8), m_SMAAOutputImage (RGBA8), plus a ping-pong
m_SMAAHistoryImages[2] for T2x. When the vendored area/search textures are
absent no SMAA resources are created at all and the renderer reports SMAA
unavailable rather than producing garbage.

commits.subject: Add shared agent guidance docs and workflow skills
commits.message:
Add shared agent guidance docs and workflow skills

Replaces the previous generic AGENTS.md advice with source-grounded guidance
written against the actual LuxEngine tree.

.claude/docs/ (single source of truth, referenced from CLAUDE.md):
  Conventions.md           style + canonical helper APIs (Ref/Scope, FileSystem,
                           StringUtils, ImGuiEx, Colors::Theme, LUX_* macros)
  Building.md              premake5 flow, configs, feature flags, and the
                           "what to re-run" table
  Threading.md             thread contexts, the Application::Run frame loop,

  Rendering.md             renderer invariants: the global (set,binding)
                           namespace, pipeline caching, frame-indexed resource

.claude/skills/ dev (preflight), cr (local-only pre-commit review), send-pr

.gitignore: .claude/ -> .claude/* plus negations for docs/ and skills/, so the

which makes negations under it unreachable. The AGENTS.md ignore entry is
