commits.subject: Persist SMAA settings in project settings
commits.message:
Persist SMAA settings in project settings

SMAA and T2x were runtime-only, so both reset off on every launch. They
now round-trip through the project file and the runtime pack alongside the
other renderer quality settings.

Persists all four values rather than just the two toggles - a threshold
that resets while the toggle sticks would be worse than neither.

The binary runtime format is versioned, so the format version goes 13 -> 14
and the new reads are guarded on version >= 14. Packs written before this
still load and keep the defaults.

Note this puts SMAA inside the settings block that gets written back to
LuxSample.luxproj whenever the project is saved - the same mechanism that
silently carried a set of experiment values into 050abe9c. Worth a glance
at that file's diff before committing after a session of tweaking.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Add SMAA T2x temporal mode
commits.message:
Add SMAA T2x temporal mode

Jitters the projection between two subpixel positions on alternating
frames, runs the full SMAA 1x pipeline on each, and resolves the pair
along the velocity buffer. Two geometric samples per pixel, so unlike 1x
it also suppresses the temporal shimmer that purely spatial AA cannot see
- the practical answer to wanting MSAA-class edges in a deferred renderer,
without multisampling the G-buffer.

Reuses infrastructure already present from TAA: the projection jitter
hook, the per-object velocity buffer, and history ping-pong.

- The two jitter positions are paired with the AreaTex subtexture computed
  for them, per the reference's @SUBSAMPLE_INDICES table: (0.25,-0.25) ->
  (1,1,1,0) and (-0.25,0.25) -> (2,2,2,0). SubsampleIndices is now a
  push constant on the blending-weight pass rather than the hardcoded zero
  used for 1x; feeding the wrong index for a position yields subtly wrong
  coverage areas. Y is negated because the reference's table assumes a
  bottom-to-top axis and Vulkan clip space is top-to-bottom.
- SMAA-Resolve ports SMAAResolvePS with SMAA_REPROJECTION. Velocity here is
  (current - previous) in UV space, so the history is fetched by
  subtracting it - the reference negates instead, assuming the opposite
  motion-blur sign convention. History off screen falls back to the current
  frame rather than dragging in a clamped edge texel.
- The neighborhood pass no longer copies back in T2x mode: this frame is
  only half the answer until combined with the other jitter position, so
  the resolve owns the final copy and the history update.

Note T2x shares m_TAAJitterIndex with TAA and the jitter branch prefers
T2x, so enabling both leaves TAA with the 2-position pattern instead of
Halton-8. They are alternatives, not complements.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Plumb MSAA sample counts through images and framebuffers
commits.message:
Plumb MSAA sample counts through images and framebuffers

Groundwork for MSAA. FramebufferSpecification::Samples already existed but
was vestigial - only ever set to 1 and never reaching nvrhi - so a caller
asking for multisampling silently got none.

- ImageSpecification gains Samples, forwarded to nvrhi TextureDesc's
  sampleCount. Multisampled images are forced to one mip and verified to be
  attachments: the API cannot generate mips for one, and a sampled-only MS
  texture is not useful.
- Framebuffer now forwards its Samples to the attachment images it creates.
- SceneRendererOptions gains MSAASamples (1/2/4/8/16).

Deliberately NOT wired to the G-buffer yet. Doing that without the lighting
work would produce a broken image rather than antialiasing: the deferred
lighting pass samples the G-buffer with ordinary sampler2D, which is invalid
against a multisampled texture, and pipeline sample counts must match their
framebuffer's. So this commit changes no rendering - it only makes the
sample count reachable.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: SMAA: add diagonal pattern detection
commits.message:
SMAA: add diagonal pattern detection

Ports SMAACalculateDiagWeights and its helpers from the reference
(Core/vendor/smaa/SMAA.hlsl), completing SMAA 1x at the High preset.

A 45 degree staircase is one long diagonal, not a run of tiny horizontal
steps. Without this it takes the horizontal/vertical path and stays
visibly ragged, so diagonals are searched first inside the north-edge
branch and take priority - finding one sets e.r = 0 to skip the vertical
pass, matching the reference's control flow.

- SMAADecodeDiagBilinearAccess (vec2 and vec4): unpacks two binary edges
  from a single bilinear fetch, including the .rb pair and the c.yxwz
  swizzle on assignment.
- SMAASearchDiag1 / SMAASearchDiag2, the latter carrying the 0.25 texel
  @SearchDiag2Optimization offset.
- SMAAAreaDiag: MAX_DISTANCE_DIAG 20 rather than 16, and the +0.5 x shift
  since diagonal areas occupy the second half of AreaTex.
- Both diagonal directions with crossing-edge merge, and the .gr swizzle
  on the second direction whose areas come back transposed.

SMAA_MAX_SEARCH_STEPS_DIAG 8 pairs with the existing 16 - together the
reference's High preset.

LuxSample.luxproj picks up FixedRenderWidth/FixedRenderHeight defaults
from the fixed-resolution render mode.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Add SMAA 1x antialiasing
commits.message:
Add SMAA 1x antialiasing

Spatial antialiasing that runs at the end of the post chain, on the
tone-mapped image. Morphological AA keys off perceived edges, so it has to
see post-tonemap colour - the opposite of TAA, which resolves HDR scene
colour before bloom. Unlike TAA it cannot address temporal shimmer; it
cleans up staircase edges within a frame.

MSAA was the original request, but it does not fit a deferred renderer:
it would need the whole G-buffer (5 attachments plus depth) multisampled,
per-sample or edge-classified lighting, and the RG32UI material/object ID
target cannot be resolved by averaging. That is a major rework for a
result slower than this.

Three passes:
- SMAA-EdgeDetection: luma edge detection with local contrast adaptation,
  which suppresses the doubled edge a strong silhouette would otherwise
  leave one pixel over. Writes RG8; non-edge pixels write 0 rather than
  discarding so the weight pass never reads undefined texels.
- SMAA-BlendingWeights: ported from the reference (Core/vendor/smaa/
  SMAA.hlsl, MIT), kept structurally identical so it can be diffed against
  it. Bilinear-accelerated edge-distance search plus the AreaTex coverage
  lookup. Edges are sampled bilinearly - the search depends on interpolated
  values - while SearchTex is point-sampled, being a lookup table where
  interpolation returns distances that do not exist. Corner detection is
  included; diagonal detection is not (SMAA_DISABLE_DIAG_DETECTION).
- SMAA-NeighborhoodBlending: resolves the final colour, folding the weight
  into the sample coordinate so bilinear filtering does the mixing.

The AreaTex/SearchTex lookup tables ship as headers in the reference
implementation rather than as loadable assets, so they are vendored under
Core/vendor/smaa and picked up by an __has_include guard on a path
relative to SceneRenderer.cpp - no premake change needed. Without them
SMAA reports itself unavailable, allocates nothing, and the panel says so.

Also guards CreateSMAAPasses against a missing shader. ShaderLibrary::Get
is a map::at and its preceding assert compiles out in Release, so asking
for an unregistered shader surfaced as an unhandled std::out_of_range
during init naming nothing - which is exactly how this landed while the
weight shader was still unwritten. It now checks all three up front and
disables SMAA with a message naming the missing one.

The three passes are registered with the GPU profiler so their cost shows
in Render Stats.

commits.subject: Add fixed-resolution rendering with a letterboxed viewport
commits.message:
Add fixed-resolution rendering with a letterboxed viewport

Lets the editor render at an absolute resolution regardless of how large
the viewport is, so a 4K display can show the exact pixel count - and
therefore the cost - of a 1080p target.

The existing scale modes are all fractions of the output, which cannot
express an absolute size, so RenderResolutionScaleMode::FixedResolution
bypasses the scale factor in SetViewportSize and sets the render size
directly from FixedRenderWidth/Height. ResolveRenderResolutionScale still
reports an equivalent linear ratio so the stats HUD keeps showing a
meaningful figure.

Because the render aspect is then independent of the panel's, the viewport
letterboxes rather than stretches:

- Viewport now treats the panel size purely as the output size. The
  framebuffer, camera bounds and scene viewport all follow the renderer's
  resolved render size, without which a 16:9 render comes out distorted on
  a differently shaped panel.
- UpdateImageBounds fits the render aspect inside the panel and centres it.
  Two rects now exist: GetBounds() is the panel, for overlays anchored to
  its corners (toolbar, stats HUD); GetImageBounds() is the rendered image.
- ImGuizmo::SetRect and CastMousePick use the image rect. With panel-
  relative coordinates both would be offset by the bar width, putting
  gizmos and picking out of step with what is on screen. Clicks landing on
  a bar now fall outside the image and correctly pick nothing.

Persisted as FixedRenderWidth/FixedRenderHeight, with a Fixed Resolution
entry in the Render Scale dropdown plus 1920x1080 / 2560x1440 / 1280x720
presets.

Note that below the target resolution this supersamples rather than saves:
rendering 1920x1080 into a smaller window costs more than native. The
saving is on displays larger than the target.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Drain the render thread before recreating framebuffer resources
commits.message:
Drain the render thread before recreating framebuffer resources

Framebuffer::Resize calls RT_Invalidate() synchronously on whichever
thread called it - despite the RT_ prefix that is the main thread, since
the deferred Renderer::Submit path has been #if 0'd out. The nvrhi images
and framebuffer are therefore destroyed and recreated while the render
thread may still be draining queued commands that reference them.

Two crashes from the same cause, both on the render thread inside a
BeginRenderPass lambda:

- Heap corruption in Allocator::Free, reached from
  RefCountPtr<IFramebuffer>::~RefCountPtr when assigning the new
  framebuffer to the persisted graphics state released the previous one.
- 0xC0000005 reading 0x332 inside the driver's vkCmdPipelineBarrier2, via
  commitBarriersInternal issuing a barrier against a destroyed image.

Dragging a dock splitter resizes the viewport every frame, so the window
is wide open.

Block until the render thread is idle before invalidating, the same way
swap chain recreation already does (Window.cpp). BlockUntilRenderComplete
only waits for State::Idle - it does not advance the frame or swap queues
- so it is safe mid-frame, and it is a no-op under the single-threaded
policy or when the render thread is already idle. Skipped when called from
the render thread itself, where it would deadlock and ordering is already
guaranteed.

This makes resizing synchronous, so dragging a splitter stalls the main
thread until the render thread idles. The same trade the swap chain path
makes; reviving the deferred path is the real fix if it proves too costly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Remove the dead DescriptorSetManagerSpecification::DefaultResources flag
commits.message:
Remove the dead DescriptorSetManagerSpecification::DefaultResources flag

The guard read `if (m_Specification.DefaultResources || true)`, so it was
unconditional. The flag defaulted to false and had exactly one setter
(Material), meaning it never gated anything and misrepresented what the
code does.

Honouring it would have been a bug rather than a cleanup: the block does
not merely choose fallback samplers and textures, it creates the
RenderPassInput entry itself - resizing Input, setting Type and
IsWriteable. Every declared input needs that, so gating on the flag would
leave every render and compute pass (all of which leave it false) with no
input entries at all.

Dropped the flag and its setter and stated the unconditional behaviour
directly. No functional change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Constrain Ref's converting move ctor; guard kinematic MoveKinematic
commits.message:
Constrain Ref's converting move ctor; guard kinematic MoveKinematic

From Hazel c0449ab and a8d3282.

Ref: the converting move constructor was an unconstrained template, so it
was a candidate for any Ref<T2> whatsoever and would reinterpret the
pointer through its C-style cast rather than dropping out of overload
resolution. Constrain it on the same inheritance relationship the copy
constructor already required.

Physics: the root cause Hazel's patch fixes - computing kinematic velocity
against wall-clock time instead of the time Jolt actually integrates - is
not present here; Simulate() already passes FixedTimestep * CollisionSteps.
Ported the surrounding hardening:

- PreSimulate early-outs on a non-positive timestep. MoveKinematic divides
  by it, so a zero step sends the body to NaN, and Jolt is built with
  floating-point exceptions enabled outside Dist, making that a hard crash
  inside the next Update() rather than a recoverable error.
- Clamp the velocity MoveKinematic just set to the body's configured
  maxima, so a bad target degrades to the body lagging behind rather than
  diverging. A no-op for normal per-frame tracking.
- The same non-positive guard on JoltBody::MoveKinematic, which scripts can
  call directly without going through PreSimulate.

Hazel's opt-in body-divergence diagnostic scanner is not ported; it is a
debugging aid rather than a fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Port Hazel's Vulkan teardown hardening and sampler defaults
commits.message:
Port Hazel's Vulkan teardown hardening and sampler defaults

From Hazel 97a9d6c (validation fixes) and e355940 (repeat sampler). Only
the parts Lux had not already solved:

- VulkanSwapChain::Destroy: release the nvrhi framebuffers and swap chain
  images and run garbage collection before vkDestroySwapchainKHR. nvrhi
  defers destruction, so image views onto the swap chain's images outlived
  the images themselves. Also clear m_AcquiredSemaphore, which aliases an
  entry of m_AcquireSemaphores and dangled once those were destroyed.
- VulkanDeviceManager::DestroyDevice: waitForIdle + runGarbageCollection
  before the device goes away, for the same deferred-destruction reason.
- Image: VERIFY the createTexture result. nvrhi returns nullptr when
  vkCreateImage or its allocation fails, which otherwise surfaces much
  later as an access violation inside createFramebuffer/BindingSet. Reports
  the image and its size via the existing Utils::GetImageMemorySize.
- Framebuffer: VERIFY colour and depth attachments have a valid image
  before handing them to nvrhi.
- DescriptorSetManager: choose the default sampler from the declared
  name instead of always using the clamp sampler. A pass declaring
  r_RepeatSampler but not binding it silently sampled tiling content
  clamped, with nothing to report - the binding was valid, just wrong.
  r_MaterialSampler follows the repeat sampler, matching what
  BindCommonSceneRenderPassInputs binds.

Already present in Lux, so not ported: swap chain destroyed before the
surface, swap chain extent clamping, the ~VulkanShader Ref(this) fix
(527de04e), and the RG format entries in GetImageFormatBPP.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Drop the SSR composite bilateral upscale, matching Hazel
commits.message:
Drop the SSR composite bilateral upscale, matching Hazel

The upscale weighted every tap by its own alpha and then normalised by
the summed weight, so a pixel with no reflection (alpha 0) next to one
with a confident hit (alpha ~1) saw a ~1000:1 weight ratio and inherited
both that neighbour's colour and its alpha. Since the composite blends
SrcAlpha/OneMinusSrcAlpha - a lerp toward the SSR colour - those pixels
were dragged toward a dark reflection they should never have received.
At reduced SSR resolution the bleed covered a source texel, which is why
the artifacts appeared as blocky rectangles rather than following surface
shapes.

Hazel's composite is a straight SampleLinear of the SSR buffer; match it.

- SSR-Composite.glsl: reduced to the single sample. Removes the bilateral
  filter, the u_Uniforms push constants, u_Depth/u_Normal and Buffers.glslh.
- SceneRenderer.cpp: drop the matching push-constant writes (the block no
  longer exists, so they would fail at runtime) and the depth/normal/Camera
  binds at all four SetInput sites. Sampler binds are guarded with
  IsInputValid since r_DefaultSampler/r_PointSampler are now unused and may
  be stripped from reflection. UsesSSRBilateralUpscale is now unreferenced.
- SSR.glsl: fix misleading indentation - the reflection-occlusion scale
  applies to both branches of the bent-normals decode, not just the else.

Note the SSRQuality presets still select resolution but no longer have a
filter behind them, so reduced-res reflections upscale bilinearly. A
replacement must weight by depth and normal only, never by a sample's own
alpha.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Fix ImGui startup asserts; async transfer off by default
commits.message:
Fix ImGui startup asserts; async transfer off by default

- ImGuiDrawDataSnapshot: point each cloned draw list's build cursors
  (_VtxWritePtr/_IdxWritePtr/_VtxCurrentIdx) at the end of its buffers so
  ImDrawData::AddDrawList()'s integrity assert passes. CloneOutput() leaves
  them null, which aborted every frame in Debug (IM_ASSERT).

  ImTextureID_Invalid, so the font atlas landing in slot 0 tripped GetTexID()'s
  "tex_id != 0" assert whenever text was drawn.

  their graphics state at upload-list close emit VERTEX_INPUT / SHADER_READ|WRITE
  barriers illegal on a transfer-only queue. Graphics-queue upload is spec-correct.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Fix GTAO non-bent black screen, toggle crash, and log spam
commits.message:
Fix GTAO non-bent black screen, toggle crash, and log spam

The GTAO packed buffer stores the visibility term in a different byte
depending on bent-normals mode (high byte when bent, low byte otherwise).
The AO-Composite/AO-Debug and SSR consumers selected that byte at compile
time via #if __HZ_GTAO_COMPUTE_BENT_NORMALS, which could fall out of sync
with the producer's runtime packing and read the (zero) high byte for
non-bent data -> occlusion 0 -> the whole scene multiplied to black.

- Decode the visibility byte at runtime from a BentNormals flag (fed from
  m_Options.GTAOBentNormals, the same source that drives the producer's
  packing), mirroring what GTAO-Temporal.glsl already does. AO-Composite
  gains a push constant; SSR repurposes its trailing padding field.
- DescriptorSetManager::InvalidateAndUpdate now skips a declared-but-unbound
  input instead of dereferencing a null Ref. Toggling GTAO on recompiles the
  AO passes into a variant that newly declares Camera; in the window before
  the rebind lands the resource is null, which crashed the render thread.
- Guard the per-frame AO-Composite/AO-Debug SetInput calls with IsInputValid
  to stop per-frame "Input not found" log spam when GTAO is compiled out.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Log chosen swapchain present mode + supported modes
commits.message:
Log chosen swapchain present mode + supported modes

commits.subject: Prefer Mailbox present mode when VSync is off
commits.message:
Prefer Mailbox present mode when VSync is off

The swapchain only ever chose FIFO (vsync) or Immediate (uncapped but tearing).
Profiling showed vkQueuePresentKHR blocking ~13.5 ms/frame under FIFO on Windows
(DWM), dominating the frame. With VSync off, prefer MAILBOX when available —
uncapped like Immediate but tear-free — falling back to Immediate, then FIFO. No
change when VSync is on (still FIFO).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Fix Ref double-free race: delete from the atomic decrement's own result
commits.message:
Fix Ref double-free race: delete from the atomic decrement's own result

Ref::DecRef() decremented the atomic refcount and then, as a SEPARATE atomic
load, checked GetRefCount() == 0 to decide deletion. Two threads releasing the
last two references to the same object (e.g. the asset worker thread and the main
thread sharing a Ref<Asset>) can both observe 0 and both `delete` -> double-free,
corrupting the heap. The corruption surfaced later as an access violation in
s_LiveReferences during shutdown.

DecRefCount() now returns the post-decrement value and DecRef() deletes only when
that atomic decrement itself yields 0, so exactly one thread can delete.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Fix data race in RefUtils::IsLive (shutdown heap corruption)
commits.message:
Fix data race in RefUtils::IsLive (shutdown heap corruption)

IsLive() read s_LiveReferences without holding s_LiveReferenceMutex, while
AddToLiveReferences/RemoveFromLiveReferences lock it. WeakRef::IsValid() calls
IsLive() from any thread (e.g. the asset thread), so a find() could race a
concurrent insert()/erase() that rehashes and reallocates the bucket array —
reading a half-freed hash table and corrupting the set. The corruption then
crashed later in erase() during EditorAssetManager shutdown (access violation in
std::_Hash::_Find_last). Lock the mutex in IsLive() so all access is serialized.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Fix shutdown heap corruption: don't capture Ref(this) in ~VulkanShader
commits.message:
Fix shutdown heap corruption: don't capture Ref(this) in ~VulkanShader

The destructor deferred its shader-module cleanup via
Renderer::SubmitResourceFree([instance = Ref(this)]...). Capturing Ref(this)
inside the destructor resurrects the object (refcount 0 -> 1) while it is already
being deleted. The deferred lambda then runs during Renderer::Shutdown on
freed memory (use-after-free of m_PipelineShaderStageCreateInfos), and when its
Ref dies the shader is deleted a second time -- double-freeing the member maps and
tripping the heap-corruption / "not in alloc map" break in Allocator::Free.

Capture the shader-module handles by value instead, matching Release().

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Guard PreConvolution and Bloom compute barriers against null image handles
commits.message:
Guard PreConvolution and Bloom compute barriers against null image handles

Same resize race as the PipelineCompute barriers: PreConvolutionCompute (SSR)
and BloomCompute record per-mip barrier lambdas that read the image's GPU handle
on the render thread. During a viewport resize the mip images are reallocated, so
the handle is momentarily null and setTextureState crashed in nvrhi's
requireTextureState. Skip the barrier when the handle is null (the resource is
unallocated, so there is no state to transition); it renders correctly again once
recreated. Sweep confirms no other unguarded setTextureState/setBufferState
GetHandle() barriers remain.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Fix editor render-thread crashes: ImGui 1.92 textures, swapchain resize, compute barriers
commits.message:
Fix editor render-thread crashes: ImGui 1.92 textures, swapchain resize, compute barriers

Three independent crashes, all surfacing as nvrhi requireTextureState(nullptr)
on the render thread when interacting with or resizing the editor UI.

- ImGui backend now implements the 1.92 texture system (RendererHasTextures +
  ImTextureData create/update/destroy + SetTexID) instead of the legacy one-shot
  font atlas, so draw commands resolve to live textures. Textures are serviced in
  ImGuiLayer::End() after ImGui::Render(), on the main thread, before snapshotting.
  Registry gains keep-alive storage and a persistent-slot free list. Defensive null
  guards kept in ResolveTexture and the draw loop.

- VulkanSwapChain no longer recreates mid-BeginFrame: destroying a swapchain whose
  acquire semaphore still has a pending signal is UB and crashed on resize.
  eSuboptimal/eOutOfDate now set a NeedsRecreate flag serviced at the idle boundary
  in Window::ProcessEvents.

- Image2D::RT_Invalidate builds the new texture and swaps m_Info.ImageHandle in a
  single store instead of Release()-then-create, so a concurrent render-thread
  reader never sees a null handle. PipelineCompute image/buffer barriers skip a
  null/mid-recreation handle instead of passing it to nvrhi.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Merge pull request #29 from starbounded-dev/feature/linux
commits.message:
Merge pull request #29 from starbounded-dev/feature/linux

Linux port: build, Vulkan/Wayland runtime, scripting, and distribution packaging

commits.subject: Scale the editor UI for HiDPI / fractional-scaling displays
commits.message:
Scale the editor UI for HiDPI / fractional-scaling displays

The editor was unusable on a 150% 4K monitor, in two different ways depending on the
windowing system. ImGui_ImplGlfw_NewFrame derives DisplaySize from glfwGetWindowSize and
DisplayFramebufferScale from the framebuffer ratio, so:

  X11/Windows - the window size is already in physical pixels, framebuffer scale is 1,
                and nothing is scaled: a 15px font on a 4K panel is physically tiny.
  Wayland     - the window size is logical and framebuffer scale is 1.5, so geometry is
                the right size but glyphs baked at 15px are stretched 1.5x and blur.

ImGui is 1.92.6 and can re-bake fonts on demand, but that needs
ImGuiBackendFlags_RendererHasTextures, which our NVRHI renderer does not advertise - it
only sets RendererHasVtxOffset and RendererHasViewports. So the atlas is static and
io.ConfigDpiScaleFonts would merely stretch it. Glyphs have to be baked at the physical
size they will be drawn at instead:

  bake at size * contentScale       glyphs rasterised at true physical pixels
  FontScaleMain = 1 / fbScale       undo scaling the compositor already applies
  ScaleAllSizes(contentScale/fbScale)  padding and rounding in DisplaySize units

Both cases then resolve correctly: on X11 fonts and metrics scale together, on Wayland
fonts bake larger while layout stays in logical units.

LUX_UI_SCALE overrides the detected scale, and the values are logged at startup, so a
wrong detection can be diagnosed and worked around without a rebuild.

Verified: at scale 1.0 the path is a no-op, so nothing changes for existing setups;
LUX_UI_SCALE=1.5 reports contentScale=1.50 fbScale=1.00 uiScale=1.50 and the editor runs
clean. The visual result still needs confirming on an actual HiDPI display.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: CI: trim the Linux editor artifact
commits.message:
CI: trim the Linux editor artifact

The artifact was 417 MB, more than double the Windows one, because packaging globbed
every *.so out of the Vulkan SDK lib/ - roughly 780 MB of validation layers and SPIRV
tooling the editor never loads. Only three vendored libraries are actually resolved.

Bundle exactly what ldd reports instead. ldd gives the full transitive closure, so
filtering it to our vendored directories keeps precisely what is needed and adapts to
the runner (locally shaderc comes from the SDK, elsewhere it may come from the system).
That takes lib/ from 38 libraries to 3, 27 MB.

Also enables stripdown on the Linux Vulkan SDK install, matching Windows, and prunes
build intermediates and asset caches from the bundled sample project.
Scripts/Binaries is kept - it holds the sample game's compiled script assembly.

The step now asserts the bundle resolves with LD_LIBRARY_PATH unset, since the binary's
RPATH is $ORIGIN/lib; otherwise we could ship an artifact that only runs on a machine
that already has these libraries. Verified locally by running the packaging step as
written: 3 libraries bundled, zero unresolved dependencies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: CI: upload artifacts for Release only, and add a Linux editor artifact
commits.message:
CI: upload artifacts for Release only, and add a Linux editor artifact

Debug and Dist no longer upload an editor bundle or build logs on either platform; the
upload steps are kept, just gated to Release. Windows previously uploaded for both Debug
and Release.

Linux had no artifacts at all, so it now matches Windows. Two differences the packaging
has to account for: the Linux build output contains only the executable, and the binary
is linked with RPATH $ORIGIN/lib - so Resources, DotNet and LuxSampleProject are copied
alongside it and the vendored shared libraries are bundled into lib/. Verified locally:
the resulting tree resolves every dependency with LD_LIBRARY_PATH unset, the vendored
libs coming from the bundled lib/. System libraries (GTK3, TBB, ...) are still expected
on the target machine, as with any distro build.

The Linux build step now tees to logs/, with pipefail so a build failure is not masked
by tee's exit status.

commits.subject: CI: install tbb, zlib and llvm-ar for the Linux build
commits.message:
CI: install tbb, zlib and llvm-ar for the Linux build

Two link-stage failures on the Linux runner, both missing packages:

  cannot find -ltbb          (Debug, Release)
  llvm-ar: not found         (Dist)

TBB is an explicit Linux-only dependency (Dependencies.lua:64). The llvm-ar case is
config-specific: only Dist compiles with -flto, and premake's clang toolset then archives
with llvm-ar because GNU ar cannot index LLVM bitcode - the other configurations use plain
ar and got far enough to hit the tbb error instead.

Adds libtbb-dev, zlib1g-dev (for -lz) and llvm, plus a fallback symlink because Ubuntu
ships llvm-ar version-suffixed and premake invokes it unversioned.

The package list was re-derived by extracting every -l flag from the generated makefiles
rather than reacting to one error at a time; everything else is either already installed,
vendored, or provided by the Vulkan SDK.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Fix Log::PrintMessage against libstdc++ versions without std::format_string
commits.message:
Fix Log::PrintMessage against libstdc++ versions without std::format_string

The Linux CI build failed compiling every LUX_CORE_* call: "no known conversion from
std::format_string<...> to format_string_t<Args...> (aka basic_string_view<char>)".

spdlog only aliases format_string_t to std::format_string when the standard library
advertises __cpp_lib_format >= 202207L, and otherwise falls back to std::string_view
(Core/vendor/spdlog/include/spdlog/common.h:151). PrintMessage hardcoded
std::format_string and forwarded it straight to the logger, so it only compiled where
that alias happened to match. It built on Arch (clang 22, new libstdc++) and on MSVC,
which is why this went unnoticed until an Ubuntu 24.04 runner built it.

Take spdlog::format_string_t instead, so the parameter follows whatever spdlog resolved
to. PrintMessageTag and PrintAssertMessage deliberately keep std::format_string: they
call std::format themselves and hand spdlog an already-formatted string.

Verified both branches: the fix compiles against a simulated string_view alias (with the
previous signature failing the same test, confirming it reproduces the CI error), and a
local Core debug build still succeeds where the alias is std::format_string.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Bootstrap premake5 on Linux instead of assuming a local binary
commits.message:
Bootstrap premake5 on Linux instead of assuming a local binary

The Linux CI job failed with "./premake5: not found". Only vendor/bin/premake5.exe is
committed, and .gitignore matches any file named "premake5", so a clean checkout has no
Linux premake at all - the root binary only ever existed on developer machines. This
affected every fresh clone, not just CI.

Linux-Build.sh now resolves premake in order: a local ./premake5, then
vendor/bin/premake5, otherwise it downloads the pinned 5.0.0-beta4 Linux release and
verifies its SHA-256 before use. The pinned archive is byte-identical to the binary
this port was developed against, so generation behaviour is unchanged. The downloaded
binary lands in vendor/bin/premake5, which the existing ignore rule already covers.

Linux-GenProjects.sh gets the same resolution order, and points at Linux-Build.sh when
no binary is available.

Also corrects CLAUDE.md, which claimed the binary was checked in at ./premake5.

Verified by removing both binaries and running the script from a clean state: it
downloads, verifies, and completes a full Release build.

commits.subject: CI: add a Linux build job

CI: add a Linux build job

from a clean checkout, but Dependencies.lua and Linux-Build.sh both prefer the
VULKAN_SDK the action exports.

build that silently produces nothing cannot report success.

commits.subject: One-shot Linux build script, generated csproj files, and CI NuGet restore
commits.message:
One-shot Linux build script, generated csproj files, and CI NuGet restore

Fix the Windows CI failure (NETSDK1004: project.assets.json not found). ScriptCore
and Coral.Managed are premake-generated SDK-style C# projects inside Lux.sln, and
those cannot build until a NuGet restore produces obj/project.assets.json. Nothing
in the pipeline ran one. Pass /restore to MSBuild so the Restore target runs first
with the same properties as the build. This break is pre-existing on dev (same error
since "Merge Coral (.NET 9) scripting into dev"), not introduced by the Linux port.

- scripts/Linux-Build.sh is now a single entry point: prerequisite checks, submodule
  sync, C# project generation, managed assemblies, native engine, and the sample
  game's scripts. Also fixes it only working from the repo root (LUX_DIR came from
  `realpath .`) and builds with -j$(nproc), overridable via JOBS.
- Make the ScriptCore premake guard action-aware: skip only for the gmake actions,
  whose C# generator shells out to csc. vs2022 is wanted on Linux because it emits
  SDK-style .csproj files that `dotnet build` consumes on any platform. Requires
  `premake5 --os=linux vs2022`, since otherwise os.target() reports "windows" and
  Coral's nethost probe hunts for win-* runtime packs and aborts.
- Add Linux-GenProjects.sh for the sample game's standalone script workspace, which
  the root generation does not cover.
- Stop tracking LuxSample.csproj and ScriptCore.csproj now that both can be generated
  on Linux; the blanket **.csproj ignore applies again and regeneration no longer
  dirties the tree.
- Force Copy Local off for assembly references in the sample project via
  Directory.Build.props. premake cannot emit <Private>, and copying ScriptCore next
  to the game assembly makes the load context resolve a second ScriptCore, giving
  scripts a different Lux.Entity identity so IsSubclassOf fails and they silently
  never run.

commits.subject: Fix Linux scripting, fullscreen swap chain extent, and script project builds
commits.message:
Fix Linux scripting, fullscreen swap chain extent, and script project builds

Scripting was silently dead in exported runtimes: the app assembly is loaded
from the asset pack via LoadAssemblyFromMemory, but assemblies loaded from a
byte[] have an empty Assembly.Location, so Coral enumerated zero local types.
BuildAssemblyCache then cached nothing, IsValidScript() failed, and the entity
was dropped in OnRuntimeStart and again every frame in OnUpdateRuntime - both
without any diagnostic. Stage the packed binary into the shadow directory and
load it by path (the route the editor already proves works), keeping the
in-memory load as a warned fallback. Coral is a submodule and was not touched.

- Fix ScriptGlue component registration on Linux: typeid().name() returns the
  Itanium-mangled "N3Lux18TransformComponentE" rather than MSVC's readable
  "struct Lux::TransformComponent", so the namespace strip kept the whole
  mangled string and no component ever resolved. Demangle via __cxa_demangle;
  the Windows path is unchanged.
- Report scripts that fail to register instead of skipping them silently, and
  log cached type / registered script counts per assembly.
- Add SDK-style LuxSample.csproj + Directory.Build.props so the sample script
  project builds via `dotnet build` on Linux (premake's C# generator needs csc).
  References use Private=false: copying ScriptCore/Coral.Managed next to the
  game assembly resolves a second ScriptCore, giving a distinct Lux.Entity
  identity that fails IsSubclassOf. BaseIntermediateOutputPath lives in
  Directory.Build.props so NuGet stops emitting an obj/ that made the editor
  consider scripts perpetually stale.
- Un-ignore the two hand-authored csproj files. The blanket **.csproj rule
  dates from when they were all premake-generated, but Linux-Build.sh builds
  ScriptCore.csproj by path, so a fresh clone could not build at all.
- Fix fullscreen swap chain creation: only the windowed branch reconciled the
  window size against the real framebuffer, and Create() was passed the
  requested spec size rather than the actual one. Also clamp imageExtent to
  [minImageExtent, maxImageExtent] (VUID-01274) - violating it is reported as
  VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY - and stop assigning the 0xFFFFFFFF sentinel
  into m_Width/m_Height on the resize path.
- Ignore exported standalone game builds.

commits.subject: Replace Mono scripting with Coral (.NET 9), Hazel-style architecture
commits.message:
Replace Mono scripting with Coral (.NET 9), Hazel-style architecture

Swap the dead embedded Mono (.NET Framework 4.7.2) C# scripting backend
for Coral (github.com/StudioCherno/Coral, .NET 9), mirroring Hazel's Script
system in both build layout and feature set.

Build:
- Vendor Coral as a submodule at Core/vendor/Coral (upstream, unpatched).
- Use Coral's own premake for Coral.Native + Coral.Managed; ScriptCore and
  LuxSample become premake C# projects (clr Unsafe, net9.0) in Lux.sln.
- Coral's upstream premake is patched from the SUPERPROJECT (re-open in
  premake5.lua) so it travels with the repo: add Debug-AS/Dist configs to
  Coral.Native and a stub Coral.Generator to satisfy its dependson.
- Deploy Coral.Managed to Editor/DotNet via a {COPYFILE} postbuild on Core.
- Remove Core/vendor/mono and Editor/mono (305-file BCL); update Setup.py,
  Linux-Build.sh, CI (setup-dotnet 9.x, Mixed Platforms), README, .gitignore.

Architecture (ported from Hazel's Script/):
- Singleton ScriptEngine with an FNV-hashed metadata cache (ScriptMetadata/
  FieldMetadata), a StableVector of ManagedObjects, HostInstance + one ALC,
  Instantiate/DestroyInstance, and shadow-copy hot reload + SynchronizeStorage.
- Dual-mode FieldStorage (serializable buffer when idle, live managed-field
  proxy when playing; arrays + asset-refs), owned per-Scene as ScriptStorage.
- CSharpObject, ScriptFileAsset, dedicated ScriptBuilder (dotnet build).
- ScriptGlue: AddInternalCall/UploadInternalCalls, Bool32/String marshalling,
  component add/has/remove maps keyed by TypeId, scoped to Lux systems.
- ScriptCore C#: [ShowInEditor]/[EditorAssignable] attributes, asset-ref
  types, delegate*-field InternalCalls, ushort-backed KeyCode/MouseButton.

Integration:
- ScriptComponent carries ScriptID; Scene drives OnCreate/OnUpdate/OnDestroy
  (gated by ScriptMetadata::HasMethod) and CopyEntityStorage on duplicate.
- SceneSerializer persists ScriptStorage; SceneHierarchyPanel drives the field
  UI from metadata + FieldStorage.
- ContactListener2D routes collisions to managed OnCollision*Internal bridges.
- New ImGuiEx::PropertyScriptReference: a searchable script-class picker
  (like the asset picker) over ScriptEngine::GetAllScripts().
- Host init in Application; per-project load in Project::SetActive; runtime
  path in RuntimeLayer.

Verified: full Lux.sln builds (Debug, Debug-AS, Dist); a standalone Coral
harness confirms host init on .NET 9, ALC load of ScriptCore + LuxSample,
Entity-subclass discovery, field/method metadata, CreateInstance and field
round-trip. Live in-editor Play not yet exercised.

commits.subject: Enrich Discord Rich Presence and fix session auto-reconnect
commits.message:
Enrich Discord Rich Presence and fix session auto-reconnect

Rich Presence now shows a count-up session timer and artwork. Activity
carries a start timestamp captured at Init(), kept constant across presence
changes so switching scenes doesn't reset it. Adds a PresenceInfo struct
(details, state, large/small image keys + tooltips) and a SetPresence
overload; the editor sends a "lux_logo" large image and a play/simulate mode
badge as the small image. Image keys reference assets uploaded to the app's
Art Assets page; missing keys just render nothing.

Fix the "must reconnect every launch" bug: the subsystem only persisted the
refresh token and called RefreshToken() on startup, which Discord rejected
every time (likely because the app isn't a Public Client). Now the session
file stores the access token + refresh token + expiry, and startup reuses the
still-valid access token directly via UpdateToken (no refresh needed for ~7
days), only falling back to a refresh once it's expired. Refresh failures now
log Discord's actual error instead of a generic "expired" message.

commits.subject: Add Discord Social SDK integration (auth + Rich Presence)
commits.message:
Add Discord Social SDK integration (auth + Rich Presence)

Opt-in engine subsystem (Core/Source/Lux/Social/) that authenticates against
Discord and publishes Rich Presence, so the editor shows what project/scene
you're in on your profile. Double opt-in: compiled in only with the --discord
premake flag (LUX_ENABLE_DISCORD), and off at runtime by default behind the
Discord.RichPresenceEnabled setting. With the flag absent every entry point is
an inline no-op, so the default build is unaffected.

DiscordSocial is a static-class subsystem in the house style: Init/Shutdown
tie into Application's ctor/dtor, Update() pumps discordpp::RunCallbacks() once
per frame from the main loop. It runs the OAuth2 PKCE flow, persists a refresh
token to resume silently on restart, and drives presence from the editor's
scene-state transitions. discordpp.h is kept out of the public header; its
single-header implementation is isolated in DiscordppImpl.cpp (NoPCH).

The Application Settings panel gains a Discord page (enable toggle, Application
ID, Connect/Disconnect, status). IsAvailable() distinguishes "not compiled in"
from "compiled but switched off" so the toggle is always reachable.

The Windows-release SDK subset (~11 MB) is vendored under
Core/vendor/discord_social_sdk/; the *.lib survives the global gitignore via a
negation. Setup steps in that dir's DISCORD_SDK_SETUP.md.

commits.subject: Upload assets on a dedicated transfer queue
commits.message:
Upload assets on a dedicated transfer queue

Route mesh/texture/buffer uploads onto the GPU's dedicated copy queue so
asset streaming and loads no longer contend with the graphics queue against
frame rendering. All uploads already funnel through the batched
RecordResourceUpload/FlushResourceUploads seam, so the change is contained:

- Enable the copy queue (Window.cpp) and make the transfer family optional in
  VulkanDeviceManager (a missing dedicated family no longer rejects the
  device); expose IsTransferQueueAvailable().
- Flush the upload batch on nvrhi::CommandQueue::Copy when async is effective,
  and make the consuming queue wait on the copy execution instance via the
  existing QueueWaitForCommandList path (same exclusive-sharing model as async
  compute). Falls back to inline graphics-queue submit otherwise.
- Runtime toggle Renderer.AsyncTransferQueue (default on), live-toggleable,
  auto-falls back when no dedicated transfer queue exists. Editor checkbox in
  the Threading settings page; honored at startup in editor and runtime.

Verified: builds Release/Mixed Platforms; editor loads the Sponza sample via
the transfer queue (family 1) with no Vulkan/device-lost errors.

commits.subject: Use VRS on low-frequency fullscreen passes
commits.message:
Use VRS on low-frequency fullscreen passes

Key changes:

- Opt Vulkan graphics pipelines into dynamic fragment shading rate when the active device supports variable rate shading.

- Add a renderer-level fragment shading rate API and keep normal pass begin state at 1x1 so coarse shading cannot leak into later geometry or UI draws.

- Apply 2x2 shading to low-frequency fullscreen graphics passes: sky atmosphere, volumetric clouds, cloud composite, atmospheric fog, AO composite, SSR composite, and DOF.

- Add a project/editor toggle for Variable Rate Shading and bump runtime project settings to version 13 with backward-compatible reads.

Validation:

- Built Editor.vcxproj Release|x64 with MSBuild after closing the running Release editor that held Editor.exe locked.

- Ran a 25 second hidden Release editor smoke on LuxSample and scanned fresh logs for VUIDs, Vulkan errors, descriptor mismatches, shader compile failures, asserts, and crashes.

commits.subject: Tune shadow cascades and soft filtering
commits.message:
Tune shadow cascades and soft filtering

Add an active directional cascade count over the existing four-layer shadow array, default realtime presets to three cascades with a less log-heavy split distribution, and render only active cascade passes.

Replace all-soft PCSS with a configurable shadow filter mode: tuned 16-tap PCF, full PCSS, or hybrid PCSS-near/PCF-far. Directional and spot shadow sampling now use std140-safe filter params and clamp inactive cascade samples.

Persist the new cascade/filter controls through project YAML and runtime project data version 12, and expose them in the renderer settings panel.

Validation: built Editor.vcxproj Release|x64, ran a 25-second hidden LuxSample editor smoke to exercise shader loading, and scanned logs for shader compile, validation/VUID/descriptor/crash errors; only known startup warnings and the existing RenderGraph warning block appeared.

commits.subject: Cull shadow casters per cascade
commits.message:
Cull shadow casters per cascade

Split directional shadow caster storage into per-cascade buckets while keeping spot shadows on a separate atlas-wide bucket, so directional cascades draw only the casters that intersect each cascade.

Add conservative tiny-caster rejection for far directional cascades using projected radius from camera distance, leaving near cascades untouched to avoid silhouette loss.

Upload object-index bases per shadow bucket, draw dynamic directional cascades only when that cascade has movers, and split directional vs spot caster hashes so cascade churn does not invalidate the spot static cache.

Validation: built Editor.vcxproj Release|x64, ran a 25-second hidden LuxSample editor smoke, and scanned logs for validation/VUID/descriptor/crash errors; only the existing RenderGraph warning block appeared.

commits.subject: Cache static shadow casters
commits.message:
Cache static shadow casters

Split shadow submissions into static and dynamic buckets using per-caster transform stability tracking, so stable casters stop re-rendering every frame while moving/transient casters remain live.

Add cached static depth targets for directional cascades and the spot shadow atlas, plus dynamic no-clear passes that render movers over a copied static cache.

Invalidate static shadow caches on caster-set, cascade, atlas, resolution, and light-state changes; keep spot and directional live caches valid when no relevant state changes.

Update shadow caster hashing to track static and dynamic sets separately and extend Renderer::CopyImage to copy layered images for directional cascade cache restores.

Validation: built Editor.vcxproj Release|x64, ran a 25-second hidden LuxSample editor smoke after the spot-cache extension, and scanned logs for validation/VUID/descriptor/crash errors; only the existing RenderGraph warning block appeared.

commits.subject: Fix meshlet frustum over-culling at the viewport edges
commits.message:
Fix meshlet frustum over-culling at the viewport edges

The task shader's Gribb-Hartmann planes are unnormalized, but the sphere test
compared the signed distance against the bare radius as if the plane normals
were unit length. Wherever length(plane.xyz) > 1 the test over-culled by that
factor, so partially-visible meshlets popped out right at the screen edges
while the camera moved. Scale the radius by the plane normal's length.

commits.subject: Drop the backface-cone cull from the meshlet PreDepth task shader
commits.message:
Drop the backface-cone cull from the meshlet PreDepth task shader

The cone test assumes the geometric (cross-product) winding matches the
rasterizer's front-face convention. With the projection Y-flip and mirrored
instance transforms that assumption inverts, so the test culled visible
meshlets - chunks of walls/arches disappeared depending on the view.

Frustum culling (the meaningful win for a depth-only pass) stays; backfacing
meshlets are already nearly free at raster via the pipeline's backface cull.
The per-meshlet cone data is still built and uploaded so the test can return
once winding is validated per-instance.

commits.subject: Add mesh-shader PreDepth path with per-meshlet culling (VK_EXT_mesh_shader)
commits.message:
Add mesh-shader PreDepth path with per-meshlet culling (VK_EXT_mesh_shader)

Mesh shading was enabled but mis-wired: the device manager requested
VK_NV_mesh_shader while NVRHI's Vulkan backend implements VK_EXT_mesh_shader
(Feature::Meshlets checks EXT, dispatchMesh calls drawMeshTasksEXT), so the
feature query always returned false. Switched the device to the EXT extension
and features.

Infrastructure:
- Shader toolchain understands task/mesh stages end to end (#pragma stage :
  task/mesh, shaderc kinds, stage macros, cache extensions, ShaderPack stages).
- MeshSource::BuildRenderGeometry splits every submesh LOD into meshlets
  (<= 64 verts / <= 124 tris) with a bounding sphere and backface cone each,
  uploaded as raw-view SSBOs; the shared vertex buffer gained raw views so the
  mesh stage reads it directly (no geometry duplication). Only built when the
  GPU supports mesh shaders.
- Pipeline creates an nvrhi MeshletPipeline when the shader has a mesh stage.

Rendering (opt-in, default off):
- PreDepth_Meshlet.glsl: the task stage culls 32 meshlets per workgroup
  against the frustum (planes derived from the camera VP) and a
  meshoptimizer-style backface cone, compacts survivors into the payload; the
  mesh stage fetches meshlet vertices and emits triangles with the same
  two-step position math as GBuffer_Static and invariant gl_Position (the
  GBuffer depth-Equal contract).
- SceneRenderer::PreDepthPass branches to the meshlet submission loop when
  "Mesh Shaders (Experimental)" is enabled in the Scene Renderer panel;
  per-mesh set-0 binding sets are cached on the MeshSource. Falls back to the
  classic vertex path automatically when unsupported.
- Option persisted in the project (YAML + runtime format v11).

commits.subject: Add auto-generated mesh LODs with distance-based selection
commits.message:
Add auto-generated mesh LODs with distance-based selection

submesh to the shared vertex/index buffers; rigged submeshes and meshes
where clustering yields <8% index reduction keep LOD 0 only. CPU-side
vertices/indices are untouched, so physics cooking and mesh export are
unaffected.

The renderer picks a LOD per submesh at submit time from the camera
distance in bounding-sphere radii (SelectStaticMeshLOD), scaled by the
new MeshLODDistanceScale option, and both the direct draw path
(RT_DrawStaticMesh) and the GPU-driven indirect path
(BuildIndirectDrawCommand) draw the selected LOD range. LODIndex is part
of MeshKey so draw-command buckets, caching, and sorting stay correct.

Mesh LODs toggle + distance scale are exposed in the Scene Renderer
panel and persisted in the project (YAML + runtime format v10).

commits.subject: Async compute (3/N): split the graphics submit around the compute wait
commits.message:
Async compute (3/N): split the graphics submit around the compute wait

Previously the graphics queue waited for the async cluster culling up front,
so the two queues never actually overlapped. Split FlushDrawList's graphics
recording at the first consumer of the compute output ("Deferred Lighting"):
the pre-lighting half submits with no wait (overlapping the compute cluster
work), then queueWaitForCommandList is inserted, then the deferred-onward half
submits and waits.

- RenderGraph::Execute gains a [begin,end) range overload.
- RenderCommandBuffer::Begin/End gain a recordFrameQueries flag so the second
  half doesn't re-reset the per-frame-in-flight timer/pipeline-stat pool the
  first half already bracketed (would trip Vulkan validation).
- All gated behind EnableAsyncCompute (off by default); the OFF path and the
  no-Deferred-Lighting fallback keep the original single-submit behavior.

Foundation only: cluster culling is cheap, so the win is marginal until the
expensive passes (GTAO/SSR) move to compute and shadows reorder after GBuffer.

commits.subject: Async compute (2/N): cluster light-culling on the compute queue (correctness-first)
commits.message:
Async compute (2/N): cluster light-culling on the compute queue (correctness-first)

With EnableAsyncCompute (still off by default), cluster build + light
culling run on the compute queue instead of inline on graphics:

- A dedicated m_ComputeCommandBuffer (compute queue) is created at init.
- FlushDrawList records both cluster passes onto it after the uploads,
  submits it, and the graphics submit waits on that instance via
  Renderer::QueueWaitForCommandList so deferred lighting reads valid light
  grids/index lists.
- The two cluster passes route their dispatches/barriers/clears to the
  compute buffer when async, and skip the graphics-buffer GPU perf markers
  (timer queries live on the graphics buffer).
- BuildRenderGraph omits the two cluster nodes when async (they ran on
  compute); the graph never modeled their SSBOs anyway, so no graph edge
  is lost — cross-queue ordering is the queue wait.

Correctness-first: this is the smallest cross-queue slice and validates
that compute-written SSBOs are safely read on graphics. The graphics queue
waits up front, so it does NOT overlap graphics work yet (perf-neutral);
the graphics-submit split for real overlap is the next step. Off path is
unchanged (cluster passes stay in the graph on the graphics buffer).

commits.subject: Cache the mip-generation compute pipeline instead of rebuilding it per texture
commits.message:
Cache the mip-generation compute pipeline instead of rebuilding it per texture

Texture2D/TextureCube::GenerateMips built a fresh LinearSample /
LinearSampleUInt PipelineCompute for every texture, so loading a project
produced hundreds of redundant 'Creating compute pipeline' driver builds
(the bulk of the first-launch/asset-load stutter and log spam).

Add Renderer::GetOrCreateMipGenPipeline(shader): a process-wide,
mutex-guarded cache keyed by shader hash that builds each mip-gen
pipeline once and hands the same object to every GenerateMips call. The
per-texture ComputePass + per-mip Material bindings are unchanged, so
each texture still mips against its own image views. Cleared in
Renderer::Shutdown before device teardown.

Net: the compute mip generator is built twice total (float + uint)
instead of once per texture -> hundreds fewer pipeline builds at load.
(A cross-run on-disk cache for the ~50 real render pipelines is separate:
nvrhi owns pipeline creation, so it needs submodule changes.)

commits.subject: Defer pass descriptor rebake on shader reload to the render thread
commits.message:
Defer pass descriptor rebake on shader reload to the render thread

RenderPass::OnShaderReloaded and ComputePass::OnShaderReloaded ran the
descriptor-set rebake synchronously on whatever thread triggered the
reload (shader hot-reload runs off UpdateDirtyShaders, called directly
from Renderer2D::BeginScene rather than through Renderer::Submit). The
render thread can still have queued GPU work reading the same pass's
binding sets, so mutating them immediately races with that work -
exactly the pattern Pipeline::Invalidate and PipelineCompute::CreatePipeline
already avoid by deferring their real work via Renderer::Submit
(RT_Invalidate / RT_CreatePipeline).

This explains why the crash changed shape after the previous fix: the
Vulkan validation error went away (the binding/ordering bugs were fixed)
but a raw access violation with no validation output took its place -
consistent with a CPU-side data race corrupting DescriptorSetManager's
state rather than a GPU-visible resource mismatch.

Both OnShaderReloaded methods now capture a Ref to themselves and submit
the actual m_DescriptorSetManager.OnShaderReloaded() call through

commits.subject: Re-bake render/compute pass descriptor sets when their shader reloads
commits.message:
Re-bake render/compute pass descriptor sets when their shader reloads

An in-place shader recompile (VulkanShaderCompiler::TryRecompile) releases
the shader's nvrhi binding layouts and rebuilds its reflection, then
Renderer::OnShaderReloaded refreshes pipelines and materials — but never
the RenderPass/ComputePass descriptor managers. Their baked binding sets
kept referencing the released layouts, so the next draw or dispatch
through such a pass was a use-after-free.

This crashed the editor on first frame after the AO fold: DeferredLighting
now references __HZ_AO_METHOD/__HZ_GTAO_COMPUTE_BENT_NORMALS, so when
project settings flip a global shader macro at load, DeferredLighting (and
SSR, recompiled for the GBuffer include change) reload in place and the
deferred pass drew with stale descriptor sets -> 0xC0000005. The landmine
was pre-existing for every pass whose shader recompiles at runtime.

Fix: passes register in the shader-dependency registry like pipelines and
materials, and OnShaderReloaded now calls a new
DescriptorSetManager::OnShaderReloaded that rebuilds declarations, input
maps and binding-set handle storage from the new reflection, re-applies
the previously bound inputs by name (names are stable across permutations,
set/binding indexes are not), and re-bakes against the new layouts.

commits.subject: Fix DeferredLighting startup crash from the AO fold
commits.message:
Fix DeferredLighting startup crash from the AO fold

Two defects from folding the AO multiply into DeferredLighting.glsl:

1. u_GTAOTex was declared at set 1 binding 4, which collides with the
   ShadowData UBO from Buffers.glslh (also set 1 binding 4). Vulkan
   flagged the duplicate descriptor binding and the descriptor manager
   reported 'Required resource is wrong type' because the two
   declarations fought over the same slot. Moved to binding 18, the
   first free slot (4-10 UBOs, 11-17 GBuffer inputs, 22-25 cluster
   buffers).

2. The deferred-lighting pass Validate() ran before the GTAO images
   were created, so the reflected u_GTAOTex input was unbound and
   verification failed fatally. Hoisted the GTAO image creation (and
   the m_GTAOFinalImage denoise-parity selection) above the
   deferred-pass creation and bound u_GTAOTex before Validate().

commits.subject: Reuse per-pass sorted draw order when the draw-list key set is unchanged

the sort inputs (pipeline/shader/material/mesh sort keys), so an

the retained DrawOrder is reused and the sort is skipped. Any membership

commits.subject: Mesh CPU memory: drop dead triangle cache, compact vertices in runtime
commits.message:
Mesh CPU memory: drop dead triangle cache, compact vertices in runtime

Two findings from the memory audit:

   triangle) and was built by both the Assimp importer and the runtime
   mesh deserializer - but GetTriangleCache had zero callers anywhere.

   read vertex positions + indices exclusively. The standalone runtime
   now compacts each MeshSource after GPU upload: positions are kept in

commits.subject: Batch resource uploads into one shared command list
commits.message:
Batch resource uploads into one shared command list

Every mesh vertex/index buffer and texture upload created its own
RenderCommandBuffer and called executeCommandList immediately under the
global graphics-queue mutex - one vkQueueSubmit per resource, serialized
against the render thread mid-frame. Loading a model with dozens of
meshes meant dozens of queue submits in one frame: the classic streaming
hitch. The per-buffer command lists were also retained for the resource's
whole lifetime.

Add Renderer::RecordResourceUpload/FlushResourceUploads: a mutex-guarded
shared nvrhi command list accumulates uploads from any thread and is
submitted once. Ordering is guaranteed structurally: RT_Submit flushes
the pending batch before executing any command list, so uploads always
reach the queue ahead of every possible consumer (frame rendering,
readbacks, env-map bakes). nvrhi stages source data at record time, so
caller-side data lifetimes are unchanged. The GPU-blocking readback path
(CopyToHostBuffer) keeps its dedicated list.

Also downgrade the per-creation TextureCube warning to a trace tag.

commits.subject: Self-heal framebuffers whose baked attachment handles went stale
commits.message:
Self-heal framebuffers whose baked attachment handles went stale

Framebuffers bake their attachment images' nvrhi texture handles into
their FramebufferDesc at RT_Invalidate. Images are recreated in place
(same Ref, new handle) on resize and aliasing changes, and
Framebuffer::Resize early-outs purely on size — so a framebuffer that
wraps a shared image via ExistingImages can be left rendering into the
orphaned old texture with no path that ever repairs it. That is how the
exported runtime lost all lit geometry in fullscreen: the deferred
lighting framebuffer (which wraps SceneColor) went one generation stale
on the fullscreen startup path, so every lit pixel landed in a dead
texture while the sky wrote to the live one.

Add Framebuffer::HasStaleAttachments (baked handles vs current) and a
per-frame sweep in BeginScene that re-invalidates any stale framebuffer,
owners before wrappers so repairs converge in one sweep. Cost when clean
is a few pointer compares per framebuffer; a repair logs a warning naming
the framebuffer so the triggering path can be identified from the field.

commits.subject: Fix permanent mesh disappearance on quality preset change
commits.message:
Fix permanent mesh disappearance on quality preset change

Changing the quality preset resized the screen-space-effect framebuffers
immediately, before the BeginScene resize block resizes the main
framebuffers. Passes whose framebuffers wrap the scene-color image via
ExistingImages (DeferredLighting, composites, fog, sky) baked the old
scene-color texture handle into their FramebufferDesc; when the resize
block then recreated SceneColor, their Framebuffer::Resize early-outed
(size already matched) and left them pointing at the orphaned texture.
Lit geometry rendered into that orphan forever — draws still submitted,
nothing on screen, unrecoverable without a renderer rebuild, and
switching the preset back just repeated the cycle one generation behind.

RefreshScreenSpaceEffectResources now defers to the BeginScene resize
block, which already runs ResizeScreenSpaceEffectResources after the
main framebuffers and with aliasing cleared. This covers all callers
(SetQualityPreset, ApplyProjectSettings, the editor panel) including
resolution-unchanged preset switches.

Also harden ClearRenderTargetAliasing: always RT_Invalidate the cleared
aliased images. ApplyRenderTargetAliasing excludes invalid images from
the rebuilt alias graph, so a storage-stripped image was never re-aliased
and never recovered, and fed a null handle into descriptor baking.

commits.subject: SceneRenderer: version-gate the per-frame texture/material table copies
commits.message:
SceneRenderer: version-gate the per-frame texture/material table copies

FlushDrawList copied the entire TextureScene handle table and

nothing changed. Give both scenes a monotonic version counter (bumped
in MarkTextureDirty/MarkMaterialDirty and Clear, which every table
mutation funnels through) and skip the copy when the same scene
instance is submitted with an unchanged version. On unchanged frames
the texture scratch is truncated back to its persistent prefix before
this frame's transient handles are appended; the material scratch
carries over untouched. The texture resolve loop is deliberately left
running every frame — it is what picks up async texture-load
completions, which do not mark the scene dirty.

commits.message:
Scene: reuse SyncRenderScene sync-item scratch across frames

SyncRenderScene rebuilt a std::vector<StaticMeshSyncItem> from scratch
every frame (one proxy with several Ref<>s per static mesh). Keep it in
a thread_local scratch so capacity is retained; clear it after the
upsert loop so no Ref<>s survive past the call.

commits.subject: SceneRenderer: single-copy captures in the GPUScene upload submit
commits.message:
SceneRenderer: single-copy captures in the GPUScene upload submit

The upload lambda copied eight per-frame vectors into locals and then
copied each local again into the closure — including the full GPUScene
instance array. Use lambda init-captures: scratch-backed vectors are
copied once (their capacity must stay with the member for next frame),
and the frame-local instance/transient GPUScene vectors are moved. The
emptiness guard evaluates before closure construction and nothing reads
the moved-from locals afterwards.

commits.subject: SceneRenderer: capture MeshDrawParams instead of TransformMapData per draw
commits.message:
SceneRenderer: capture MeshDrawParams instead of TransformMapData per draw

Every mesh-pass draw captured TransformMapData by value into its
Renderer::Submit lambda, heap-copying the ObjectIndices vector once per
draw per pass on the main thread. RT_DrawStaticMesh only reads four
scalars from it, so snapshot those into a POD MeshDrawParams at submit
time and capture that instead. Snapshot semantics are unchanged: the
old closure copied the whole struct at submit time; the new one copies
the four fields actually read.

commits.subject: SceneRenderer: reuse push-constant scratch in RT_DrawStaticMesh

RT_DrawStaticMesh heap-allocated (and freed) a std::vector<uint8_t> for
every draw command in every mesh pass on the render thread. Replace it
with a persistent render-thread-only scratch member; assign() preserves
the zero-fill semantics of the old value-initialized vector while
retaining capacity across draws.

commits.subject: Replicate Hazel's shadow rendering (no cache) + split SceneRenderer
commits.message:
Replicate Hazel's shadow rendering (no cache) + split SceneRenderer

Shadows: drop the shadow-map caching and render the directional cascades and
the spot-shadow atlas every frame (clearing when idle), matching Hazel. The
cache toggled the shadow pass in/out of the render graph each frame, which
desynced the depth-attachment barriers/layout (garbage depth reads) and made
the transient alias plan stale -> mesh and shadows flickered on/off. Always
running the passes keeps the graph topology and barriers stable. The shadow
passes are now unconditionally in the graph, and transient render-target
aliasing is re-enabled (valid again with stable topology).

Split: begin breaking up the 8k-line SceneRenderer.cpp. Shared helpers moved to
SceneRendererInternal.h; profiling, post-process, and stats methods moved to
SceneRenderer_{Profiling,PostProcess,Stats}.cpp. Pure relocation, no behavior
change (premake regen picks up the new files). Shadows/geometry/atmosphere
groups deferred (active clustered + shadow work).

Renderer core: wire clustered froxel passes and drop forward/tiled wiring (Phases 1-6)

Consolidated cross-cutting renderer changes (SceneRenderer.cpp has ~40
interleaved hunks across phases that cannot be cleanly bisected):

- Phases 1-2: create + dispatch the ClusterBuild and ClusterLightCulling
  compute passes (counter reset, barriers, render-graph nodes), allocate the
  cluster AABB / grid / index-list / counter storage buffers.
- Phase 3: ClusterZParams plumbing; bind the cluster lists via PassInputLights.
- Phases 4-5: remove the forward geometry/light-culling passes, the tiled
  visible-light buffers, Renderer::LightCulling(), and load the cluster
  compute shaders instead of LightCulling.glsl; deferred path is unconditional.
- Phase 6: bind the spot shadow atlas (PassInputShadowMaps) to the fog pass so
  in-fog spot shafts are shadowed.

commits.subject: Phase 6: clustered local-light in-scattering in the volumetric fog march
commits.message:
Phase 6: clustered local-light in-scattering in the volumetric fog march

Feed the froxel light grid into the height-fog ray-march so point/spot
lights produce RDR2-style shafts and glow in fog.

- FogClusterLights.glslh (new): self-contained per-sample froxel resolve +
  point/spot in-scatter with Cornette-Shanks phase. Spot lights are
  shadow-sampled (single hard tap vs. the spot atlas); points are unshadowed
  (no point shadow maps). Density-modulated by the march step opacity.
- Atmosphere.glslh: LUX_FOG_CLUSTER_LIGHTS-gated hook in the volumetric
  march so non-fog includers (sky) don't pull the light lists.
- AtmosphericFog.glsl: define the macro, declare the spot atlas, include the
  scattering body.

commits.message:

Add the 16x9x32 froxel grid foundation for clustered deferred shading:

commits.subject: Fix StarEngine's black flicker when resize the viewport
commits.message:
Fix StarEngine's black flicker when resize the viewport

This solution will render the 'old' sized framebuffer onto the 'new' sized ImGuiPanel and store the 'new' size in m_ViewportSize. The next frame will first resize the framebuffer as m_ViewportSize differs from m_Framebuffer.Width/Height before updating and rendering. This results in never rendering an empty (black) framebuffer.

Foliage materials: coverage-preserving mips, diffuse transmission, two-sided transparents, prepass fixes

commits.subject: Renderer: report a Cutout albedo that cannot get coverage-preserving mips
commits.message:
Renderer: report a Cutout albedo that cannot get coverage-preserving mips

Review fixes for the foliage materials branch. A Cutout material whose
albedo is not 8-bit RGBA (float or block-compressed) silently kept its
box-filtered chain; it now warns once per texture, naming why its foliage
may thin out with distance. The texture-slot hasher uses named casts, and
RT_SwitchRenderPassPipeline's comment states that it returns false
silently outside a pass, as RT_DrawIndexed does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0175UJhckawytKSTiQeh3u9C

commits.subject: Renderer: depth-only prepass for opaque draws, alpha test for Cutout only
commits.message:
Renderer: depth-only prepass for opaque draws, alpha test for Cutout only

Every prepass fragment ran the alpha-test shader: a material-row fetch
and a discard that costs early depth, even for opaque geometry. PreDepth
is now depth-only (no material reads, no discard); Cutout draws
(MeshKey::AlphaMasked on the main key) switch inside the pass to
PreDepth_Masked, held with its sets by the never-begun
m_PreDepthMaskedPass, plus a no-cull variant for two-sided Cutout.

Measured with golden captures (Release, 1280x720, medians of 3, images
pixel-identical): PreDepthPass 0.936 -> 0.916 ms on Benchmark, 0.061 ->
0.038 ms on FMODDemo; total GPU time unchanged within noise. The
mesh-shader prepass keeps its single alpha-testing shader.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0175UJhckawytKSTiQeh3u9C

commits.subject: Renderer: the mesh-shader prepass alpha-tests and draws two-sided
commits.message:
Renderer: the mesh-shader prepass alpha-tests and draws two-sided

With Mesh Shaders on, the meshlet prepass replaced the classic one but
had an empty fragment stage and one culling pipeline: Cutout geometry
wrote the depth of its whole quad and two-sided back faces were culled,
so the G-buffer's depth-equal test dropped both.

The mesh stage now outputs the UVs (the G-buffer's (u, 1 - v)), object
index and view position, and the fragment stage runs PreDepth's alpha
test with the same mip bias. m_PreDepthMeshletPass binds the same
material inputs, and two-sided draws switch to a no-cull meshlet
pipeline inside the pass (the task stage never cone-culls).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0175UJhckawytKSTiQeh3u9C

commits.subject: Renderer: two-sided transparents draw back faces, then front faces
commits.message:
Renderer: two-sided transparents draw back faces, then front faces

A BLEND + doubleSided material (glass panes, hair cards) lost its back
faces to the transparent pass's culling. Transparent draw keys now carry
TwoSided, and such a draw records twice inside the open pass: first
through a new back-faces pipeline (PipelineSpecification::
FrontFaceCulling), then through the default one, so its far side blends
in before its near side, as HDRP's "Back Then Front" does. Sort keys are
unchanged, so blend order between materials does not move.
HazelPBR_Transparent flips the normal on back faces, and the material
editor's Two Sided checkbox now applies to transparent materials too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0175UJhckawytKSTiQeh3u9C

commits.subject: Renderer: light passes through thin translucent surfaces
commits.message:
Renderer: light passes through thin translucent surfaces

Materials with diffuse transmission now transmit light, per glTF's
mix(diffuse_brdf, diffuse_btdf, t): a back-lit leaf glows instead of
going dark.

GBuffer_Static writes the per-pixel factor (material factor x map) into
the G-buffer normal's alpha, unused until now; DeferredLighting reads the
colour from the material row through MaterialID. It scales the albedo by
1 - t after F0 (so only diffuse reflection gives up energy) and adds a
Lambert lobe about -N for every light, plus IBL irradiance from -N. The
directional back lobe gets its own shadow lookup, offset toward the
light's side, or the surface would shadow itself; point and spot shadows
test the surface point and are shared by both lobes. Pixels with no
transmission take none of the new branches, and the lobe stays zero in
every other shader.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0175UJhckawytKSTiQeh3u9C

commits.subject: Materials: diffuse transmission inputs (glTF KHR_materials_diffuse_transmission)
commits.message:
Materials: diffuse transmission inputs (glTF KHR_materials_diffuse_transmission)

Thin surfaces such as leaves pass some of their diffuse light through to
the far side. Materials gain the glTF diffuse-transmission inputs: a
factor (0 = off, the default, so existing materials are unchanged), a
transmission colour, and a factor map read from alpha.

They serialize only when not default, register the map as a dependency,
and appear in the material editor's new Translucency section for opaque
and Cutout materials. The GPU material row grows to 11 vec4 (Transmission
and TransmissionTextureIndices, mirrored in MaterialScene.glslh); the
lighting that reads them comes next.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0175UJhckawytKSTiQeh3u9C

commits.subject: Renderer: Cutout albedo keeps its alpha coverage at every mip
commits.message:
Renderer: Cutout albedo keeps its alpha coverage at every mip

Box-filtered mips average alpha down around every hole, so an
alpha-tested texture lost coverage with each level and foliage thinned
out as the camera backed away.

A Cutout material's albedo now binds a copy whose mip chain preserves
mip 0's coverage at the material's cutoff (Castano's method): the
box-filtered chain is histogrammed per mip (256 bins, exact for 8-bit
alpha), and each level's alpha is rescaled by the cutoff whose coverage
is closest to mip 0's (AlphaCoverageHistogram/AlphaCoverageScale, one
storage buffer at set 1 binding 26). Texture slots key on the cutoff
(GPUTextureSlot::AlphaCoverageCutoff, 1/255 steps), so every pass that
alpha-tests samples the same chain.

MaterialAsset builds the variant when the albedo, alpha mode or cutoff
changes and drops the copy it stopped binding once unused; the loader
applies the surface before the maps so a Cutout .lmat builds one chain.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0175UJhckawytKSTiQeh3u9C

commits.subject: Renderer: alpha masks sample the UVs the G-buffer draws; Two Sided toggle
commits.message:
Renderer: alpha masks sample the UVs the G-buffer draws; Two Sided toggle

PreDepth and the masked shadow shaders alpha-tested at (u, v) while
GBuffer_Static, which decides what is seen, samples at (u, 1 - v). The
prepass therefore discarded a vertically mirrored mask: only pixels both
masks kept survived the G-buffer's EQUAL depth test, the rest were holes,
and cut-out shadows were mirrored relative to their leaves. All three now
use the G-buffer's UVs.

The material editor's Rendering section gets a Two Sided checkbox for
opaque materials; it was only reachable through .lmat files or import.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0175UJhckawytKSTiQeh3u9C
